relationship_to_protagonist: The film's subject; Bachchan contributes only the offscreen narration that introduces and frames him
relationship_to_romance: No romance in the film; his fascination with Gauri is an awakening rather than a courtship
character_gist: Rigid, widowed railway bureaucrat feared as a martinet, who takes an amateurish hunting holiday in Gujarat, is loosened by a village girl, and returns to reprieve the offending railwayman he would once have punished.
performance_recognition: National Film Award for Best Actor

relationship_to_protagonist: Shares no scenes with Bachchan, whose contribution is narration only; she is the agent of Bhuvan Shome's change
relationship_to_romance: Not a romantic interest; the film keeps her relation to Shome affectionate and unconsummated
character_gist: Talkative married village girl, better schooled than Shome expects, who feeds him, makes him change out of his city clothes so the birds will not know him, and stage-manages his one successful shot.

relationship_to_protagonist: One of the seven comrades alongside Bachchan's Anwar Ali
relationship_to_romance: No romantic plot; the group's bond is nationalist, not romantic
character_gist: Bengali member of the seven-man group that infiltrates Portuguese Goa to hoist Indian flags, one of the older and more deliberate heads in the party.

relationship_to_protagonist: Fellow volunteer in the seven-man group that includes Bachchan's Anwar Ali
relationship_to_romance: No romantic plot
character_gist: One of the seven men drawn from different religions and regions of India who join to raise nationalist sentiment in Portuguese-occupied Goa.

relationship_to_protagonist: The Goan seventh comrade the six men join; the only woman in the group
relationship_to_romance: No romance is developed between her and Bachchan's Anwar Ali despite their being the film's only man-woman pairing
character_gist: Native of Portuguese-occupied Goa and the seventh of the Saat Hindustani, whose local knowledge makes the flag-hoisting campaign possible. Credited as Shahnaz.

relationship_to_protagonist: Fellow comrade; note that this actor's own name is identical to the name of Bachchan's character in the film
relationship_to_romance: No romantic plot
character_gist: One of the seven volunteers. The credit is a standing source of confusion: the actor Anwar Ali, Mehmood's brother, plays Ram Bhagat Sharma, while Bachchan plays the character named Anwar Ali.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection; Bachchan's uncredited walk-on is a man attending a funeral
relationship_to_romance: Carries the film's central affair as the married star who takes up with Lucia
character_gist: Famous and married Bombay film star who begins an affair with a visiting British author, the relationship that drives the film to its tragedy.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's uncredited mourner
relationship_to_romance: The film's romantic centre, loved by Hari and involved with the married Vikram
character_gist: British author researching the Hindi film industry who falls into an affair with the star Vikram while his friend Hari is in love with her.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's walk-on
relationship_to_romance: Vikram's friend, in love with Lucia, which complicates the central affair
character_gist: Writer and friend of Vikram whose unreturned love for Lucia sets him against the affair he is too close to ignore.

relationship_to_protagonist: The dying patient who becomes Bhaskar's friend and the subject of the book Bhaskar writes
relationship_to_romance: Discovers Bhaskar's feelings for Renu, pushes him to declare them and persuades her mother to bless the marriage
character_gist: Patient with lymphosarcoma of the intestine who, knowing he has six months, refuses a hospital bed and spends his time making strangers into friends. He leaves behind a taped voice that plays as he dies.
performance_recognition: Filmfare Award for Best Actor; BFJA Award for Best Actor (Hindi)

relationship_to_protagonist: Former patient of Bhaskar's, treated for pneumonia, who becomes his wife
relationship_to_romance: The film's only romance and a secondary thread, brought about by Anand rather than by Bhaskar himself
character_gist: Young woman Bhaskar treated for pneumonia and silently loves; Anand engineers the declaration and the consent of her mother.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bhaskar's colleague and friend, who introduces him to Anand
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Doctor who treats the imaginary ailments of the rich to fund care for the poor, the pragmatic counterweight to Bhaskar's austerity, and the man who brings Anand into his life.

relationship_to_protagonist: Friend acquired through Anand rather than through Bhaskar
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Theatre actor whom Anand befriends on sight and binds to himself emotionally, one of the demonstrations of Anand's gift for collecting people.

relationship_to_protagonist: Ram's intended bride, chosen by his parents
relationship_to_romance: The film's romance; its obstacle is not her feeling for Ram but her history with his friend
character_gist: Young woman betrothed to Ram, whose past connection with Ravi and the reputation attached to her are the secret the film withholds until late.

relationship_to_protagonist: Man Ram talks out of suicide, houses and finds work for; later the source of the film's crisis
relationship_to_romance: Withholds his approval of Kusum for reasons that turn out to be his own past with her
character_gist: Suicidal young man rescued and sheltered by Ram, who rises to manager in the same office and marries a colleague, then evades every question about why he disapproves of Ram's bride.

relationship_to_protagonist: Colleague who marries Ram's friend Ravi
relationship_to_romance: Part of the settled couple against which Ram's stalled engagement is measured
character_gist: Office co-worker whom Ravi falls in love with and marries, and who shares in judging the photograph of Ram's prospective bride.

relationship_to_protagonist: Opponent of Ram
relationship_to_romance: Pressure from outside the couple
character_gist: Local strongman heading a party of hangers-on, the film's antagonistic force against the peon Ram.

relationship_to_protagonist: The man Asha loves, whom Bachchan's Kumar frames for murder
relationship_to_romance: Kumar's rival and the reason his pursuit of Asha can never succeed
character_gist: Wealthy Ooty tea-plantation owner who wins Asha's love, is framed by Kumar for her uncle's murder and sentenced to death, then exonerated by Kumar's written confession.

relationship_to_protagonist: The woman Bachchan's Kumar loves and kills for
relationship_to_romance: The object of the film's obsessive pursuit; she never returns Kumar's feeling
character_gist: Dance-competition winner who falls in love with Rajeshwar in Ooty, believes in his innocence against the evidence, and offers to stay with Kumar forever if he will save the man she loves.

relationship_to_protagonist: Asha's uncle and guardian, who refuses Bachchan's Kumar her hand and is murdered by him
relationship_to_romance: The external obstacle whose refusal triggers the murder plot
character_gist: Asha's uncle, who turns down Kumar's demand for her hand in marriage and is killed by him in an elaborately alibied murder.

relationship_to_protagonist: Woman of the rival clan who shelters Bachchan's Chhotu and marries him to stop the killing
relationship_to_romance: The film's romantic centre is Reshma and Shera; her marriage to Chhotu is a device to end the feud, not a romance
character_gist: Woman in love with Shera across a clan feud, whose father and newly married brother are shot by Shera's mute brother; she finally marries that brother so the bloodshed can stop, and dies on Shera's body in the desert.
performance_recognition: National Film Award for Best Actress

relationship_to_protagonist: Elder brother of Bachchan's Chhotu, who swears to kill him for the murders
relationship_to_romance: Reshma's lover, and the pair whose love the feud destroys
character_gist: Sagat Singh's son, in love with Reshma across the feud. He kills his own father over the murders, hunts his brother, and shoots himself when he sees the sindoor that makes Chhotu untouchable to him.

relationship_to_protagonist: Father of Bachchan's Chhotu, whose orders Chhotu carries out
relationship_to_romance: The paternal authority whose orders destroy Reshma and Shera's chance
character_gist: Clan patriarch who orders the killing of Reshma's father and brother when the lovers are discovered, and is killed by his own son Shera in the belief that he pulled the trigger.

relationship_to_protagonist: Widow of the man Bachchan's Chhotu shoots
relationship_to_romance: Her widowing is the grief that turns Shera against his own father
character_gist: Bride widowed on the day of her marriage when Chhotu shoots her husband Gopal; her grief is what drives Shera to kill his father.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan, who appears briefly as himself in the film-industry passages
relationship_to_romance: Her fixation on a film star is the obstacle to the marriage the film ends with
character_gist: Schoolgirl who cannot separate Dharmendra the star from the man, refuses Navin's proposal on that account, and is cured by being shown the grime behind the glamour; she agrees to marry Navin at the end.
performance_recognition: Filmfare Award for Best Actress nomination

relationship_to_protagonist: Fellow star appearing as himself, as Bachchan does, in a film about film stardom
relationship_to_romance: The illusion standing between Guddi and Navin, which he himself dismantles
character_gist: Plays himself as the object of Guddi's crush and then as the agent of her cure, agreeing to show her that the star is as human and insecure as anyone.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's appearance as himself
relationship_to_romance: The suitor whose proposal frames the whole plot
character_gist: Brother of Guddi's sister-in-law, who proposes to her, is refused because of Dharmendra, and takes the matter to his uncle; Guddi accepts him once the illusion is broken.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's cameo as himself
relationship_to_romance: Designs the cure that clears the way for Guddi's marriage
character_gist: Navin's uncle, who decides the only remedy for Guddi's infatuation is to show her the difference between illusion and reality, and arranges it through a mutual friend of Dharmendra's.

relationship_to_protagonist: The film's protagonist; Bachchan's Dalaljit is a guest appearance in this Bengali production
relationship_to_romance: Carries the film's romance with Laxmi
character_gist: Young man in love with Laxmi who is framed for theft and imprisoned while she is sold into a brothel by her uncle.

relationship_to_protagonist: No recorded connection to Bachchan's guest appearance
relationship_to_romance: The film's romantic lead opposite Binu
character_gist: Young woman who wants to marry Binu and is sold by her uncle to Janardan, who sends her to a brothel.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan, whose appearance is a guest walk-on
relationship_to_romance: The film's romantic and marital centre
character_gist: Village bride matched to Ram by a matchmaker, who moves into his one-room chawl apartment shared with nine relatives and nearly leaves for want of any privacy with her husband.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's guest appearance
relationship_to_romance: The husband in the film's central marriage
character_gist: Bombay chawl dweller matched to Malti, whose extended family fills the single room; the couple's failed attempts at privacy are the film's comedy and its crisis.

relationship_to_protagonist: Appears as himself, as Bachchan does in his guest walk-on
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Star appearing as himself, one of two guest turns in the film alongside Bachchan's.

relationship_to_protagonist: Mohan's first wife, married in a temple and separated from him by his mother
relationship_to_romance: One of the two women in the film's double marriage; her reappearance as Mohan's superior officer reopens it
character_gist: Woman married to Mohan in a temple and cast off by his family while pregnant; her father makes her a collector, and she is posted over the office where Mohan clerks. She dies saving his second wife and donates her eyes to her.

relationship_to_protagonist: Mohan's second wife, married in the belief that Asha was dead
relationship_to_romance: The second of the film's two marriages, destabilised by the rumour of an affair
character_gist: South Indian wife who bears Mohan two children, is broken by the rumour of his affair with the new collector, learns that the collector is his first wife, and is saved by her at the cost of Asha's life.

relationship_to_protagonist: Asha's father, who takes her away from Mohan's family
relationship_to_romance: Acts on the judgment that no man will marry his daughter twice, and makes her a career instead
character_gist: Asha's father, who responds to her abandonment by putting her through to the collectorate rather than seeking another marriage for her.

relationship_to_protagonist: Office colleague of Mohan's whose gossip wrecks his household
relationship_to_romance: Manufactures the rumour of an affair that turns Seema against Mohan
character_gist: Office wag who with his friends spreads the rumour that the collector and the clerk are having an affair, the lie that drives the second half of the film.

relationship_to_protagonist: The woman Bachchan's Ravi Kumar protects and travels with
relationship_to_romance: The film's romance, which grows over the course of the bus journey
character_gist: Aspiring actress who runs away from an arranged marriage with money for two men promising her a film career, witnesses one murder the other, and flees to Goa by bus with a killer aboard.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bus conductor on the journey Bachchan's Ravi shares; offscreen, Mehmood produced the film and gave Bachchan this first lead
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance, though the bus he runs is where it happens
character_gist: Bus conductor whose running comic business with the passengers and the driver carries much of the film. Mehmood cast Bachchan in the lead a year before Zanjeer, when established producers would not.

relationship_to_protagonist: Pursues Mala, whom Bachchan's Ravi is protecting
relationship_to_romance: The threat that gives Ravi his role as Mala's protector
character_gist: One of the two men who put Mala's photographs in a magazine, kills his partner Verma out of greed, and sends an armed henchman onto the bus to silence the witness.

relationship_to_protagonist: Driver of the bus Bachchan's Ravi rides
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Bus driver who with the conductor Khanna keeps the mixed busload of passengers in some kind of order on the road to Goa.

relationship_to_protagonist: Father of the woman Bachchan's Ravi protects
relationship_to_romance: His arranged match for Mala is what she runs from
character_gist: Mala's father, who finds her photographs in a magazine and arranges her marriage to a man she has never met, precipitating her flight.

relationship_to_protagonist: The film's protagonist; Bachchan's Robert Taylor is a special appearance
relationship_to_romance: Carries what romantic interest the film has, opposite Jugnu
character_gist: Prince of Sabzbag raised by Hercules to be a clownish figure so the regent can rule through him, who turns out to be one of the masked men fighting the Captain's soldiers.

relationship_to_protagonist: No recorded scenes with Bachchan's special appearance
relationship_to_romance: The film's female lead opposite the prince
character_gist: Gypsy girl who separates the prince from his retinue to demand justice, finds him incapable of giving it, and resolves to fight for it herself.

relationship_to_protagonist: The film's villain, opposed by the masked men rather than by Bachchan's role
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Despotic regent who had the prince raised in everything but kingship so that he could rule in his name, and who taxes the poor on the pretext of the prince's birthday.

relationship_to_protagonist: Ally of the film's antagonist
relationship_to_romance: The Captain's beloved, a counterpoint to the prince's story
character_gist: The Captain's beloved and partner in the plan to rule through a puppet king.

relationship_to_protagonist: The courtesan singer Bachchan's Akash loves
relationship_to_romance: The film's central romance and its social scandal
character_gist: Singer and dancer in a courtesan's house who admires Akash's poetry without knowing him, falls in love with him, and is then accused of Amina Bai's murder.

relationship_to_protagonist: Head of the house Bachchan's Akash takes Shabnam from
relationship_to_romance: External opposition to the romance; her murder becomes its crisis
character_gist: Mistress of the courtesan's house who refuses to let Shabnam go to Akash, and whose murder puts Shabnam in the dock.

relationship_to_protagonist: Father of Bachchan's Akash, opposed to the match
relationship_to_romance: The respectable half of the opposition to the romance, matching Amina Bai's refusal
character_gist: Akash's father, unwilling to accept a courtesan's singer as his son's choice.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Akash's lawyer friend
relationship_to_romance: The romance's only practical hope once Shabnam is charged
character_gist: Lawyer friend of Akash's on whom Shabnam's defence against the murder charge depends.

relationship_to_protagonist: The film's protagonist; Bachchan narrates the credits and introduces the characters
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance; he repairs the household rather than courting anyone
character_gist: Young man who takes the cook's job in a house no servant will stay in, becomes indispensable to every member of the quarrelling Sharma family, and defuses their feuds. Also Professor Prabhakar.
performance_recognition: BFJA Award for Best Actor (Hindi)

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: The film's one romantic thread, secondary to the household comedy
character_gist: Orphaned niece at everyone's beck and call in Shanti Niwas, who keeps a sunny disposition and is the only person the grumbling patriarch thinks about.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Aging, disgruntled patriarch of the ironically named Shanti Niwas, complaining about his sons, his daughters-in-law and the morning tea, and alone in caring for the orphaned Krishna.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Meeta's dance teacher, one of the household's comic fixtures.
performance_recognition: Filmfare Best Comedian Award

relationship_to_protagonist: The woman Bachchan's Birju shelters and comes to love
relationship_to_romance: The film's central romance
character_gist: Village girl orphaned young, sold to an ashram in Bombay and raised there, who escapes onto the streets and is hidden by Birju from those pursuing her.

relationship_to_protagonist: Part of the threat Bachchan's Birju shields Bansi from
relationship_to_romance: External pressure on the couple
character_gist: Figure among those pursuing Bansi after her escape, one of the continued threats the couple faces.

relationship_to_protagonist: Secondary figure in the world Bachchan's Birju moves through
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Supporting figure in the Bombay milieu of the film; the surviving article gives the role no detail.

relationship_to_protagonist: The woman Bachchan's Jai Shankar loves
relationship_to_romance: The film's romance and its humiliation: she is involved with Jai's own boss
character_gist: Woman Jai Shankar loves, whose relationship with his superior precipitates his personal crisis and exposes the bargain he has made by lending out his flat.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Jai's closest friend, whom he tries to place in an advertising job and finally saves in court
relationship_to_romance: His marriage to Tanu is the film's second relationship, ruined by poverty rather than by rivalry
character_gist: Idealistic unemployed writer who refuses to write commercial trash, drives his household into poverty, looks away while his wife dances in clubs to keep them afloat, and is framed for a murder in Jai's flat.

relationship_to_protagonist: Wife of Bachchan's Jai's best friend; a client brings her to Jai's own flat
relationship_to_romance: Her marriage is the film's study of a relationship degraded by need
character_gist: Wife of the principled writer Arun, who takes work as an evening club dancer out of desperation, is brought by a client to Jai's flat, witnesses a criminal quarrel there, and is framed with her husband.

relationship_to_protagonist: Part of the criminal faction whose cover-up Bachchan's Jai finally breaks
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Member of the blackmailing criminal group whose dealings end in a murder in Jai's apartment and the framing of Arun and Tanu.

relationship_to_protagonist: The film's protagonist; Bachchan contributes narration only
relationship_to_romance: Her relationship with the doctor is the film's romantic thread, secondary to the addiction story
character_gist: Wealthy young woman who drifts into drug addiction out of boredom, complicating her own life and her family's.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: The male half of the film's central relationship
character_gist: Doctor at the centre of the film's account of Reena's addiction and its consequences for her family.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Senior figure in the film's social world; one of the last screen appearances of Prithviraj Kapoor, who died in 1972.

relationship_to_protagonist: Stage dancer who loves Bachchan's thief in his stolen identity as the poet Deepak
relationship_to_romance: The film's central romance, conducted entirely under a false name
character_gist: Stage artist and dancer at Roop Kala Theatre whose love changes Shyamu, who is wearing the dead poet Deepak's identity; she learns the truth from Inspector Kumar.

relationship_to_protagonist: The policeman who suspects Bachchan's Shyamu is alive and impersonating the poet
relationship_to_romance: Breaks the romance open by telling Mala who her poet really is
character_gist: Police inspector unconvinced by the reported death of the thief Shyamu, who tracks the impersonation and discloses it to Mala.

relationship_to_protagonist: The real Deepak's love interest, courted by Bachchan's impostor only to recover incriminating letters
relationship_to_romance: A feigned courtship rather than a romance, which is why she has no pairing record
character_gist: Women's rights activist and daughter of the millionaire Shyamu once robbed, who holds the letters the poet wrote her; the impostor woos her only to retrieve them before a handwriting test.

relationship_to_protagonist: The thief who trained Bachchan's Shyamu; his death starts the film
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Criminal mentor whose death prompts Shyamu's decision to go straight and sets the identity theft in motion.

relationship_to_protagonist: Pathan usurer beaten by Bachchan's Vijay who becomes his staunchest ally
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance; his bond with Vijay is the film's central friendship
character_gist: Pathan gambling-den keeper whom Vijay shuts down and defeats in a fist fight, and who transfers his loyalty to the policeman on the spot. His qawwali 'Yari Hai Imaan Mera' became the film's emblem of male friendship.
performance_recognition: Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actor nomination

relationship_to_protagonist: Knife-sharpener and street vendor who becomes Bachchan's Vijay's companion
relationship_to_romance: The romance is secondary to the revenge plot; she is the one softening presence in it
character_gist: Street knife-sharpener with a police record who attaches herself to the angry inspector, gives up her trade at his word, and stays with him after his dismissal.

relationship_to_protagonist: The smuggler who murdered Bachchan's Vijay's parents and the target of his revenge
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Respectable-seeming smuggling boss behind the killing of Vijay's parents, whose white suit and suave menace set the template for the 1970s screen villain.

relationship_to_protagonist: Older ally of Bachchan's Vijay
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Sympathetic older figure who stands by Vijay through his suspension and his pursuit of Teja.

relationship_to_protagonist: Attached to the antagonist's circle rather than to Bachchan's Vijay
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Cabaret performer in Teja's orbit, a fixture of the film's underworld nightlife.

relationship_to_protagonist: The film's protagonist; Bachchan appears in a guest turn as himself
relationship_to_romance: No romance for him; the plot is a heist comedy
character_gist: Career criminal from a long line of them, plotting a kidnapping and pressing his reluctant nephew into it, with an old enemy Ghaffoor working against him throughout.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's guest appearance
relationship_to_romance: Outside any romance
character_gist: Nephew jailed seven times over his uncle's disastrous schemes, who wants to sell bananas honestly and is blackmailed back into crime by his mother's feigned heart disease.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's guest appearance
relationship_to_romance: Outside any romance
character_gist: Club dancer recruited into Mama Rampuri's gang for the kidnapping of a smuggler's son.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Ratan's visiting friend, who turns out to be the CBI officer investigating him
relationship_to_romance: Outside the film's concerns; there is no meaningful romance
character_gist: Friend arriving from Delhi whose profession makes him a police suspect, then is revealed as the CBI officer sent to find evidence for the Olympic Bank robbery Ratan helped commit.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Ratan's sister, not a romantic interest
relationship_to_romance: No romance in the film; the top-billed actress plays the protagonist's sister, which is why there is no pairing record
character_gist: Sister who finds their father's body, is kept ignorant of the suicide note, and is the one witness able to identify a robber, which Ratan makes her conceal.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Ratan's best friend and the film's real criminal
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Ratan's closest friend, the prime suspect in the robbery, who shoots the witness Shobha and is finally revealed as the murderer of Ratan's father.

relationship_to_protagonist: Robber identified by Bachchan's Ratan's sister and pressed by him for evidence
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Woman seen at the robbery, cornered by Ratan and Sagar, and shot by Madan before she can name him; she lives long enough to reveal that the father was murdered.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Ratan's father, whose apparent suicide starts the plot
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Chairman of the Olympic Bank found dead before a final audit, leaving a note confessing an embezzlement of twenty lakhs that was in fact Madan's.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Subir's wife, whose success destroys him
relationship_to_romance: The film's whole subject: a marriage broken by the husband's envy of his wife's talent
character_gist: Musically gifted village girl who marries the established singer Subir, outgrows him professionally, is driven from the marriage by his jealousy, miscarries, and returns to sing with him in the reconciliation.
performance_recognition: Filmfare Award for Best Actress

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Subir's friend and associate in the music world
relationship_to_romance: Observes the marriage from close range as it fails
character_gist: Friend within Subir's professional circle, present through the rise of Uma's career and the collapse of the marriage.
performance_recognition: Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actor nomination

relationship_to_protagonist: Figure from Bachchan's Subir's professional world before his marriage
relationship_to_romance: Adjacent to the marriage; the article's plot summary does not detail her part in it
character_gist: Singer connected to Subir's career before Uma; the surviving plot summary gives the role no detail beyond the performance itself.
performance_recognition: Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actress nomination

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Subir's aunt, whose reproach finally breaks his pride
relationship_to_romance: The agent of the reconciliation that ends the film
character_gist: Aunt whose heavy criticism makes Subir see the folly of his vanity and go back to Uma.

relationship_to_protagonist: Widow and business associate whom Bachchan's Moti marries for her labour and then divorces
relationship_to_romance: One of the film's two marriages, and the one it treats as the moral centre
character_gist: Widow whose skill at making gur is the real source of Moti's trade. He marries her to avoid paying her, divorces her on a slander once he has saved the bride price, and she curses him and marries a fish trader who treats her with courtesy.

relationship_to_protagonist: The young woman Bachchan's Moti wants and buys with the bride price
relationship_to_romance: The second marriage, entered for desire and undone by economics
character_gist: Young woman Moti falls for and finally marries after raising the mehar. She cannot make gur, his trade collapses, he beats her for a burnt batch, and she leaves for her father's house.

relationship_to_protagonist: The man who marries the wife Bachchan's Moti discarded
relationship_to_romance: The honest counter-example to Moti's calculating marriages
character_gist: Fish trader who asks Majubee to marry him, tells her plainly that he has small children and wants her to look after them, and always treats her with courtesy.

relationship_to_protagonist: Phoolbanu's father, whose bride price sets Bachchan's Moti's scheme in motion
relationship_to_romance: The economic obstacle that produces the first, mercenary marriage
character_gist: Phoolbanu's father, who demands a mehar Moti cannot pay, and marries his daughter to him once it is raised.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Vicky's closest friend, sent into the factory on his behalf and finally killed by his father
relationship_to_romance: Carries the film's romantic thread with Shyama; Bachchan's own romance is only implied
character_gist: Friend who infiltrates the mill as a worker to avenge an insult to Vicky, becomes the union leader, is converted by the workers' plight, and is shot by Vicky's father when the friendship turns to confrontation.
performance_recognition: BFJA Award for Best Actor (Hindi)

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Vicky's father and the mill owner whose interests set the friends against each other
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Mill owner whose class position defines his son's loyalties and who kills Somu himself, leaving Vicky to take the blame and go to jail.

relationship_to_protagonist: The union leader whose public insult to Bachchan's Vicky starts the entire plot
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Trade union leader at the Maharaj mill whose humiliation of Vicky provokes the revenge scheme, and whom Somu displaces as leader before changing sides.

relationship_to_protagonist: Belongs to Somu's side of the story rather than to Bachchan's Vicky
relationship_to_romance: The film's romantic interest, attached to Somu in the workers' world
character_gist: Young woman of the mill workers' quarter, sister of Dhondu, and the romantic interest in Somu's life among the workers.

relationship_to_protagonist: Figure in Bachchan's Vicky's own class world
relationship_to_romance: The implied romantic connection on Vicky's side, never developed enough to constitute a pairing
character_gist: Woman of Vicky's own social world, present in the industrialist household against which the workers' story is set.

relationship_to_protagonist: Belongs to the workers' world Bachchan's Vicky is set against
relationship_to_romance: Shyama's brother, adjacent to Somu's romance
character_gist: Shyama's brother among the mill workers, the film's comic presence in the chawl.
performance_recognition: Filmfare Best Comedian Award nomination

relationship_to_protagonist: The film's male lead; Bachchan contributes narration only
relationship_to_romance: Half of the film's central relationship
character_gist: Top-billed male lead. The article's cast list gives no character names; its plot describes the protagonist as Ram, an idealist whose one ambition is to do something for his village.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: The female half of the film's central relationship
character_gist: Leading actress of the film, released in her debut year. The cast list gives no character names; the plot describes a rich girl, Rekha, who loves the idealist Ram and takes a job as a city tour guide to be near him.

relationship_to_protagonist: The film's protagonist; Bachchan's Anand is an uncredited guest appearance
relationship_to_romance: Carries the film's romance with Kaajal
character_gist: Orphan raised by a priest who comes to Bombay, befriends the thief who tried to rob him, falls in love with his employer's daughter, and returns to make sense of his friend's crime.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's guest appearance
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance; his family reconciliation is the film's parallel story
character_gist: Alcoholic thief estranged from his wife and son, reformed by Maanav's friendship, whose right hand is chopped off by his crime boss and who is later arrested for marketing contaminated milk powder.
performance_recognition: Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actor nomination

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's guest appearance
relationship_to_romance: The film's romantic lead opposite Maanav
character_gist: Daughter of the owner of Hercules Milk Foods who falls in love with Maanav against her father's wish that she marry Shyamal.

relationship_to_protagonist: The woman Bachchan's Amit rescues, promises to marry and searches for
relationship_to_romance: The film's central romance, kept apart by his family and her criminal record
character_gist: Slum dweller fleeing a drunken stepfather, saved by Amit from a smuggler, jailed on a false robbery charge, and rejected by Amit's father; she leaves the city, becomes a stage success in Calcutta, and is reunited with him at the end.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Amit's friend, who searches for Sapna with him
relationship_to_romance: Actively works to restore the couple
character_gist: Friend who joins Amit in the long search for Sapna after she disappears from Bombay.

relationship_to_protagonist: The smuggler from whom Bachchan's Amit saves Sapna
relationship_to_romance: The predatory threat that brings the couple together
character_gist: Playboy smuggler who wants Sapna for his own pleasure and from whose clutches the taxi driver Amit takes her.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Amit's father, who refuses the marriage
relationship_to_romance: The external opposition that separates the couple for most of the film
character_gist: Father who refuses to accept Sapna on the eve of the wedding, prompting her to leave rather than break up Amit's family.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Vijay's elder brother and the film's protagonist
relationship_to_romance: Carries the film's romance with Sheetal and loses her to a richer man
character_gist: Graduate reduced to singing for a low wage who must support the family after his father's retirement, loses Sheetal to a wealthy businessman, burns his diploma on his father's pyre, is framed by the man who bought his services, and finds a second life with Tulsi.
performance_recognition: Filmfare Award for Best Actor nomination; won Best Director for the same film

relationship_to_protagonist: Bharat's girlfriend, outside Bachchan's Vijay's story
relationship_to_romance: The film's central romance and its moral question, choosing security over love
character_gist: Bharat's girlfriend, frustrated by his poverty, who takes work as a rich businessman's secretary and accepts his proposal; she regrets the choice and dies sacrificing herself in the final confrontation.

relationship_to_protagonist: Rival to Bachchan's Vijay's brother rather than to Vijay himself
relationship_to_romance: The wealthy rival who takes Sheetal from Bharat, and who joins the family's side at the end
character_gist: Rich businessman who employs Sheetal, is drawn to her, and marries her; he stands with Bharat and his brothers against Nekiram in the climax.

relationship_to_protagonist: Belongs to Bharat's story, not to Bachchan's Vijay's
relationship_to_romance: The second romance, which replaces the lost one
character_gist: Woman living in poverty whom Bharat helps and finds salvation in helping; he accepts her as his wife at the end, seeing Sheetal in her.
performance_recognition: Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actress nomination

relationship_to_protagonist: Ally of Bachchan's Vijay's brother
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Sardar who comes to Bharat's rescue when he tries to save Tulsi from a gang of hoodlums, and stands with the family in the final fight.
performance_recognition: Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actor nomination

relationship_to_protagonist: The man Bachchan's Vijay joins his brother to bring down
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Corrupt businessman who persuades Bharat to run his illegal trade as a way out of poverty, then frames him when Bharat moves to inform the police.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Amit's wife
relationship_to_romance: An established marriage under threat rather than a courtship, which is why the film carries no pairing record
character_gist: Wife who witnesses the murder attempt with her husband and whose son is kidnapped to force his silence; the marriage is the stake of the thriller rather than its subject.

relationship_to_protagonist: The policeman who helps Bachchan's Amit find his son
relationship_to_romance: Outside the marriage plot
character_gist: Police inspector who works with Amit to identify the blackmailer and recover the kidnapped child.

relationship_to_protagonist: Part of the conspiracy against Bachchan's Amit
relationship_to_romance: Outside the marriage plot
character_gist: Figure in the criminal group behind the attempted murder of the reporter and the campaign of threats against the one witness.

relationship_to_protagonist: The unseen blackmailer dictating to Bachchan's Amit
relationship_to_romance: Outside the marriage plot
character_gist: Anonymous voice that blackmails Amit into obedience after the kidnapping — a voice-only credit, and one of Kader Khan's earliest appearances in a Bachchan film.

relationship_to_protagonist: The film's protagonist; Bachchan's Anthony is one of several special appearances
relationship_to_romance: No romance; the film's bond is between the rickshaw puller and the abandoned child
character_gist: Rickshaw puller who rescues an abandoned newborn, blames himself when the boy develops polio, raises him as his own, and gives him up sorrowfully to the wealthy parents who can pay for his operation.

relationship_to_protagonist: The child at the film's centre; no connection to Bachchan's special appearance
relationship_to_romance: No romance
character_gist: Boy abandoned outside a temple and raised by the rickshaw puller, disabled by polio and finally operated on, whose return coincides with his foster father's death.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's special appearance
relationship_to_romance: Her reconciliation with her husband is the film's only relationship thread
character_gist: Deserted wife who abandons her newborn outside a temple, reconciles with her husband, and turns to the police to find the son she gave up.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Ravi's fiancee, the only daughter of a wealthy man
relationship_to_romance: The film's romance, secondary to the thriller plot and suspended by his illness
character_gist: Wealthy man's daughter engaged to the travel agent Ravi, whose planned marriage is overtaken by his brain tumour and his entanglement in a murder investigation.

relationship_to_protagonist: Ally who stands by Bachchan's Ravi through the murder case
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Figure from outside respectable society who becomes Ravi's most effective ally once the law has him cornered.
performance_recognition: Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actor nomination

relationship_to_protagonist: The real murderer, whose crime Bachchan's Ravi is suspected of
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Adopted younger brother of the murdered Surendra Sinha, who agrees to pay the ransom for a kidnapping that never happened and is the actual killer.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Ravi's wheelchair-using sister, one of the dependants he is trying to provide for
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance; she is part of the family obligation that overrides it
character_gist: Ravi's disabled sister, whose care, along with their widowed mother and younger brother, is the responsibility that shapes every decision he makes after the diagnosis.
performance_recognition: Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actress nomination

relationship_to_protagonist: The investigator whose interest in Bachchan's Ravi drives his panic
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: CID inspector who finds Surendra Sinha's body six months after the supposed kidnapping and takes a keen interest in the last man known to have met him.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Vijay's younger brother, the policeman who finally shoots him
relationship_to_romance: His courtship of Veera is the film's conventional romance, set against Vijay's unsentimental attachment to Anita
character_gist: Younger brother educated at Vijay's expense, unwavering in his commitment to the law, who joins the police, romances the DCP's daughter, and is assigned the case against his own brother.
performance_recognition: Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actor

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Vijay's mother, who chooses the younger son's morality over the elder's provision
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance; the mother, not the lover, is the emotional centre of Vijay's life
character_gist: Widowed in effect by her husband's flight, she raises both sons by manual labour on a Bombay pavement, refuses to live on Vijay's criminal money, goes to live with Ravi, and holds Vijay as he dies in the temple.
performance_recognition: Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actress nomination

relationship_to_protagonist: The woman Bachchan's Vijay takes up with, on terms that exclude marriage until it is too late
relationship_to_romance: The film's romance, kept deliberately marginal to the family drama
character_gist: Bar hostess who attaches herself to Vijay without demanding respectability, carries his child, and is killed by his enemies before the marriage he finally offers.

relationship_to_protagonist: Belongs to the younger brother's story, not to Bachchan's Vijay's
relationship_to_romance: The respectable romance that contrasts with Vijay and Anita's arrangement
character_gist: Daughter of DCP Narang, courted by Ravi, whose father sends him for police training and starts his career.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Vijay's father, whose disgrace is tattooed on Vijay's arm
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Trade union leader blackmailed into signing away the labourers' rights to save his family, beaten by the men he led, and driven to abandon his family and live out his life on trains.

relationship_to_protagonist: The smuggler who recruits Bachchan's Vijay and makes him a power in the city
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Smuggling boss who sees what the dockworker is worth after he takes on Samant's men, and brings him into the trade that makes his fortune.

relationship_to_protagonist: The shipyard boss whose extortion Bachchan's Vijay refuses to pay
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Shipyard owner and crime boss whose weekly protection money Vijay refuses and whose henchmen he thrashes, the act that begins his criminal career.

relationship_to_protagonist: Believed to be the sister of the man Bachchan plays, and in love with him
relationship_to_romance: The film's romance and its scandal: the couple are thought to be siblings
character_gist: Daughter of the house who falls in love with the young man passed off as her long-lost brother. The article's cast list calls her Smita Singh while its plot calls her Sunita.

relationship_to_protagonist: Believes Bachchan's Badal to be his kidnapped son, then keeps his confession secret
relationship_to_romance: Holds the secret that makes the romance appear incestuous, and lets it stand
character_gist: Horse breeder who killed a dacoit's son defending his farmhouse and lost his own child to the reprisal. Told the truth by Badal, he conceals it from his ailing wife rather than lose the son a second time.

relationship_to_protagonist: The real son whose place Bachchan's Badal has taken
relationship_to_romance: His existence is the threat hanging over the impostor's romance
character_gist: The abducted son, raised as the dacoit Maan Singh's adoptive child, whose return would expose the impersonation. A special appearance.

relationship_to_protagonist: The dacoit whose vendetta created the situation Bachchan's Badal exploits
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Dacoit leader who loses a son in the raid on the Singh farmhouse, swears revenge, and abducts the Thakur's child to raise as his own.

relationship_to_protagonist: The mother whose belief in Bachchan's Badal must not be disturbed
relationship_to_romance: The reason the truth is suppressed, and the person most endangered by the romance
character_gist: Ailing mother overjoyed at the return of her son, from whom the impersonation is concealed and whom the sight of the supposed siblings in love threatens to destroy.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Sukumar's best friend, who recruits him into the deception
relationship_to_romance: His own courtship and marriage frame the film; he engineers the prank that produces Sukumar's romance
character_gist: Botany professor and compulsive prankster who courts Sulekha in disguise, marries her, and to deflate her admiration for her brother-in-law poses as the driver Pyare Mohan while his friend impersonates him.

relationship_to_protagonist: Wife of Bachchan's Sukumar's friend, and his co-conspirator in the prank
relationship_to_romance: Her marriage is the film's established couple, against which Sukumar's courtship runs
character_gist: Wife whose excessive praise of her intellectual brother-in-law provokes the entire deception, and who plays along by pretending to be unhappily married and then unfaithful.

relationship_to_protagonist: The woman Bachchan's Sukumar courts while impersonating his friend
relationship_to_romance: The film's second romance, conducted under a false name until he confesses
character_gist: Younger sister of Prashant's wife, who suspects the false Parimal of betraying his wife, is told the truth by Sukumar, and elopes with him.

relationship_to_protagonist: The target of the entire deception Bachchan's Sukumar is enlisted into
relationship_to_romance: His pedantry is what the two couples conspire against
character_gist: Self-satisfied brother-in-law revered for his intellect, who demands a driver speaking pure Hindi and is comprehensively fooled by the man who answers the call.

relationship_to_protagonist: Friend of both Bachchan's Sukumar and Parimal, party to the prank
relationship_to_romance: His household is where Sukumar meets Vasudha
character_gist: Long-time friend of Parimal's and a knowing participant in the deception; his wife Lata's sister is the woman Sukumar falls for.

relationship_to_protagonist: The neighbour who draws Bachchan's Shekhar out of his drinking and isolation
relationship_to_romance: The film's central romance, defined by her illness rather than by any obstacle between them
character_gist: Cheerful, inquisitive girl with pernicious anaemia, then untreatable, whose liveliness lifts the whole building and changes the depressive next door; the film ends with the couple flying to Switzerland to seek a cure.
performance_recognition: Filmfare Award for Best Actress nomination

relationship_to_protagonist: Mili's father, whose household Bachchan's Shekhar enters
relationship_to_romance: Carries the grief the romance is set against
character_gist: Father who knows his daughter is dying and keeps the household cheerful around her.

relationship_to_protagonist: Neighbour whose reproach stops Bachchan's Shekhar from leaving
relationship_to_romance: The single intervention that produces the film's ending
character_gist: Neighbour who reproaches Shekhar when he decides to go away rather than watch Mili die, making him reconsider and offer marriage and treatment abroad.

relationship_to_protagonist: Mili's mother in the household Bachchan's Shekhar joins
relationship_to_romance: Part of the family setting of the romance
character_gist: Mili's mother, part of the household that shields its daughter from the knowledge of her illness.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Jai's partner in crime and inseparable friend
relationship_to_romance: His noisy courtship of Basanti is the film's comic romance, against Jai's near-silent one with Radha
character_gist: Small-time crook recruited with Jai to capture Gabbar Singh, who falls for the horse-cart driver Basanti, is captured with her, and survives to avenge Jai.

relationship_to_protagonist: The dacoit Bachchan's Jai is hired to take alive, and who kills him
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance; the force that destroys both couples' prospects
character_gist: Dacoit terrorising Ramgarh with a ₹50,000 bounty, who slaughtered the Thakur's family and severed his arms, executes his own men at a game of chance, and forces Basanti to dance on broken glass.
performance_recognition: BFJA Award for Best Supporting Actor; Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actor nomination

relationship_to_protagonist: The former inspector who hires Bachchan's Jai and withholds the truth about himself
relationship_to_romance: Radha's father-in-law, whose household silence surrounds Jai's unspoken romance
character_gist: Retired police inspector who recruits the two crooks who once saved him, conceals under his shawl that Gabbar severed both his arms, and reveals it only when they threaten to quit.
performance_recognition: Filmfare Award for Best Actor nomination

relationship_to_protagonist: Veeru's love interest rather than Bachchan's Jai's, though Jai brokers the match
relationship_to_romance: The film's overt romance, the comic counterpart to Jai and Radha's wordless one
character_gist: Talkative horse-cart driver who takes up with Veeru, is captured by Gabbar's men, and is made to dance on broken glass to keep Veeru alive.

relationship_to_protagonist: The widowed daughter-in-law Bachchan's Jai comes to love
relationship_to_romance: The film's restrained romance, conducted almost without dialogue and ended by his death
character_gist: Thakur's widowed, reclusive daughter-in-law whose family Gabbar massacred, drawn to Jai across a silence the film never breaks; his death widows her a second time.

relationship_to_protagonist: Village elder whose loss keeps Bachchan's Jai and Veeru in Ramgarh
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Village imam whose son Ahmed is murdered by Gabbar to break the villagers' will, and who leads the community in refusing to give up the two mercenaries.

relationship_to_protagonist: Jailer of Bachchan's Jai and Veeru before their recruitment
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Comic prison governor modelled on Chaplin's Great Dictator, whose strutting authority the two prisoners run rings around.
performance_recognition: Filmfare Best Comedian Award nomination

relationship_to_protagonist: One of the dacoits opposing Bachchan's Jai
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Gabbar's sidekick perched above the gang, whose single line confirming the bounty became one of the most quoted moments in Hindi cinema despite amounting to a few seconds of screen time.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Rajesh's former sweetheart, now the wife of the officer hunting him
relationship_to_romance: The film's romance, revived in the worst possible circumstances and never resumed
character_gist: Woman once in love with Rajesh before circumstances separated them, now married to Inspector Sanjay, who finds the fugitive in her own house and is torn between her family and her compassion for him.

relationship_to_protagonist: Leads the manhunt for Bachchan's Rajesh, who is hiding in his home
relationship_to_romance: The husband of the woman the fugitive once loved
character_gist: Police officer leading the hunt for Rajesh, unaware that the fugitive is sheltering under his own roof with his wife and son; Rajesh dies in his arms.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Rajesh's mother
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Mother of the man whose sister's rape and murder, and the killer's acquittal, turn him into a fugitive.

relationship_to_protagonist: Wife of Bachchan's Dharam Chand and mother of the son he also plays
relationship_to_romance: An established marriage destroyed by his imprisonment and hardening
character_gist: Farmer's wife who refuses compensation money as ill-gotten, works as a maid and seamstress while her husband is jailed, falls from the stairs while pregnant, and loses the baby.

relationship_to_protagonist: The romantic interest of the son, the second of Bachchan's two roles
relationship_to_romance: The younger generation's romance, running against the father's ruined marriage
character_gist: Young woman attached to the son Raju, whose connection to the Verma family places her on the other side of the father's vendetta.

relationship_to_protagonist: One of the men Bachchan's Dharam Chand saved, who then ruins him
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: One of three men saved from a tiger by the farmer, who repays him with a warehouse job and then tricks him into signing ownership of the smuggling operation he is jailed for.

relationship_to_protagonist: Rapes the sister-in-law of Bachchan's Dharam Chand while he is in prison
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance; the act that ends any possibility of restoring the family
character_gist: Second of the rescued men, who offers the destitute family compensation, rapes Laxmi when she comes to him for money, and is the immediate cause of her suicide.

relationship_to_protagonist: Sister-in-law of Bachchan's Dharam Chand, who dies in his arms
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Sister-in-law left to nurse the pregnant Radha, who goes to Sujit for medicine money, is raped, delivers the medicines and dies of poison in Dharma's arms while he is out on parole.

relationship_to_protagonist: The officer who arrested Bachchan's Dharam Chand and is set on him again
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Police inspector who made the original arrest at the warehouse and is called in again by the bosses when they sense the released man means to take revenge.

relationship_to_protagonist: The film's protagonist; Bachchan appears only as himself in the song 'Jaaneman Jaaneman'
relationship_to_romance: Carries the film's entire romance, as the suitor too timid to speak
character_gist: Timid Bombay accounting supervisor infatuated with a fellow commuter, who trails her at a distance, is outmanoeuvred by a brasher rival, and is finally coached into confidence by a retired colonel.
performance_recognition: Filmfare Award for Best Actor nomination

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's appearance as himself
relationship_to_romance: The film's romantic lead, and knowingly in charge of a courtship the hero thinks is secret
character_gist: Independent young woman on Arun's commute who is fully aware of his interest from the start and simply waits for him to approach, while a pushier colleague monopolises her attention.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's appearance as himself
relationship_to_romance: Manufactures the confidence that wins the romance
character_gist: Self-appointed confidence coach in Khandala who runs a programme of instruction for lovelorn young men and sends Arun back to Bombay transformed.
performance_recognition: Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actor nomination

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's appearance as himself
relationship_to_romance: The rival whose scooter and self-assurance make the hero's diffidence unbearable
character_gist: Prabha's self-assured colleague, who courts her with scooter rides and monopolises her attention while Arun watches from the sidelines.
performance_recognition: Filmfare Award for Best Performance in a Comic Role nomination

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Amit's college love, married to another man and reunited with him twenty years later
relationship_to_romance: The film's central romance and its long aftermath
character_gist: Student who loves the poet Amit, is married off to an architect against her wishes, and extracts from Amit a promise to marry and keep writing. Two decades on, as a television host, she introduces him to an audience as a stranger.
performance_recognition: Filmfare Award for Best Actress nomination

relationship_to_protagonist: The man who marries the woman Bachchan's Amit loves, and an admirer of his poetry
relationship_to_romance: The husband who works out, on his own, that his wife was the poet's lost love
character_gist: Architect who marries Pooja and, unknowingly, gifts her Amit's first anthology on their wedding night. Years later he invites Amit home and deduces aloud why the poetry stopped.
performance_recognition: Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actor nomination

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Amit's wife, keeping a secret of her own
relationship_to_romance: The second marriage, threatened by a daughter Amit knows nothing about
character_gist: Amit's wife, who gave up an illegitimate daughter years earlier. When that daughter traces her, she acknowledges her privately but presents her to the household as a niece from Delhi, to protect the marriage.
performance_recognition: Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actress nomination

relationship_to_protagonist: Son of the couple whose marriage displaced Bachchan's Amit
relationship_to_romance: The younger generation's romance, which exposes the older one's secret
character_gist: Pooja and Vijay's son, in love with his college friend Pinky; their courtship is what brings the buried history of both families to the surface.

relationship_to_protagonist: The adopted daughter of Bachchan's Amit's wife, unknown to him
relationship_to_romance: Her search for her mother is what threatens Amit's marriage
character_gist: Young woman who learns she was adopted, severs ties with the parents who raised her, and traces her birth mother to Kashmir, only to be introduced there as a distant niece.

relationship_to_protagonist: The young bride of the character whose adult voice Bachchan supplies
relationship_to_romance: The film's central relationship, between two children married young
character_gist: Child bride of the title, whose marriage to the young Amal the film follows. The Wikipedia article carries no plot section, so the role is described only from the cast list and the film's premise.

relationship_to_protagonist: Plays the character on screen whose adult voice Bachchan dubs
relationship_to_romance: The husband in the film's child marriage
character_gist: Young Amal as seen on screen. Bachchan supplies the adult Amal's voice and Ashok Kumar the aged Amal's, so one character is carried by three performers across the film's timespan.

relationship_to_protagonist: Voices the oldest version of the character Bachchan voices as an adult
relationship_to_romance: Narrates the marriage from its far end
character_gist: Provides the voice of Amal in old age, the third and last of the performers sharing the role, after Sachin on screen and Bachchan as the adult voice.

relationship_to_protagonist: Voices the wife opposite the adult Amal that Bachchan voices
relationship_to_romance: The female half of the film's adult voice casting
character_gist: Supplies the adult Rajni's voice, paired with Bachchan's adult Amal — the two stars voice the grown versions of the child couple without appearing on screen.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's voice role
relationship_to_romance: Outside the central marriage
character_gist: Comic figure in the village world around the child marriage.
performance_recognition: Filmfare Best Comedian Award

relationship_to_protagonist: Sister of the character whose adult voice Bachchan supplies
relationship_to_romance: Family presence around the child marriage
character_gist: Amal's sister. The award listings spell the performer's name Kajari; the cast list gives Kajri.
performance_recognition: Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actress

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Vijay's partner in confidence tricks, and the friend the film turns him against
relationship_to_romance: His own love interest runs parallel to Vijay's; neither romance is developed enough for a pairing record
character_gist: Con man who works every scheme alongside Vijay until the discovery that his own father may have caused Vijay's father's death curdles the friendship into suspicion and revenge.
performance_recognition: Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actor nomination

relationship_to_protagonist: Love interest of Bachchan's Vijay
relationship_to_romance: One of the two women caught between the feuding friends; the article's summary is too thin to support a pairing record
character_gist: One of the two women attached to the con men, caught in the middle when the partnership collapses into revenge.

relationship_to_protagonist: Attached to Bachchan's Vijay's partner rather than to him
relationship_to_romance: The second of the two love interests the plot summary mentions without developing
character_gist: Love interest on Ajay's side of the partnership, present through the friendship's collapse.

relationship_to_protagonist: The law circling Bachchan's Vijay and his partner
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Police commissioner who circles the growing chaos as the two con men turn on each other.

relationship_to_protagonist: Tied to the paternity secret that destroys Bachchan's Vijay's friendship
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Figure from the fathers' generation whose identity is bound up in the revelation that recontextualises the first half of the film.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Amit's wife, who believes him dead for six years
relationship_to_romance: The film's central romance, resumed through a disguise
character_gist: Wife who becomes a successful film actress under the name Sunita Devi while her husband, thrown from a train and amnesiac, is presumed dead; her manager is the man who tried to kill him.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Amit's former best friend, who threw him from a train
relationship_to_romance: Interposes himself between the couple as the wife's manager
character_gist: Amit's one-time best friend, who attempted to murder him on a moving train and then made himself indispensable to his widow as her manager.
performance_recognition: Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actor — the film's only win

relationship_to_protagonist: Figure in the world Bachchan's Amit re-enters in disguise
relationship_to_romance: Adjacent to the reunion plot
character_gist: Supporting figure in the film world through which the disguised Amit reaches his wife and her manager.

relationship_to_protagonist: Neighbour of Bachchan's Amit
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Amit's neighbour, a small early role for Mithun Chakraborty in the year of his screen debut.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Ahmed Raza's partner in the professional-witness racket
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance; the film's bond is the friendship of the two false witnesses
character_gist: One half of the pair who loiter around courts selling perjured evidence, reformed by Kabir Das and then unable to earn honestly, who sets out to clear the man who reformed them.

relationship_to_protagonist: The man whose example turns Bachchan's Ahmed Raza honest, and whom he then tries to save
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Upright figure who influences the two mock witnesses into going straight, and is then arrested for a murder he says he did not commit, sending them after the real killer.

relationship_to_protagonist: Connected to Bachchan's Ahmed Raza's side of the story
relationship_to_romance: The romance is implied rather than developed, which is why the film carries no pairing record
character_gist: Young woman in the world of the two witnesses; the article's plot summary is too compressed to give the role a developed arc.

relationship_to_protagonist: Belongs to the parallel strand of the ensemble around Bachchan's character
relationship_to_romance: Adjacent to the film's undeveloped romantic threads
character_gist: Schoolmaster's daughter in the film's ensemble; the plot summary does not detail her part.

relationship_to_protagonist: Part of the ensemble around Bachchan's Ahmed Raza
relationship_to_romance: Outside the central relationships
character_gist: One of the film's women, whose own court case is among the strands the article's award and cast listings preserve better than its plot summary does.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Shiva's long-lost childhood friend, reunited with him in adulthood
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance; the film's emotional centre is the restored friendship
character_gist: Taciturn loner separated from Shiva as a boy when both families were destroyed, who fights crime alone, is sent to avenge a death, tracks Shiva down and discovers who he is.

relationship_to_protagonist: The woman Bachchan's Shiva falls in love with and marries
relationship_to_romance: The film's romance, secondary to the friendship plot
character_gist: Woman Shiva loves and marries, and one of the two voices — with his mother — who persuade him to leave the village and live without violence.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Shiva's mother, and the moral check on him
relationship_to_romance: Shares with the wife the decision that sends him away
character_gist: Mother whose insistence, alongside his wife's, sends Shiva out of the village to attempt an honest and nonviolent life after he is blamed for a farmer's murder.

relationship_to_protagonist: The villain who destroyed the families of Bachchan's Shiva and his friend
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Main antagonist, responsible for separating the two boys and destroying both their families, and the target of the reunited friends at the end.

relationship_to_protagonist: Ally of Bachchan's Shiva whose death drives the second half
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Figure whose killing is the death the loner Shera is charged with avenging, the thread that brings the two friends back together.

relationship_to_protagonist: The film's protagonist; Bachchan contributes the narration only
relationship_to_romance: No romance; his neglect of his wife is one of the film's charges against his class
character_gist: Wealthy Lucknow nobleman so absorbed in chess that he neglects his wife and ignores the British annexation of Awadh, fleeing the city with his friend to keep playing.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: No romance; his marriage is likewise abandoned to the chessboard
character_gist: The second of the two inseparable, indolent noblemen, who ends the film shooting at his friend over a quarrel about the game and is forgiven in the same breath.
performance_recognition: Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actor

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Nawab of Awadh: a languid poet and artist no longer in command of events, devoted to religious practice and pleasure, unable to resist the East India Company's demand for his throne.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: The neglected wife, the film's domestic measure of her husband's abdication
character_gist: Mirza's wife, harangued and ignored while her husband plays chess, whose frustration the film uses to indict the nobleman's detachment.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: East India Company general executing the annexation of Awadh, the historical force against which the two chess players' indifference is set.

relationship_to_protagonist: The woman Bachchan's Alok loves, from the world his father despises
relationship_to_romance: The film's romance, secondary to the father-son rupture
character_gist: Young woman of the courtesan's household Alok frequents for music, and the attachment that confirms his father's conviction that his son is throwing his life away.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Alok's father, and his antagonist
relationship_to_romance: Opposes the world the romance belongs to
character_gist: Widowed advocate who wins the case that demolishes the slum his son's friends live in, throws Alok out for driving a horse-carriage, then runs cheap motor coaches specifically to starve his son's livelihood.

relationship_to_protagonist: The former courtesan whose company Bachchan's Alok keeps against his father's orders
relationship_to_romance: Presides over the household the romance belongs to
character_gist: Former courtesan of the slum quarter whose music draws Alok back repeatedly, and who is rendered homeless by his own father's courtroom victory.

relationship_to_protagonist: Companion to Bachchan's Alok in his life outside the family firm
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Friend from the world Alok chooses over his father's law practice.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Alok's music teacher
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Music teacher whose classes Alok enrols in instead of learning to practise law; a guest appearance.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Anthony's eldest brother, separated from him in childhood
relationship_to_romance: His courtship of Lakshmi runs parallel to Anthony's of Jenny
character_gist: Eldest of the three separated brothers, raised Hindu by a police superintendent and grown into a police inspector, unaware that the men beside him are his brothers.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Anthony's youngest brother
relationship_to_romance: His pursuit of Dr Salma against her father's objection is the third of the film's parallel romances
character_gist: Youngest brother, raised Muslim by the tailor who found him, and a popular qawwali singer courting a doctor whose father disapproves.

relationship_to_protagonist: The woman Bachchan's Anthony courts
relationship_to_romance: Anthony's romance, one of three running in parallel
character_gist: Young woman under a bodyguard's protection whom Anthony pursues, and whose family history is entangled with the crime boss at the centre of the plot.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Anthony's mother, blinded and separated from all three sons
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance; the mother is the film's organising emotional claim
character_gist: Mother who leaves a suicide note, is blinded by a falling branch in the storm that scatters her sons, and twenty-two years later is saved by blood donated by all three without any of them knowing who she is.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Anthony's father, who left the three boys at the Gandhi statue
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Chauffeur jailed for his employer's hit-and-run, who returns to a starving family, escapes with a car full of smuggled gold, leaves his sons at a statue to draw off pursuit, and becomes rich and alone.

relationship_to_protagonist: Belongs to the youngest brother's romance, not Bachchan's
relationship_to_romance: The third parallel romance, opposed by her father
character_gist: Doctor courted by the qawwali singer Akbar over the objections of her grumpy father Taiyyab Ali.

relationship_to_protagonist: Attached to the eldest brother's story
relationship_to_romance: Amar's romance, the second of the three
character_gist: Young woman living with her grandmother and a stepmother, whose life intersects the eldest brother's police work and becomes his romance.

relationship_to_protagonist: The crime lord whose betrayal scattered Bachchan's Anthony's family
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Crime lord who lets his chauffeur serve his prison sentence and then disowns him, setting the entire plot in motion; he plays the twins Robert and Albert, with Tom Alter dubbing Albert's voice.

relationship_to_protagonist: The film's protagonist; Bachchan appears only as a qawwali singer in a special appearance
relationship_to_romance: His feigned romance with Lalli is the film's central device, and is revealed to be nothing of the kind
character_gist: Mechanic whose workshop becomes an engineering empire over ten years, and whose wife and children turn into party animals on the money. He leaves home, teams up with an abandoned housewife to act the doting lover, and finally wills the business to his workers.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's special appearance
relationship_to_romance: The wife whose jealousy the staged romance is designed to provoke
character_gist: Charandas's dutiful, religious wife, transformed by money into someone who throws parties for the dog's birthday, and who later sues her husband and schemes to have him declared mentally ill.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's special appearance
relationship_to_romance: Half of the film's pretended couple; the film ends by insisting the relationship was paternal
character_gist: Lonely housewife abandoned by a self-serving stage actor, who meets Charandas by accident and joins him in playing a lovey-dovey couple to shame both their families. He reveals at the end that he had taken her only as a daughter.

relationship_to_protagonist: Appears in the same qawwali special appearance as Bachchan
relationship_to_romance: Outside the plot
character_gist: One of three stars — with Bachchan and Sunil Dutt — brought in for special appearances; he and Bachchan appear together as qawwali singers.

relationship_to_protagonist: Raises Bachchan's Amit as his own son after promising the boy's dying mother
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Police officer who captures the bandit Mangal Singh, promises his dying wife to raise her son, and brings up that boy alongside his own — the honest one turning out to be the bandit's, the wicked one his own.

relationship_to_protagonist: Raised as Bachchan's Amit's brother, and his adversary through most of the film
relationship_to_romance: His courtship of Shabbo parallels Amit's of Neetu
character_gist: The DSP's biological son, who comes to believe he is the bandit's, teaches blind children by day and smuggles for Mangal's gang, and repents by leading the blinded Amit to the bandit's lair.

relationship_to_protagonist: The pickpocket Bachchan's Amit is drawn to, and the carrier of the locket that reveals his parentage
relationship_to_romance: The film's romance on Amit's side
character_gist: One of two orphaned pickpocketing sisters, smitten with the inspector and half-heartedly going straight for him. The locket he gives her is the one Mangal gave his wife, and it exposes Amit as Mangal's son.

relationship_to_protagonist: Sister of the woman Bachchan's Amit loves
relationship_to_romance: The second of the paired romances, attached to Kishen
character_gist: The other pickpocketing sister, who with Neetu sets out to kill the bandit who murdered their parents and is taken hostage in the attempt.

relationship_to_protagonist: The bandit who is revealed to be Bachchan's Amit's father
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Bandit captured on the night his son is born, who emerges from fourteen years in jail believing the wrong boy is his, draws that boy into his gang, and recognises his real son only by a locket.

relationship_to_protagonist: Head of the smuggling network Bachchan's Amit is assigned to destroy
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Crime boss above Mangal Singh in the smuggling operation, working through a second-in-command named Jackson.

relationship_to_protagonist: The film's protagonist; Bachchan appears as himself among the many stars in guest turns
relationship_to_romance: Carries the film's romance with Mary
character_gist: Shopkeeper's son who runs away to Bombay to become an actor, lives in a chawl, becomes a star, is accused in a scandal that costs him his love, and is vindicated.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's appearance as himself
relationship_to_romance: The film's romantic lead, who leaves during the scandal and returns to marry him
character_gist: Murari's love interest, who leaves him when the scandals break and marries him once he proves his innocence.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's appearance as himself
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Cloth-shop owner who wants his son in the family business rather than in films, the obstacle the hero runs from.
