relationship_to_protagonist: The film's protagonist; Bachchan appears in a guest turn as himself
relationship_to_romance: His late remarriage is the film's central relationship — companionship rather than courtship
character_gist: Parsi widower nearing retirement, living with four sons, who decides to remarry for help and company and merges his household with a widow's, to the horror of both families.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's guest appearance
relationship_to_romance: The other half of the late-life marriage
character_gist: Parsi widow with a daughter and two sons, introduced to Homi by a mutual friend, whose family must learn to live with his.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's guest appearance
relationship_to_romance: Part of the younger generation adjusting to the merged household
character_gist: One of the widow's sons, among the children who must accommodate the new marriage.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's guest appearance
relationship_to_romance: The younger romantic thread in the combined family
character_gist: Daughter of a wealthy father, attached to the younger generation of the two Parsi families the film brings together.

relationship_to_protagonist: The landlord whose persecution turns Bachchan's Jeeva into a dacoit
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Tyrant who rapes his secretary's daughter, raises taxes on inheriting the region, assaults Jeeva's mother, and frames Jeeva for poisoning a cow. He dies crashing a chartered plane at Laxman Jhula.

relationship_to_protagonist: The shoemaker who tries to protect Bachchan's Jeeva from the Thakur's men
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Shoemaker who intervenes when Jeeva is beaten by the Thakur's men and fails, then leads the exiled villagers in founding a new colony.

relationship_to_protagonist: Billed immediately after Bachchan in the film's infobox, but the article's plot gives her no role
relationship_to_romance: The film's romance is recorded as Minor with no pairing record, because no source describes the relationship
character_gist: Leading actress of the film. The Wikipedia article has no cast section, and its plot summary never names her character, so the part cannot be described from the available sources.

relationship_to_protagonist: Victim of the Thakur, in the village Bachchan's Jeeva is driven from
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Daughter of the secretary Keshavram, raped by Thakur Jaswant Singh in the episode that establishes his impunity at the film's opening.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Jeeva's mother, whose assault and death drive the plot
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Old woman washing a floor whom the Thakur assaults after slipping on it, bringing her son into the quarrel; her death shortly after his exile is what turns Jeeva to dacoity.

relationship_to_protagonist: Engaged to Bachchan's Amit, and later drawn to his double Shankar
relationship_to_romance: The film's romance, split across both of Bachchan's roles
character_gist: Woman engaged to the teacher Amit, who takes widow's garb after his murder and resolves never to remarry, then finds his criminal look-alike entering her household; her affection is part of what reforms him.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Amit's younger brother, whose bad company gets Amit killed
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance, but the reason the look-alike is brought into the household
character_gist: Spoiled unemployed younger brother whose trouble draws Amit to his death, and who, guilt-ridden, hires the look-alike Shankar believing he has his brother back.

relationship_to_protagonist: Attached to the brother of Bachchan's character
relationship_to_romance: A small secondary romance beside the main one
character_gist: Raju's fiancée, a small role in the household around the two brothers.

relationship_to_protagonist: The kingpin holding Bachchan's Shankar to his criminal past
relationship_to_romance: Kidnaps Suman to force the hero's hand
character_gist: Crime boss who kidnaps Suman and forces Shankar to smuggle diamonds under cover of an international car rally.

relationship_to_protagonist: The woman Bachchan's Ram Kumar loves, and the villain's sister
relationship_to_romance: The film's romance, compromised by her relation to the man he is hunting
character_gist: Young woman Ram Kumar falls in love with, unaware that she is the sister of the criminal posing as the industrialist Dharamdas.

relationship_to_protagonist: Drove Bachchan's Ram Kumar's father to suicide and is the target of his investigation
relationship_to_romance: Both the hero's romance and his impersonation run through this man's household
character_gist: Criminal who frames an honest teacher as corrupt, driving him to suicide, then poses as a respectable industrialist while smuggling drugs and keeping venomous snakes to kill traitors.

relationship_to_protagonist: The woman Bachchan's hero woos in disguise to get close to the villain
relationship_to_romance: A calculated courtship rather than a romance, run in parallel with the real one
character_gist: Dharamdas's beloved, wooed by Ram Kumar in the guise of Prince Chandrashekhar, a diamond businessman from South Africa, purely to get near her protector.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Ram Kumar's father, whose suicide opens the film
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Honest teacher wrongly implicated as corrupt by Digvijay Singh, whose suicide sets his son on the search that drives the film.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Vijay's father, who abandoned his mother, and the target of his revenge
relationship_to_romance: His abandonment of Shanti is the original act the whole film answers
character_gist: Man who leaves his pregnant girlfriend in 1953 to marry an heiress and a partnership, refuses to recognise the son who returns 25 years later, and is ruined in a business war he does not understand is a family one.
performance_recognition: Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actor nomination

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Vijay's legitimate half-brother, caught in the crossfire
relationship_to_romance: His engagement to Sheetal is the relationship Vijay deliberately destabilises
character_gist: Son returned from abroad to take his place in his father's company, whose girlfriend and whose sister's marriage both become instruments in his unknown half-brother's campaign.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Vijay's romance, and the employee he first tries to buy
relationship_to_romance: The film's romance, beginning with an attempted bribe and ending in loyalty
character_gist: Gupta's devoted secretary who refuses Vijay's bribe for tender information, is wrongly fired when Gupta assumes she sold him out, is cleared by Vijay himself, and goes to work for him.

relationship_to_protagonist: Courted by Bachchan's Vijay as a tactic against his half-brother
relationship_to_romance: A romance used as a weapon rather than pursued for itself
character_gist: Daughter and general manager of the industrialist P. L. Verma, and Shekhar's girlfriend, between whom Vijay sets out to create differences at his company's anniversary party.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Vijay's mother, whose life is the grievance he acts on
relationship_to_romance: The abandoned romance that generates the plot
character_gist: Woman abandoned while pregnant in 1953, who refuses her lover's guilty offer of help, leaves the city and raises her son alone; her death releases him to Delhi and revenge. A special appearance.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Vijay's half-sister, whose marriage he encourages against their father's wishes
relationship_to_romance: The third romance, used tactically like the second
character_gist: Gupta's daughter, encouraged by Vijay to marry Ravi against her father's wishes — another blow struck at the family through its relationships.

relationship_to_protagonist: Criminal opponent in the business war Bachchan's Vijay wages
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Operator on the criminal side of the construction business, part of the escalation as father and son turn their wealth and integrity into weapons.

relationship_to_protagonist: Infiltrates the gang to kill Bachchan's Don, then allies with the double who replaces him
relationship_to_romance: The film's romance, beginning with her intent to murder him
character_gist: Woman who joins Don's gang to avenge her brother Ramesh and his fiancée, trains in combat for it, and nearly kills the impostor before learning he is not Don.

relationship_to_protagonist: Steals the diary that could clear Bachchan's Vijay, then joins him
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Father who steals the incriminating diary to trace his own children, meets Vijay and Roma, joins their side, and escapes the hideout with his son and daughter.

relationship_to_protagonist: Recruits Bachchan's Vijay to impersonate the dead Don, then dies leaving him unprovable
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Officer who buries Don in secret, recruits his look-alike to infiltrate the gang in exchange for educating the street performer's adopted children, and is shot dead in a crossfire — taking with him the only proof of the impersonation.

relationship_to_protagonist: Poses as the Interpol officer holding Bachchan's Vijay, having killed the man who could clear him
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Criminal who captures the real R. K. Malik and takes his place, murders D'Silva at the party, exposes Roma to the gang and kidnaps the children to force a surrender.

relationship_to_protagonist: Killed by the criminal Bachchan also plays
relationship_to_romance: Her death is half of Roma's motive for revenge
character_gist: Fiancée of Roma's brother Ramesh; both were killed by Don, which is what puts Roma inside the gang.

relationship_to_protagonist: The woman Bachchan's Sikandar has loved since childhood, who refuses him
relationship_to_romance: The film's central unrequited love, running one way while another runs toward him
character_gist: Daughter of the man who threw Sikandar out, the one person who was kind to him as a boy, who as an adult demands he never speak to her again and loves his friend Vishal instead.

relationship_to_protagonist: The courtesan who loves Bachchan's Sikandar without return
relationship_to_romance: The mirror of the main romance: she loves him as hopelessly as he loves Kaamna
character_gist: Courtesan who falls in unrequited love with her regular visitor, refuses other clients for him, and is coveted by the criminal Dilawar, whose jealousy turns lethal.
performance_recognition: Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actress nomination

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Sikandar's closest friend, and the man Kaamna loves
relationship_to_romance: The friend for whom the hero gives up the woman he has wanted since childhood
character_gist: Down-on-his-luck lawyer who risks his life to save Sikandar from a bomb blast and moves into his house with his mother — and becomes the man Kaamna loves.
performance_recognition: Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actor nomination

relationship_to_protagonist: Swears to kill Bachchan's Sikandar over the courtesan
relationship_to_romance: The violent third point of the Zohra triangle
character_gist: Criminal in love with Zohra Begum who learns of her love for Sikandar, is thrashed by him in the ensuing fight, and swears to kill him.

relationship_to_protagonist: The Muslim woman who adopts and names Bachchan's Sikandar
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Servant in Ramnath's house who adopts the orphan boy, names him Sikandar — the conqueror — and dies leaving him to raise her daughter Mehroo.

relationship_to_protagonist: The fakir who gives Bachchan's Sikandar the film's governing idea
relationship_to_romance: Frames the fatalism with which the hero bears his unrequited love
character_gist: Fakir who tells the grieving boy to find happiness in sadness and embrace what life brings, and so become the conqueror of fate. A cameo appearance.

relationship_to_protagonist: Sent to stop the inspector, and mistakes Bachchan's gambler for him
relationship_to_romance: One of the film's two romances, built entirely on the mistaken identity
character_gist: Club dancer sent by Saxena to stop the CID inspector, who meets the gambler Jay in Rome and takes him for his look-alike.

relationship_to_protagonist: Targeted by Bachchan's Jay for her money, and met instead by his double
relationship_to_romance: The second romance, and the other half of the switched-identity device
character_gist: Heiress whom Jay plans to marry for her inheritance, and who meets Inspector Vijay at Rome airport instead; he plays along to find out who his look-alike is.

relationship_to_protagonist: The don both of Bachchan's roles are ultimately set against
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Underworld boss after the blueprints of a top-secret laser weapon, whom the twin brothers finally combine to stop.

relationship_to_protagonist: Hires Bachchan's Jay and turns his gift into a weapon
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Don who recruits the unbeaten gambler to fleece rich men at cards so that he can blackmail them afterwards.

relationship_to_protagonist: Part of the network Bachchan's inspector role pursues to Rome
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Member of the smuggling network around Saxena, in the Rome half of the plot.

relationship_to_protagonist: The film's protagonist; Bachchan appears as himself in a guest turn
relationship_to_romance: Carries the romance with his employer's daughter, conducted in his second identity
character_gist: Chartered accountant who invents a clean-shaven twin brother to cover one lie to his moustache-loving employer, then has to sustain both identities, hire a fake mother, and court the boss's daughter as the invented brother.
performance_recognition: Filmfare Award for Best Actor

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's guest appearance
relationship_to_romance: The obstacle the whole deception exists to manage, and the father of the woman in question
character_gist: Employer of rigid traditional values who distrusts men without moustaches and secretly loves sport, is fooled into believing in a twin brother and a fake mother, and ends the film shaving off his own moustache.
performance_recognition: Filmfare Best Comedian Award; Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actor nomination

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's guest appearance
relationship_to_romance: The romance at the centre of the deception
character_gist: Bhawani Shankar's daughter, taught music by the invented brother and drawn to him, then upset to learn the truth and married to the man in his real identity.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's guest appearance
relationship_to_romance: Sustains the deception on which the romance depends
character_gist: Socialite recruited to impersonate the hero's long-dead mother, who is then recognised at a party and must invent a twin sister of her own.
performance_recognition: Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actress nomination

relationship_to_protagonist: Appears under his own name, as Bachchan does in his guest turn
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Plays himself as the friend who helps shave off the moustache and set the double life going.
performance_recognition: Filmfare Best Comedian Award nomination

relationship_to_protagonist: The woman Bachchan's Inder bets he can buy, and comes to love
relationship_to_romance: The film's central romance, which begins as a wager and costs her everything
character_gist: Professor's daughter who cannot be bought with money but is won by the publication of her poems. Shamed by her father for one lie, she leaves home forever, is robbed, is presumed dead in a train accident, and becomes a renowned singer heard on the radio.
performance_recognition: Filmfare Award for Best Actress nomination

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Inder's college mate, who provokes the bet that drives the film
relationship_to_romance: Secretly admires Rama himself, and so sets the terms of the wager
character_gist: Old college friend who, while privately admiring Rama, tells Inder she is the kind of woman money cannot lure — the remark Inder turns into a bet.

relationship_to_protagonist: Rama's father, who finds her in Bachchan's Inder's bedroom
relationship_to_romance: His scorn is what drives the romance apart
character_gist: Professor who arrives unannounced at Inder's house, finds his daughter there and scorns her for lying, driving her out of the household for good.

relationship_to_protagonist: The alibi Rama uses when she goes to meet Bachchan's Inder
relationship_to_romance: The lie told in her name is what exposes the meeting
character_gist: Friend Rama claims to be seeing off when she goes to meet Inder — the lie that brings her father to his door.
performance_recognition: Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actress nomination

relationship_to_protagonist: Figure in the Pratapgarh world Bachchan's Inder is sent to supervise
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Local character in the town where the contractor is sent to oversee his project, nephew of the pandit Prabhakar Chaturvedi.

relationship_to_protagonist: The woman Bachchan's Natwar meets in the village he infiltrates
relationship_to_romance: The film's romance, running alongside the revenge plot
character_gist: Young woman of Chandanpur, where Natwar arrives disguised as a hunter to reach the man who ruined his brother.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Natwar's elder brother and guardian, who comes to despise him
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Police officer framed for bribery by Vikram, who raised his younger brother and then, not understanding the criminal persona the boy adopts to avenge him, develops a grudge against him.

relationship_to_protagonist: The mastermind who framed Bachchan's Natwar's brother
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Criminal mastermind who framed the honest inspector for bribery and now terrorises the villagers of Chandanpur using a tiger, while hunting a diamond necklace.

relationship_to_protagonist: The informant who points Bachchan's Natwar at the villain
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Underworld figure posing as a burnt man, once Vikram's ally and now bent on his own revenge, who tells Natwar where Vikram is and what he wants.

relationship_to_protagonist: Village authority in the world Bachchan's Natwar enters in disguise
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Village headman in Chandanpur, part of the community living under Vikram's terror.

relationship_to_protagonist: One of the four stars interviewed, as Bachchan is
relationship_to_romance: No romance; the film is a quasi-documentary on Hindi cinema
character_gist: Appears as himself in the original interviews the film is built around, alongside Bachchan, Hema Malini and Zeenat Aman.

relationship_to_protagonist: Interviewed in the same film as Bachchan, in the same capacity
relationship_to_romance: No romance
character_gist: One of the four stars giving original interviews in Krishna Shah's history of Hindi cinema, framed by the reactions of a 1970s theatre audience.

relationship_to_protagonist: Interviewed alongside Bachchan
relationship_to_romance: No romance
character_gist: Appears as herself among the film's interviewed stars. The article has no cast section; these credits come from its infobox.

relationship_to_protagonist: The engineer who befriends Bachchan's disgraced Vijay at the mine
relationship_to_romance: His romance with the reporter Anita runs beside Vijay's with the doctor
character_gist: Engineer in charge of the mines who becomes Vijay's friend, romances the press photographer Anita, and injures his leg saving the trapped miners in the flood.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Vijay's enemy at the mine, then his friend after Vijay gives him blood
relationship_to_romance: His romance with Channo is the third of the film's parallel pairings
character_gist: Escaped convict hiding among the miners who repeatedly fights Vijay, is carried to the doctor by him and saved with his blood, becomes his friend, and dies rescuing the trapped men.
performance_recognition: Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actor nomination

relationship_to_protagonist: The one person who supports Bachchan's Vijay and makes him confront his past
relationship_to_romance: The film's romance for Bachchan's character, therapeutic rather than ardent
character_gist: Doctor at the colliery who alone stands by the disgraced captain, pressing him to face what he did and move on.

relationship_to_protagonist: Belongs to the convict's story rather than Bachchan's
relationship_to_romance: Mangal's romance, the liveliest of the three
character_gist: Bangle seller at the mining settlement, attached to the fugitive Mangal Singh.
performance_recognition: Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actress nomination

relationship_to_protagonist: Attached to the engineer rather than to Bachchan's Vijay
relationship_to_romance: Ravi's romance, the second of the three pairings
character_gist: Press reporter and photographer covering the colliery, and the engineer Ravi's romantic interest.

relationship_to_protagonist: The mine owner whose negligence Bachchan's Vijay and his friends unite against
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Greedy colliery owner who gives the miners poor equipment, insufficient medical supplies and no facilities — the conditions that produce the flood the three men die trying to survive.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Vijay's father, who disowned him
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Retired military man who disowns his son after the navy court-martials him for abandoning ship — part of the disgrace that sends Vijay into the mines.

relationship_to_protagonist: The wealthy young woman Bachchan's Ajay courts under a false impression of wealth
relationship_to_romance: The film's romance, built on a pretence he eventually confesses
character_gist: Rich man's daughter who returns Ajay's feelings while he passes off a borrowed suit, car and flat as his own; she stays attached to him after the confession that gets him thrown out of her father's house.

relationship_to_protagonist: Aruna's father, who takes the case against Bachchan's Ajay personally
relationship_to_romance: The external opposition, acting through the courts
character_gist: Lawyer who, wanting to teach the young man a lesson for deceiving his daughter, eagerly takes the client's case against him.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Ajay's mother, who funds and then rescues his venture
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Mother who hands over her insurance money to bail out her son's galvanometer business, then urges him to repair the instruments himself and sells her gold jewellery when he runs short.

relationship_to_protagonist: The friend who lends Bachchan's Ajay the trappings of wealth
relationship_to_romance: Makes the pretence the romance rests on possible
character_gist: Chartered accountant who supplies the suit, car and flat that let Ajay pass as rich, and later sends him ten thousand rupees disguised as an order.

relationship_to_protagonist: The craftsman whose defection ruins Bachchan's Ajay's business
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Skilled repairer of galvanometers on whom the venture depends, bought off by bigger businessmen with money for his daughter's wedding.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Amit's twin, separated at birth and raised by their mother
relationship_to_romance: His romance with Anu parallels Amit's with Basanti
character_gist: Twin kept by their mother and raised into a dedicated police officer, who clashes with the petty criminal Amit, becomes his closest friend, and is blinded in the attack their own father commissioned.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Amit's romance
relationship_to_romance: The film's romance on Amit's side, secondary to the brothers' plot
character_gist: Young woman attached to the drunken, exploited Amit, one of the two romances running beside the story of the separated twins.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Amit's mother, who never knew he survived
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Mother whose newborn is stolen and sold to a bootlegger, abandoned by her criminal husband, who raises the remaining twin alone and gives up hope of finding the other.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Amit's father, who unknowingly hires him to kill his own twin
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Criminal who abandons his wife after one twin is stolen, and years later — ignorant that his family survives — hires the son he does not recognise to murder the other son at a Navratri dance.

relationship_to_protagonist: The man who stole Bachchan's Amit as a newborn and sold him
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Rival gangster who steals one of the twins at birth and sells him to the bootlegger Pascal, the act on which the whole plot rests.

relationship_to_protagonist: Attached to Bachchan's Amit's twin rather than to him
relationship_to_romance: The second of the film's paired romances
character_gist: Romantic interest of the police officer Kishan, on the respectable side of the twin narrative.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Vijay's sworn rival among burglars, and his partner in the school deception
relationship_to_romance: His courtship of the dance teacher runs parallel to Vijay's of the principal's daughter
character_gist: Petty burglar sent by his own boss on the same kidnapping as his enemy, who enters the school as the music teacher Lakshman, falls for the dance teacher, and grows too fond of the boy to go through with it.

relationship_to_protagonist: The woman Bachchan's Vijay courts while posing as a games teacher
relationship_to_romance: The film's romance on Bachchan's side, and one of the two forces that reform him
character_gist: The principal's daughter, who falls in love with the man she knows as the PE instructor Ram and, on learning what he is, changes him by insisting on it rather than exposing him.

relationship_to_protagonist: Attached to Bachchan's partner rather than to him
relationship_to_romance: The second romance, mirroring the first
character_gist: Dance teacher at the school who falls for the disguised Sunil and, like Anju, turns her burglar toward honesty.

relationship_to_protagonist: The boss whose kidnapping plan Bachchan's Vijay abandons and then thwarts
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Crime boss who loses faith in his man, carries out the abduction of the boy himself, and is arrested when the two former rivals join forces to rescue him.

relationship_to_protagonist: Father of the child Bachchan's Vijay is sent to abduct
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Wealthy man whose son Bittoo is the target of the ransom plot that brings both burglars into the school.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Vijay's closest friend, and his rival for the same woman
relationship_to_romance: The friendship and the romance are the same conflict: both men love Sheetal
character_gist: Lawyer who bails out the criminals his policeman friend arrests, loves the woman who loves his friend, takes the villain's side to make Vijay's life hell, and repents on finding the letter in which Vijay had given her up for him.
performance_recognition: Filmfare Award for Best Actor nomination

relationship_to_protagonist: The woman Bachchan's Vijay loves and then renounces for his friend
relationship_to_romance: The film's romance, and the wedge the villain drives into the friendship
character_gist: Woman who returns Vijay's love while his friend nurses a one-sided crush on her, and who is later made the price of Ravi's agreeing to defend him.

relationship_to_protagonist: Sets out to destroy the friendship Bachchan's Vijay depends on
relationship_to_romance: Weaponises the romance by revealing it to the rival
character_gist: Crime boss who discovers the romance from a photograph, tells Ravi about it to split the friends, frames Vijay for murder, and has an informant's family run down by a truck.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Vijay's informant, who dies in his arms
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Former checkpoint officer who refused to let a truck through unchecked and lost his wife and his son's mobility to the reprisal; he feeds Vijay his information and dies asking him to care for the boy.

relationship_to_protagonist: Part of the criminal apparatus Bachchan's Vijay is up against
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Daaga's associate, shot by Daaga himself during the final escape when a sprained ankle slows him down.

relationship_to_protagonist: Saves Bachchan's Vijay and his friend at the climax
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Daaga's moll who is in fact a spy and the sister of the informant's wife, feeding Tony his information and freeing the captured men.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Balram's elder brother, forced into theft while Balram was sent to school
relationship_to_romance: His romance with Madhu is the more developed of the two
character_gist: Elder brother made a thief by their uncle and kept on pocket money into adulthood, who becomes a police informer inside the smuggling world at his policeman brother's suggestion.

relationship_to_protagonist: The uncle who raised Bachchan's Balram after murdering his parents
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Uncle who kills the boys' parents, tells them it was an accident, makes one a thief and the other a policeman to serve his own scheme, and keeps both in line with a needle set in the end of his cane.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Balram's love interest
relationship_to_romance: Recorded as Minor with no pairing record: the article establishes the attachment but nothing of its development
character_gist: College professor's daughter attached to the policeman brother; the plot summary gives the relationship no development beyond its existence.

relationship_to_protagonist: Attached to Bachchan's Balram's brother
relationship_to_romance: The second romance, entangled with the uncle's paternity
character_gist: Young woman who has come to the area with her courtesan mother in search of her father, whom she believes to be Jagatpal — a belief he refuses and then disproves.

relationship_to_protagonist: The smuggler Bachchan's Balram's brother infiltrates
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: One of India's biggest smugglers, in whose organisation Ram rises to lieutenant before robbing him.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Vijay's honest elder brother, whose death the film avenges
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance; his widow's grief motivates the brothers
character_gist: Upright police officer transferred to Mumbai, estranged from his two conning younger brothers, whose killing by Shakaal turns their swindling into a campaign of revenge.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Vijay's brother and partner in every confidence trick
relationship_to_romance: His attraction to Renu is the film's second romance
character_gist: The second of the con-artist brothers, who works the hotel and restaurant scams with Vijay, falls for a woman running a con of her own, and joins the mission against Shakaal.

relationship_to_protagonist: The villain who kills Bachchan's Vijay's brother and becomes the film's target
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Bald, island-dwelling criminal mastermind who has the honest DCP killed — the role that set the template for the Hindi film supervillain of the 1980s.

relationship_to_protagonist: The thief who outsteals Bachchan's Vijay and then joins him
relationship_to_romance: The film's romance for Bachchan's character, between two professionals of the same trade
character_gist: Glamorous jewel thief who lifts the Maharani's necklace before the four con artists can, and is drawn into the mission against Shakaal.

relationship_to_protagonist: Cons Bachchan's Vijay and his brother before joining them
relationship_to_romance: The second romance, attached to Ravi
character_gist: Young woman who plays a debt-ridden heiress named Pushpa to sell the brothers a stolen car, and is recruited into their team once the trick is exposed.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Vijay's sister-in-law, widowed by the villain
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: The DCP's wife, living with him and their young daughter in Mumbai and widowed by Shakaal.

relationship_to_protagonist: Joins Bachchan's Vijay in the mission against Shakaal
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Member of the team assembled to reach Shakaal's island, with a wife, Roma, waiting for him.

relationship_to_protagonist: The film's title character; Bachchan appears only in a cameo as a truck driver
relationship_to_romance: No romance involving Bachchan's cameo; the article carries no plot summary
character_gist: Title role of the film. The Wikipedia article has no plot section, so the part is recorded from the cast list alone and no arc can be described.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's cameo
relationship_to_romance: The article gives no plot, so the role's relation to any romance is unrecorded
character_gist: Leading female role, credited second after Amjad Khan. No plot summary survives in the article to describe the part.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's cameo
relationship_to_romance: Unrecorded; the article has no plot section
character_gist: Police inspector in the film, six years before the television Ramayan that made Arun Govil a household figure.

relationship_to_protagonist: The woman Bachchan's Abhijeet rescues, marries and is separated from
relationship_to_romance: The film's romance, and the target of the villain's final revenge
character_gist: Blind daughter of the tea-estate manager who resists the local racket. Abhijeet saves her from an attempted molestation, marries her, and settles in a village with her awaiting their first child before the villain traces them.

relationship_to_protagonist: The man Bachchan's Abhijeet humiliates repeatedly and finally jails
relationship_to_romance: His assault on Tamosha is what forces Abhijeet to reveal himself
character_gist: Merchant's son running a reign of terror on the tea estate — drinking without paying, beating anyone in his way, carrying off unmarried village girls and burning the houses of parents who resist. He loses to the stranger at every encounter, including a Durga Puja drumming contest.

relationship_to_protagonist: The corrupt power Bachchan's undercover officer is sent to break
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Merchant known as Sahuji who has woven corruption through every layer of the estate — supplying inferior goods, bribing accountants, smuggling across the border, and owning the local police inspector and jeweller.

relationship_to_protagonist: Father of the woman Bachchan's Abhijeet marries
relationship_to_romance: His resistance to the racket is what brings the officer to the estate
character_gist: Estate manager who refuses to pass Sahuji's inflated bills and has the workers turned against him by a paid strike; his blind daughter becomes the officer's wife.

relationship_to_protagonist: The singer Bachchan's Johnny loves and gives up
relationship_to_romance: The film's central romance, renounced for friendship
character_gist: Hotel singer loved by both the waiter Johnny and his wealthy best friend, and revealed at the end to be a daughter of the murdered lottery winner Jaggi.
performance_recognition: Filmfare Award for Best Actress nomination

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Johnny's best friend, and his rival for Asha without knowing it
relationship_to_romance: The friend for whom the hero surrenders the romance
character_gist: Son of the man who framed Johnny's father, educated in England on the stolen lottery money, who loves the same singer his waiter friend does and is targeted for murder by his father's partner.

relationship_to_protagonist: Joins Bachchan's Johnny in a matching act of renunciation
relationship_to_romance: The second sacrifice: she gives up Vicky as Johnny gives up Asha
character_gist: Childhood friend in love with Vicky, who sees her only as a friend; she and Johnny sacrifice their own loves together so that Vicky and Asha can marry.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Johnny's father, presumed dead for twenty years
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Waiter who buys the lottery ticket with three friends, is framed for a murder and thrown off a bridge, survives, and returns undercover — fighting his own son without either recognising the other until a witness intervenes.

relationship_to_protagonist: Employs Bachchan's Johnny as a waiter in the hotel built on his father's ruin
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: One of the two friends who turned on the others over the winning ticket; he photographs his partner committing the murder, builds a hotel on the proceeds, and is killed when that photograph resurfaces.

relationship_to_protagonist: The man who actually committed the murder Bachchan's Johnny's father was framed for
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: The partner who murdered Jaggi and let Namdev take the blame, photographed in the act by his own accomplice, and thrown from a balcony by his elder son.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Johnny's younger brother
relationship_to_romance: His courtship of Asha's sister is the film's junior romance
character_gist: Younger brother in love with Kim, the sister of the singer Johnny loves, and the one who finds the proof of their father's innocence.

relationship_to_protagonist: The film's protagonist; Bachchan appears as himself, alongside Rekha
relationship_to_romance: Carries the film's romance, which his flatmates then wreck
character_gist: Shy, studious Delhi University student who answers the door to a detergent saleswoman his flatmates are hiding from, begins dating her, and breaks it off when their jealous slander poisons him against her.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's appearance as himself
relationship_to_romance: The film's romantic lead, and the target of the two friends' character assassination
character_gist: Neighbour and door-to-door saleswoman who rebuffs the two boisterous flatmates, dates the shy one, is slandered by the pair in revenge, and is then genuinely kidnapped during a staged kidnapping meant to reunite the couple.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's appearance as himself
relationship_to_romance: One of the two friends who destroy the romance and then repair it
character_gist: Boisterous flatmate who fails with Neha, vows revenge when he discovers his friend dating her, assassinates her character, and confesses everything on mistakenly concluding that Siddharth is suicidal.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's appearance as himself
relationship_to_romance: The second of the pair whose jealousy drives the plot
character_gist: The other boisterous flatmate, partner in both the failed courtship and the slander, and co-author of the staged kidnapping that goes wrong.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's appearance as himself
relationship_to_romance: The students' confidant through the whole affair
character_gist: Local paan and cigarette stall owner with a heart of gold, and the three students' perpetual creditor and confidant.

relationship_to_protagonist: Appears as herself in the same guest capacity as Bachchan
relationship_to_romance: Outside the plot
character_gist: Appears as herself alongside Bachchan — the two stars in guest turns in a film whose leads were the emblems of Hindi cinema's parallel middle-class comedy.

relationship_to_protagonist: The woman who loves Bachchan's Heera without knowing his parentage
relationship_to_romance: The film's romance, secondary to the question of the hero's birth
character_gist: Kailashnath's daughter, who falls in love with the factory worker Heera without knowing whose son he is.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Heera's father, who wanted him aborted and finally acknowledges him
relationship_to_romance: His refusal of the mother is the original wrong the film settles
character_gist: Businessman who demanded that his pregnant lover abort the child, lives an unhappy married life believing her dead, meets the grown son without knowing him, and accepts him as his legitimate heir after being wounded in his place.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Heera's mother, who dies at his birth
relationship_to_romance: The abandoned romance that generates the plot
character_gist: Famous singer who refuses to abort her child and leaves her lover, then dies in childbirth; her brother hands the baby to a driver with orders to kill him. A special appearance.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Heera's legitimate half-brother and employer, who plots to kill him
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Ranvir Singh's legitimate son, whose factory underpays its workers; angered by Heera's agitation, he transfers him to a hill estate intending to have him killed, and wounds his own father instead.

relationship_to_protagonist: The drunkard who raised Bachchan's Heera instead of killing him
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Driver ordered to kill the newborn, who keeps and names him instead with a view to making money out of him, and whose drunken taunt about the boy's parentage finally drives Heera out.

relationship_to_protagonist: Figure in the estate world Bachchan's Heera is transferred into
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Supporting role in the household and estate around Ranvir Singh.
performance_recognition: Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actor nomination

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Amit's lover before his marriage and again after it
relationship_to_romance: The affair that is the film's subject
character_gist: Woman Amit loves and means to marry, dropped by letter when duty makes him marry his brother's widow, married herself to a doctor, and drawn back into a secret affair that she finally gives up to return to her husband.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Amit's wife, married out of obligation to his dead brother
relationship_to_romance: The marriage the affair betrays, and the one the film ends by restoring
character_gist: His brother's pregnant fiancée, married by Amit to spare her the stigma of unwed motherhood, who miscarries after a car accident, comes genuinely to love him, and announces she is carrying his child at the wreckage site.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Amit's elder brother, whose death creates the marriage
relationship_to_romance: His death and his unborn child are why the affair has to be an affair
character_gist: Air force squadron leader and Amit's closest relation, engaged to Shobha and killed in the 1971 Indo-Pakistani war before the wedding.

relationship_to_protagonist: Husband of the woman Bachchan's Amit is involved with, and the man he befriends to reach her
relationship_to_romance: The wronged husband, aware and silent
character_gist: Doctor who treats Shobha after the accident and is married to Chandni. Amit cultivates his friendship to get near her; he knows of the infidelity and is devastated by it, and is rescued from his own plane crash by Amit.

relationship_to_protagonist: The policeman investigating the accident Bachchan's Amit causes
relationship_to_romance: The threat of exposure hanging over the affair
character_gist: Police officer investigating the pedestrian Amit and Chandni injure on their way back from a tryst, and Shobha's protective cousin, who intends to expose him. A guest appearance.

relationship_to_protagonist: The film's title character; Bachchan's Jagga is a special appearance
relationship_to_romance: No romance involving Bachchan's role; the article carries no plot summary
character_gist: Title role of this Punjabi film. The Wikipedia article has no plot section, so the part is recorded from the cast list alone.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection recorded to Bachchan's special appearance
relationship_to_romance: Unrecorded; the article gives no plot
character_gist: Leading female role, credited second. No plot summary survives in the article to describe the part.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection recorded to Bachchan's special appearance
relationship_to_romance: Unrecorded; the article gives no plot
character_gist: Supporting role in the Punjabi film, credited third in the cast list.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Kishan's childhood friend, who makes him a singer and is then rescued by him
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance; the friendship, not the courtship, is the film's subject
character_gist: Affluent friend who discovers Kishan's voice and mortgages what is left of his looted family wealth to launch him, is kidnapped and tortured into a false confession by his own uncle and cousin, and loses his memory in an asylum until Kishan feeds him rotis as he did in childhood.
performance_recognition: Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actor

relationship_to_protagonist: Hired to groom Bachchan's Kishan, and the woman who declares her love for him
relationship_to_romance: The film's romance, which grows out of the grooming she is paid for
character_gist: Woman engaged by Bishan to turn a village singer into a performer and a gentleman, who endures his deliberate disruption and professes her love once he becomes a star.

relationship_to_protagonist: Wife of Bachchan's Kishan's friend, convinced he will betray her husband
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance; her mistrust tests the friendship instead
character_gist: Bishan's wife, certain that Kishan will turn his back on her husband once he succeeds, and reconciled with Bishan only when Kishan's earnings clear the mortgages.

relationship_to_protagonist: Separated Bachchan's Kishan from his friend in childhood and engineers the kidnapping
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Maternal uncle with designs on his widowed sister's wealth, who breaks up the boys' friendship by sending Bishan abroad, loots the family fortune over eighteen years, and has him confined to an asylum.

relationship_to_protagonist: The cousin working with the uncle against Bachchan's Kishan and his friend
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: The uncle's son and partner in the looting of the family wealth and the trap set for Bishan.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Kallu's partner after prison, and the jailer's stolen daughter
relationship_to_romance: The film's romance, resolved through the revelation of her parentage
character_gist: Woman who pairs up with Kaalia in his campaign against Shahani, and is revealed to be the daughter the jailer Raghuvir Singh lost to a kidnapping twenty years earlier.

relationship_to_protagonist: The mill owner whose refusal kills Bachchan's Kallu's brother, and the target of his revenge
relationship_to_romance: Kidnaps the niece and coerces the family, which is what sets the trial in motion
character_gist: Mill owner who refuses money for the treatment of a maimed worker, has Kallu jailed for the theft that came too late, smuggles gold through his mill, and kidnaps Kallu's niece to force false testimony. He ends the film with his own arm chopped off.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Kaalia's jailer, then his ally once he learns the truth
relationship_to_romance: His lost daughter turns out to be the woman at Kaalia's side
character_gist: Upright jailer whose own daughter was kidnapped as a child by a prisoner. He first pursues the escaped Kaalia and then joins him, and learns at the villain's own confession that Shalini is his daughter.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Kallu's elder brother, whose death turns him criminal
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Mill worker who loses both arms in an accident at work, is refused help by his employer, and dies before his brother's desperate burglary can pay for treatment.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Kallu's sister-in-law, coerced into testifying against him
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Widow of the maimed mill worker, told by Kaalia's accomplices that he is in America earning for her, and finally forced by the kidnapping of her daughter to testify against him at a murder trial.

relationship_to_protagonist: The nurse Bachchan's Ravi tricks into marriage, and the civilising force on the household
relationship_to_romance: The film's central romance, courted under a deception about the size of the family
character_gist: Hospital nurse repelled by Ravi's manners until he grooms himself and passes off his six brothers as one; she discovers the truth after the wedding, stays at their request, and sets about civilising all seven.

relationship_to_protagonist: The heiress Bachchan's second role, the killer Babu, is hired to murder
relationship_to_romance: The love interest of Bachchan's criminal double, the film's second pairing
character_gist: Wealthy paraplegic heiress in the care of six sisters, whose uncle wants her dead for the ancestral property and hires a released prisoner who happens to be Ravi's double.

relationship_to_protagonist: Discovers that the hired killer is Bachchan's double and exploits the resemblance
relationship_to_romance: Threatens both of the film's couples
character_gist: Seema's uncle, who plots her murder for the property, has the convict Babu released to do it, and seizes on the discovery that Babu is the exact double of the farmer Ravi.

relationship_to_protagonist: The youngest brother Bachchan's Ravi always defends
relationship_to_romance: Helps run the deception that wins Indu, and has a romance of his own among the six sisters
character_gist: Youngest of the seven brothers, protected by Ravi from the other five, and his accomplice in passing the family off as a household of two.

relationship_to_protagonist: One of Bachchan's Ravi's six younger brothers
relationship_to_romance: One of the six brothers paired off with the six sisters
character_gist: The second of the uncouth younger brothers on the farmhouse, among those Indu sets out to civilise and who fall for Seema's six caretakers.

relationship_to_protagonist: The woman Bachchan's Sudhir loves and deliberately hands to his friend
relationship_to_romance: The film's romance, refused rather than pursued
character_gist: Woman both doctors meet on holiday, whom Sudhir recommends to his friend rather than marry himself, and who is told a story of madness and crime as the reason. She welcomes him out of prison nine years later with her husband and son.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Sudhir's foster brother, for whom he gives up both the woman and his career
relationship_to_romance: Marries the woman his friend loved, without knowing it
character_gist: The magistrate's son, raised alongside Sudhir and given the same education, who marries Kavita, returns from America charging patients heavily and performing illegal abortions, and is saved from prison when Sudhir falsifies the records and takes the sentence.
performance_recognition: Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actor nomination

relationship_to_protagonist: The magistrate who adopts Bachchan's Sudhir instead of sentencing him
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Magistrate who recognises the boy brought before him for petty theft, adopts him, and raises him alongside his own son as a doctor.

relationship_to_protagonist: Comic presence in Bachchan's Sudhir's professional world
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Comic figure around the two doctors' practice.

relationship_to_protagonist: The romance of Bachchan's second role, the son Raju
relationship_to_romance: The film's romance, attached to the younger of Bachchan's two roles
character_gist: Young woman in the slum world of Bharat Nagar, paired with Master Dinanath's son Raju while he works for the man who destroyed his own family.

relationship_to_protagonist: Wife of Bachchan's Master Dinanath, lost to him for fifteen years
relationship_to_romance: An established marriage severed by the villain, not a courtship
character_gist: Wife kidnapped in reprisal for her husband's honesty, who contracts leprosy, escapes her captor leaving her daughter with a friend, and is believed dead when her necklace is found by a railway line.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Master Dinanath's daughter, separated from him as a child
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Daughter kidnapped with her mother and left in a friend's care, grown into a doctor, and among those her father believes dead.

relationship_to_protagonist: The landlord Bachchan's Master Dinanath jails, who destroys his family in return
relationship_to_romance: Destroys the marriage by having the wife abducted
character_gist: Former British-era landlord turned arms smuggler, jailed on Master Dinanath's evidence, who has his wife and daughter kidnapped, turns the villagers against him as a traitor, and later employs his son without either knowing it.

relationship_to_protagonist: Carries out the abduction of Bachchan's Master Dinanath's family
relationship_to_romance: The instrument of the family's separation
character_gist: The Thakur's partner in crime, who kidnaps the schoolmaster's wife and daughter and holds them until she escapes.

relationship_to_protagonist: One of the four slum dons Bachchan's Master Dinanath reconciles
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: One of four dons ruling the Punjabi, Tamil, Bengali and Muslim quarters of Bharat Nagar, brought to peace by the schoolmaster and then using that peace as cover for their own rackets.

relationship_to_protagonist: The heir Bachchan's Arjun protects, and the son his mother raised in his place
relationship_to_romance: His romance with the hired dancer Nisha runs beside Arjun's with Poonam
character_gist: Hotel owner raised as Savitri's son after his father's murder, who comes to suspect her of the crime, is targeted by his manager, and falls for the dancer sent to kill him.
performance_recognition: Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actor nomination

relationship_to_protagonist: The woman Bachchan's Arjun meets and marries in the city
relationship_to_romance: The film's romance for Bachchan's character, secondary to the plot of protection and revenge
character_gist: Young woman Arjun meets while working as a bellboy at the five-star hotel, and marries at the end alongside Raja's wedding to Nisha.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Arjun's mother, who gave him up to raise another woman's son
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance; the mother's sacrifice is the film's emotional core
character_gist: Widow who promises her dying husband to protect the orphaned heir, hands her own son to his grandfather and passes herself off as Raja's mother, and is blamed by everyone — including her employer's son — for murders she did not commit.

relationship_to_protagonist: Hired to kill the man Bachchan's Arjun is sworn to protect
relationship_to_romance: The second romance: the assassin who falls for her target
character_gist: Dancer hired by the hotel manager to murder Raja, who falls in love with him instead, arranges a boat party to carry out the plan and cannot go through with it.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Arjun's grandfather, who raised him in the village
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Father of the murdered bodyguard, who believes his daughter-in-law killed her husband for money and raises her son himself, keeping him naive of the whole history.

relationship_to_protagonist: The hotel manager Bachchan's Arjun works under and finally exposes
relationship_to_romance: Sends the dancer who becomes the second romance
character_gist: Hotel manager and son of the man who murdered Raja's father, plotting Raja's death, framing Savitri, and finally kidnapping the family to force a transfer of the property into his name.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Govind's much older half-brother, and the judge at his murder trial
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Half-brother who raised the two boys and left to finish his law degree, becoming a leading lawyer and then the judge trying Govind for murder — who steps down from the bench to defend him once he learns who the accused is.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Govind's romance in his taxi-driving life
relationship_to_romance: A minor romance beside the family drama — the film scores 2 for romance centrality
character_gist: Young woman attached to the taxi driver Chhotu Ustaad in the Bombay world he builds after leaving home.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Govind's younger brother, whose education he drives a taxi to pay for
relationship_to_romance: His marriage into money is a transaction rather than a romance
character_gist: Ambitious younger brother who spurns the taxi driver's pride, marries a rich man's daughter and lives in her house, and is used by her uncle to run drugs through the family transport company.

relationship_to_protagonist: The sister-in-law whose cruelty drives Bachchan's Govind out of the house
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Newly married wife of the half-brother, jealous of his affection for the two boys, whose ill treatment in his absence sends them to Bombay.

relationship_to_protagonist: Frames Bachchan's Govind for the murder he commits himself
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Seth Verma's brother, who arranges the younger brother's marriage, uses him to smuggle drugs in the company's vehicles, murders Verma, and leaves Govind to be found at the scene.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Govind's friend in the Bombay streets
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Banana seller and friend of the taxi driver — Mehmood again in a Bachchan film, a decade after giving him his first lead in Bombay to Goa.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Vijay's father, whose refusal to trade the law for his son defines the film
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance; the father-son rupture is the film's subject
character_gist: Incorruptible police commissioner who tells a kidnapper on a tapped phone that he will not betray the law even if his only son dies — words the boy hears played back, and never forgives.
performance_recognition: Filmfare Award for Best Actor

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Vijay's mother, standing between her husband's principles and her son's estrangement
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Wife and mother caught between the two men, unable to reconcile a husband who would let their son die for the law and a son who cannot forgive him for saying so.
performance_recognition: Filmfare Award for Best Actress nomination

relationship_to_protagonist: The woman Bachchan's Vijay rescues and marries
relationship_to_romance: The film's romance, secondary to the father-son conflict
character_gist: Young woman Vijay saves from four men who try to molest her, who becomes his wife and the mother of the grandson to whom the whole story is being told.

relationship_to_protagonist: Kidnapped Bachchan's Vijay as a child and caused the breach with his father
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Gangster who abducts the commissioner's son to trade for a jailed henchman, tapes the father's refusal, and plays it to the boy — the act that shapes the rest of Vijay's life.

relationship_to_protagonist: Saved Bachchan's Vijay as a child and later employs him
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Gangster in the rival's outfit who pities the kidnapped boy and helps him escape, becomes J. K.'s sworn enemy for it, and years later hires the grown Vijay on sight.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Vijay's son, to whom the whole story is narrated
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Grandson returning from his B.A. exams wanting to join the police like his grandfather, whose question opens the film and prompts the flashback that is its body. A guest appearance.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Shankar's partner in the city
relationship_to_romance: Romance is only implied here, which is why the film carries no pairing record
character_gist: One of the pair Shankar joins forces with in the city after fleeing his village as a thief; the article establishes the association but not a developed romance.

relationship_to_protagonist: Murdered Bachchan's Shankar's father and burned his mother and sister
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Man who kills the village temple priest and sets fire to his house, is blinded rather than killed by the priest's son, and remains the object of Shankar's atheism and revenge.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Shankar's associate in the city, who saves his sister
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Companion in Shankar's city life as a thief, who rescues his sister Shanti from Tiger's men when she goes out for their mother's medicine.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Shankar's mother, whom he believed burned to death
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Mother thought killed in the fire, found alive years later when her fugitive son hides in her house — the discovery that makes him give up stealing.

relationship_to_protagonist: Sister of the man who destroyed Bachchan's Shankar's family
relationship_to_romance: Outside the film's implied romance
character_gist: Tiger's sister, on the other side of the vendetta that drives the film.

relationship_to_protagonist: The film's avenger, whom Bachchan's Jaan Nisar Khan joins after his release from prison
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance; his cause is vengeance, not courtship
character_gist: Man set on killing the three men who traumatised and killed members of his family, refusing the law his sister serves, who takes up with the embittered ex-convict Khan when their vendettas prove to overlap.

relationship_to_protagonist: The lawful counterpart to the revenge Bachchan's Khan and her brother pursue
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Sister who joined the police specifically to take revenge on the same three men through lawful means, and so stands against her brother's method while sharing his cause.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Jaan Nisar Khan's wife, destroyed by his imprisonment
relationship_to_romance: A marriage ended offscreen by rape and suicide — the film's darkest relationship
character_gist: Wife of the forest officer, who is raped after he is sentenced to twenty years for a killing he did not commit, and who kills herself and their daughter Neelu. An extended special appearance.

relationship_to_protagonist: The poacher Bachchan's Khan was jailed for killing, and who turns out to be alive
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Sandalwood poacher whose apparent death in a struggle sent the forest officer to prison for twenty years, and whose survival Khan discovers after his release.

relationship_to_protagonist: One of the three men the film's avengers pursue
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: One of the trio responsible for the destruction of Vijay and Durga's family, hunted by brother and sister through opposite methods.

relationship_to_protagonist: A guest turn alongside Bachchan's own extended special appearance
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Cameo as a truck driver — the same kind of walk-on Bachchan himself had taken in Commander two years earlier.

relationship_to_protagonist: Wife of Bachchan's Amit, who believes him dead and raises one of their twins alone
relationship_to_romance: An established marriage severed by the plot rather than a courtship, which is why the film has no pairing record for it
character_gist: Pregnant wife left behind when her husband goes on the run, who gives birth to twins, loses one to a barren couple, and raises the other alone believing herself widowed.

relationship_to_protagonist: Attached to Guru, the theatre actor among Bachchan's three roles
relationship_to_romance: One of the film's two romances, pursued by her rather than by him
character_gist: Woman who pursues the theatre actor Guru, the twin raised by the couple who stole him.

relationship_to_protagonist: Adopted daughter of Bachchan's Rana Ranveer, in love with his own lost son
relationship_to_romance: The second romance, and the thread that finally reunites the family
character_gist: Adopted daughter of the fugitive living as Rana Ranveer, who falls in love with the police inspector Shankar without either of them knowing he is her guardian's son.

relationship_to_protagonist: Framed Bachchan's Amit for murder and scattered his family
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Man framed for drug possession who kills the associate he blames and pins it on his own lawyer, driving Amit into hiding and his family into three separate lives.

relationship_to_protagonist: Figure in the world Bachchan's fugitive lawyer rebuilds his life within
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Senior figure in the film's social world, among those around the family as its three strands converge.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Ronnie's girlfriend through his years as a criminal
relationship_to_romance: Recorded as Minor with no pairing record: the article establishes the attachment but not its development
character_gist: Glamorous companion of the criminal Ronnie in Portuguese Goa, present through his betrayals of the independence movement and his change of heart.

relationship_to_protagonist: The young rebel Bachchan's Ronnie resents and finally sets out to save
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Young revolutionary who steals Ronnie's gold, frees a captured rebel and assassinates the Portuguese police chief; sentenced to death, his heroism shames the man whose parents' shelter once saved Ronnie's life.

relationship_to_protagonist: The revolutionary Bachchan's Ramdas wrongly believes murdered his father
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Separatist leader who ends his mortally wounded comrade's life at the man's own begging, is seen doing it by the dead man's young son, and is betrayed to the police by that son twenty years later — the second betrayal killing him.

relationship_to_protagonist: The colonial police inspector whose favour Bachchan's Ronnie courts
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Portuguese police inspector to whom Ronnie betrays the independence fighters, twice.

relationship_to_protagonist: Belongs to the young rebel's side of the story
relationship_to_romance: Attached to Shekhar rather than to Bachchan's Ronnie
character_gist: Young woman in the circle around the rebel Shekhar, daughter of the Kamats.

relationship_to_protagonist: Raised by the woman who is Bachchan's Iqbal's mother, and his ally against her captor
relationship_to_romance: His romance with Deepa runs beside Iqbal's with Julie
character_gist: Infant adopted from a Kanpur orphanage for the amnesiac Salma to raise, grown into a young reporter covering the coolies' strike, who threatens to publish Zafar's crimes and becomes Iqbal's friend.

relationship_to_protagonist: The woman Bachchan's Iqbal loves
relationship_to_romance: The film's romance for Bachchan's character, secondary to the recovery of his mother
character_gist: Christian girl whom the coolie Iqbal falls in love with, and daughter of the man John D'Costa.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Iqbal's mother, who cannot recognise him
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Woman separated from her young son in the flood engineered by her rejected suitor, held by him as his wife, and given electric shocks by a psychiatrist so that her memory will never return.

relationship_to_protagonist: Took Bachchan's Iqbal's mother and engineered the flood that separated them
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Wealthy man refused by Salma and her father, who murders the father on his release from prison, floods the region to destroy her marriage, abducts her, and passes her off to the world as his wife.

relationship_to_protagonist: Father of the woman Bachchan's Iqbal loves
relationship_to_romance: Stands on the family side of the romance
character_gist: Julie's father, in the Christian community around the railway station where the coolies work.

relationship_to_protagonist: One of the men Bachchan's Iqbal fights
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Henchman in Zafar Khan's employ, opposite whom Bachchan plays one of the film's fight sequences.

relationship_to_protagonist: The film's protagonist; Bachchan's Nahar Singh is a special appearance
relationship_to_romance: Carries the film's romance and marriage with the paan seller Lali
character_gist: Upright stick fighter devoted to his Thakur, who asks for eleven years of unpaid wages and is told to send his wife instead; he attacks the Thakur, is jailed on fabricated charges, and learns in prison that he is to be a father.

relationship_to_protagonist: No recorded connection to Bachchan's special appearance
relationship_to_romance: The film's romantic lead, and the object of the landlord's predatory demand
character_gist: Paan vendor who marries Bhola, is demanded by the Thakur in lieu of wages, and is slandered with rumours of an illicit affair while her husband is in prison.

relationship_to_protagonist: No recorded connection to Bachchan's special appearance
relationship_to_romance: The predatory force against the film's marriage
character_gist: Landlord who withholds eleven years of wages, demands his servant's wife as settlement, has him imprisoned on fabricated charges, and spreads rumours about her from a distance.

relationship_to_protagonist: A special appearance alongside Bachchan's own in this Bhojpuri film
relationship_to_romance: Outside the plot
character_gist: Appears as herself in a special appearance, paired with Bachchan's guest turn as Nahar Singh.

relationship_to_protagonist: The woman Bachchan's Amar marries, and the daughter of the man corrupting him
relationship_to_romance: The film's romance, broken by her misreading of his corruption and restored when she learns the truth
character_gist: Only daughter of the businessman Seetharam, who marries Amar after her father is won over, leaves him with their newborn when she misunderstands his crimes, and reconciles once she learns he was blackmailed.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Amar's father-in-law, and one of the syndicate that owns him
relationship_to_romance: His criminality is what destroys the marriage
character_gist: Wealthy businessman who accepts Amar as a son-in-law and is revealed to be part of the criminal network, ordering him to retrieve diamonds from an international smuggler; he dies in the cabinet-room massacre.

relationship_to_protagonist: The politician who makes Bachchan's Amar a policeman and then a pawn
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Politician promising an end to corruption, stoned by a crowd and rescued by Amar, who trains him for the police and later reveals himself as head of the syndicate that has manipulated him throughout.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Amar's mother
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Mother of the unemployed graduate who will not compromise his morals for a job, in the household the film opens with.

relationship_to_protagonist: Member of the syndicate Bachchan's Amar finally massacres
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: One of the criminal network's men, among the cabinet of syndicate members Amar guns down at the film's climax.

relationship_to_protagonist: The dancer Bachchan's Vicky loves, and the reason his father disowns him
relationship_to_romance: The film's romance, and the occasion of the final break with the father
character_gist: Professional dancer and daughter of a poor blind man, loved by the alcoholic heir. Her agent robs her of Vicky's gifts and finally kidnaps her; the father's insult that no poor girl would marry him is what breaks the household.
performance_recognition: Filmfare Award for Best Actress nomination

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Vicky's father, whose neglect made him an alcoholic
relationship_to_romance: Opposes the marriage and disowns his son over it
character_gist: Billionaire industrialist with no time for his son, who did not visit his dying wife, blames the caretaker for the boy's drinking, and disowns Vicky over a woman and a framed scandal — refusing even to attend the caretaker's last rites.

relationship_to_protagonist: The caretaker who raised Bachchan's Vicky in his father's place
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: His father's friend and the boy's real guardian, entrusted with him by his dying mother, who stays when Vicky is disowned, goes out to find work so the two can eat, and is killed in an accident.

relationship_to_protagonist: Frames Bachchan's Vicky and kidnaps the woman he loves
relationship_to_romance: The direct threat to the romance
character_gist: Meena's greedy agent, who harasses her and her blind father, steals the gifts Vicky gives her, frames Vicky with another woman to turn his father against him, and kidnaps her.

relationship_to_protagonist: The orphan Bachchan's Vicky secretly raised, grown into a policeman
relationship_to_romance: Shelters the woman Vicky loves once she is rescued
character_gist: Orphan whose schooling Vicky quietly paid for through the principal and the caretaker, now a police inspector who learns who his secret benefactor was, rescues Meena, and takes them both in.

relationship_to_protagonist: A guest appearance in a song with Bachchan's Vicky
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Guest appearance in the song 'Jahan Chaar Yaar Mil Jaye'.

relationship_to_protagonist: The film's protagonist; Bachchan appears in a cameo as himself
relationship_to_romance: No romance involving Bachchan's cameo
character_gist: Factory worker paid insufficient wages who calls a strike and is entrapped on false charges and arrested — the whole of the plot the article records.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's cameo as himself
relationship_to_romance: The article's plot summary is a single sentence and does not describe the romance
character_gist: Top-billed lead of the film. The Wikipedia article's plot section covers only the factory worker's arrest, so the role cannot be described further.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's cameo as himself
relationship_to_romance: Unrecorded; the article's plot is one sentence long
character_gist: Leading female role, credited second. The surviving plot summary does not reach her part.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's cameo as himself
relationship_to_romance: Outside any romance
character_gist: Third-billed role in the film; the article's plot summary does not describe it.

relationship_to_protagonist: The film's protagonist; Bachchan contributes narration only
relationship_to_romance: Carries both sides of the film's love triangle
character_gist: Landless Jat peasant's son, rebellious against caste prejudice from his schooldays, who returns for his father's funeral, refuses to repay the landlord's loan on principle, and ignites a class revolt.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: The woman the protagonist marries, and the reason the triangle resolves as it does
character_gist: Childhood friend whom the landlord's sons attempt to rape; Ranjit rescues her and marries her because she plainly needs a protector.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: The unrequited half of the triangle, carried into a marriage she did not choose
character_gist: The landlord's daughter, sympathetic to Ranjit since school and deeply impressed when he confronts her father, who marries the police officer her father selects and carries her unrequited love into that marriage — as her husband soon discovers.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: On the side of the family opposing both of the film's couples
character_gist: One of the Rajput landlord's sons who bullied Ranjit at school and whose family's grip on the village land the film sets him against.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Ally in the revolt against the zamindar family in the Rajasthan village where the film is set.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Police havaldar in the village, in a performance the film's article records as its only acting nomination.
performance_recognition: Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actor nomination

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Karan's younger brother, raised apart from him
relationship_to_romance: His romance with the struggling actress Lucy is the film's main courtship
character_gist: Struggling actor raised by their mother after the elder boy's supposed death, in love with a fellow struggler whose father drinks her earnings, and drawn into the family's old enmity with Vidyanath and Ranjit.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Karan's mother, who drove him from the house believing he killed his father
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Widow who beats her small son and tells him to go away after he pulls the lever that kills his policeman father, then spends years broken by his apparent suicide, saying she never meant such a punishment.

relationship_to_protagonist: The boy who saved Bachchan's Karan from drowning and became his brother in all but blood
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
