character_gist: Boy who pulls the drowning Karan from the sea and brings him home to a new mother, growing up as his closest friend — the film's example of brotherhood across faiths. A guest appearance.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Karan's fellow officer and romantic interest
relationship_to_romance: The film's romance for Bachchan's character, minor beside the family plot
character_gist: Police inspector and daughter of the commissioner, working alongside Karan.

relationship_to_protagonist: Caused the death of Bachchan's Karan's father and blamed the child for it
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Drug dealer who, with Ranjit Saxena, tries to kill the arresting inspector on machinery, then accuses the man's small son of the killing — the lie that scatters the family for twenty years.

relationship_to_protagonist: Sister of the criminal Bachchan's Karan's family is set against
relationship_to_romance: Adjacent to the younger brother's romance
character_gist: Arrogant young woman who runs her car into the actress Lucy, is jailed by Kishen when the officer refuses her brother's bribe, and is courted by Vidyanath's lisping son.

relationship_to_protagonist: The woman Bachchan's Raju falls in love with, and the daughter of the man who betrayed his father
relationship_to_romance: The film's romance, running across the divide between the hero and the collaborator's household
character_gist: Daughter of the collaborating doctor Harry, confronted by the tanga driver Raju over her reckless behaviour and falling in love with him, and reunited with him and his parents at the end.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Raju's father, who branded him 'mard' at birth
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Ruler who stops British soldiers plundering an Indian fort and marks his newborn son with the word mard, then is sedated by a doctor in British pay, captured and held prisoner for twenty years until his son fights him in a staged gladiatorial bout.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Raju's mother, separated from him in infancy
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Queen who escapes the raid and is shot, loses her speech, and lives as a washerwoman while her infant son, carried away by the family horse, is raised by a blacksmith.

relationship_to_protagonist: Betrayed Bachchan's Raju's father, and is the father of the woman he loves
relationship_to_romance: His household is the one the romance has to cross into
character_gist: Local doctor who sedates Raja Azad Singh for the British, is made mayor for the betrayal, demolishes a slum, and tries to bribe and then kill the tanga driver who resists him.

relationship_to_protagonist: The colonial authority Bachchan's Raju is set against
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: British general who conspires with the mayor to capture the Raja, and whose son runs the blood camps and slave labour at the film's centre.

relationship_to_protagonist: Kills Bachchan's Raju's adoptive parents and stages the fight with his real father
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: The general's son, running blood camps, slave labour and the imprisonment of the Raja, who captures Raju and pits him against his own father without either knowing the other.

relationship_to_protagonist: Wife of Bachchan's David, whose rape and suicide drive the film
relationship_to_romance: The marriage destroyed in the first act, and the reason for everything after it
character_gist: Pregnant wife who names her son with the blessings of the politician her husband worships, and is raped by him; her suicide note is the only evidence, and it is taken from David and burned.

relationship_to_protagonist: The romance of Bachchan's second role, the policeman son Vijay
relationship_to_romance: The film's living romance, attached to the son rather than the father
character_gist: Daughter of DIG Bhatnagar and the police officer Vijay's love. The cast list records that her voice was dubbed by Rekha.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's David's best friend, entrusted with his son and defying his instructions
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Bootlegger friend asked to raise David's son as a fearsome criminal, who instead renames the boy Vijay, raises him as his own son and makes him a police officer — and has become wealthy and respectable by the time David is released.

relationship_to_protagonist: The politician Bachchan's David worshipped, and who raped his wife
relationship_to_romance: Destroys the marriage that opens the film
character_gist: Member of Parliament whom David revered enough to die for, who blesses the naming of his son and rapes his wife, then lets him serve twenty-four years for her death.

relationship_to_protagonist: The officer who double-crossed Bachchan's David and took the evidence from him
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Police inspector allied to Chaturvedi, who intercepts David on his way to confront the politician and manipulates the suicide note out of his hands.

relationship_to_protagonist: Destroyed the only proof of the crime against Bachchan's David
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Doctor in Chaturvedi's circle who burns Mary's handwritten note while the three men laugh at David, and lies in court to have him convicted.

relationship_to_protagonist: The film's protagonist; Bachchan appears as himself in a guest turn
relationship_to_romance: Carries the film's romance with Jojo alongside the drug-war plot
character_gist: CID inspector who joined the police after his younger brother died of an overdose, sees his friend killed in front of him, is blocked from the case and goes to Goa alone, where he has no powers and ends up on the run from police and goons alike.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's guest appearance
relationship_to_romance: The film's romantic lead and the hero's only ally in Goa
character_gist: Young woman who helps Kapil try to uncover Albert's death while the local police treat him as a nuisance.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's guest appearance
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Friend from Goa killed in front of Kapil, the death he vows to avenge and is forbidden to investigate.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's guest appearance
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Figure in the Goa drug trade the inspector is trying to break without any authority to do it.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection recorded to Bachchan's guest appearance as himself
relationship_to_romance: Unrecorded; the article has no plot section
character_gist: Top-billed performer. The Wikipedia article carries no plot summary and its cast list gives no character names, so the role cannot be described. Released in October 1987, the month of Kishore Kumar's death.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection recorded to Bachchan's guest appearance
relationship_to_romance: Unrecorded; the article has no plot section
character_gist: Credited second in the cast list. No plot summary or character names survive in the article.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection recorded to Bachchan's guest appearance
relationship_to_romance: Unrecorded; the article has no plot section
character_gist: Credited among the principals. The article gives no character names, and the antagonist function is inferred only from his standing casting of the period — recorded at low confidence.

relationship_to_protagonist: The woman Bachchan's Vijay loves, and the daughter of the dancer who framed his father
relationship_to_romance: The film's romance, entangled with the revenge plot through her mother
character_gist: Small-time trickster living in a slum with her ailing mother Julie, who infiltrates J. K.'s circle as an exotic dancer to kill him, shoots him and finds he is wearing a bulletproof vest.

relationship_to_protagonist: Framed Bachchan's Vijay's father and later puts Vijay himself on his payroll
relationship_to_romance: Ordered the killing of the woman who becomes his lover's mother
character_gist: Crime baron who orchestrates a bank robbery to bail out a corrupt manager, frames the DCP investigating it, and later buys the dead man's son — not knowing that the son is also the masked Shahenshah dismantling his empire.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Vijay's father, whose suicide he avenges
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Honest DCP framed for corruption using a dancer and a staged robbery, imprisoned for three months by the CBI, and driven to hang himself after release — leaving the noose his son keeps.

relationship_to_protagonist: Takes in Bachchan's Vijay and his mother after the suicide
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Honest inspector and friend of the dead DCP, who houses the widow and her son; his daughter Shaheena grows up alongside Vijay and is widowed when J. K. kills her journalist husband.

relationship_to_protagonist: The dancer whose false evidence destroyed Bachchan's Vijay's father
relationship_to_romance: Mother of the woman he loves — the romance and the revenge share one person
character_gist: Exotic dancer hired to frame the DCP, marked for assassination by J. K. afterwards and on the run ever since, living ailing in a slum with her daughter, and finally agreeing to testify.

relationship_to_protagonist: The corruption whose cover-up destroyed Bachchan's Vijay's father
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Bank manager who illegally lends ₹2.5 million to the crime baron and is bailed out by a staged robbery — the crime the DCP was about to solve when he was framed.

relationship_to_protagonist: The film's protagonist; Bachchan appears as a police inspector in a special appearance
relationship_to_romance: The trap set for him uses a dancer, but the film gives him no romance of his own
character_gist: Timber merchant who wants to give his wealth away to humanity and is exploited for his innocence, pursued by an identical step brother claiming half his inheritance and by smugglers after the necklace meant for his bride. Jagdeep directed the film, spun off from his own Sholay character.

relationship_to_protagonist: A special appearance alongside Bachchan's own
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Appears both as a character and as himself — one of several stars, Bachchan included, lending guest turns to the directorial debut of their Sholay co-star.

relationship_to_protagonist: A guest turn in the same film as Bachchan's special appearance
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Cameo as a drunk woman, one of the film's many star walk-ons.

relationship_to_protagonist: Another of the film's star guest appearances
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Cameo as a qawwali singer in the film's guest-studded musical sequences.

relationship_to_protagonist: The film's protagonist; Bachchan is one of many stars in an uncredited-scale cameo
relationship_to_romance: Carries the film's romance from rescue to marriage to caregiving
character_gist: Ambitious young actress whose life is saved by her co-star during a stunt, who defies her sister to marry him, attempts suicide during a desperate search for him, and becomes his carer when an accident leaves him paralysed.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's cameo
relationship_to_romance: The male half of the film's romance
character_gist: Film star who saves his co-star during a high-risk stunt, marries her against her family's wishes, and is left paralysed by an accident.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's cameo
relationship_to_romance: The external opposition to the romance, later withdrawn
character_gist: Protective elder sister who vehemently disapproves of the romance, is defied and run away from, and finally accepts the couple and allows the marriage.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's cameo
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Film director in the industry setting where the stunt accident and the romance both take place.

relationship_to_protagonist: The film's protagonist; Bachchan appears as himself in a special appearance
relationship_to_romance: Carries the film's entire romance, to the point of staging his own death for it
character_gist: Hyderabadi auto-rickshaw driver who becomes a starlet's tour guide and falls in love, follows her to Bombay, is rejected under family pressure, and is talked into dying publicly like a great lover in a staged spectacle.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's special appearance
relationship_to_romance: The film's romantic lead, forced to choose between career and love
character_gist: Upcoming film starlet who falls in love with her tour guide, is pressed by her family to reject him for her career, and arrives at the last moment to stop his public suicide.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's special appearance
relationship_to_romance: Turns the hero's despair into the spectacle that resolves the romance
character_gist: Show lady who saves the suicidal Hiralal and then arranges for him to die like a great lover in what she bills as the greatest show on earth.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's special appearance
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Supporting figure in the Hyderabad and Bombay world through which the rickshaw driver pursues his starlet.

relationship_to_protagonist: The woman Bachchan's Ganga shelters, marries and loses to amnesia
relationship_to_romance: The first of the film's two romances, and the one it is built to restore
character_gist: Young woman who jumps into Ganga's truck fleeing a goon, passes as his wife at a lodge, and after a bridge explosion falls into the river, loses her memory and is taken in by the singer who recognises her from a qawwali performance.

relationship_to_protagonist: The woman who raises Bachchan's Ganga's son and falls in love with him
relationship_to_romance: The second romance, created by the first one's collapse
character_gist: Woman who takes care of Ganga's son after Jamuna is lost, falls in love with him, and is one of the two people who eventually bring him and his wife back together.

relationship_to_protagonist: Shelters and loves the amnesiac wife of Bachchan's Ganga
relationship_to_romance: The rival claim on Jamuna, resolved in Ganga's favour
character_gist: Qawwali singer who recognises the memory-less Jamuna from a performance she once gave, takes her in and falls in love with her, and finally helps reunite her with her husband.

relationship_to_protagonist: The uncle whose theft of the family property Bachchan's Ganga is sworn to avenge
relationship_to_romance: His men cause the explosion that separates the couple
character_gist: Greedy landlord who kills his brother-in-law, tricks his sister into signing away her property, has Ganga jailed for two years, and sends men to kill him — the attempt that costs Jamuna her memory.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Ganga's mother, whose dispossession is his grievance
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Widow tricked by her own brother into signing away her husband's property, whose wrong her son takes a pledge to avenge.

relationship_to_protagonist: The film's protagonist; Bachchan contributes narration only
relationship_to_romance: His marriage to the orphaned Jinna is the film's romance
character_gist: Village policeman whose famous friendship with a landlord's son ends when that friend turns bandit and burns the farmers' homes; he marries Jina, orphaned by those killings, and declares the friendship over.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance; his vendetta is what destroys it
character_gist: Landlord's son who cannot bear his brother's lynching, kills many farmers and burns their homes, and escapes to the ravines to lead a bandit gang funded and protected by his own family.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: The film's romance, contracted out of the violence rather than despite it
character_gist: Woman orphaned when her brother is killed by the bandit, married immediately afterwards by the policeman who was the bandit's closest friend.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Patriarch who cannot accept the land-ceiling law, backs his eldest son's plan to back-date transfers, and urges his policeman son to shield the bandit and punish the villagers.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Eldest son who schemes to evade the land ceiling by back-dating transfers, panics at a farmers' meeting and shoots a villager dead, and is lynched by the mob.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Police officer whom the Thakur invites to suppress the farmers' rebellion, and who says his hands are tied by his own superior — the Thakur's younger son.

relationship_to_protagonist: Paired with one of Bachchan's two roles
relationship_to_romance: Recorded as Minor with no pairing record: the article's plot is two sentences and describes no relationship
character_gist: Leading female role, daughter of the tribal leader Manglu. The Wikipedia plot summary runs to two sentences about the two brothers and does not reach her part.

relationship_to_protagonist: Father of both of Bachchan's roles
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Police inspector and father of the twin brothers — one an avid devotee of Lord Hanuman with superhuman strength, the other a meek magician.

relationship_to_protagonist: Figure alongside Bachchan's two roles
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Doctor's son in the film's supporting cast, married to Laxmi. The article's plot summary does not describe the part.

relationship_to_protagonist: Figure in the world of Bachchan's two roles
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Pickpocket in the film's supporting cast; the cast list gives the role no name and the plot summary does not mention it.

relationship_to_protagonist: The fraudulent godman Bachchan's Goga is brought in to dethrone, and who then fights to expose him
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Jailed businessman who learns conjuring tricks from a fellow inmate and sets up in a small town as a divine soothsayer, is ousted from his own temple by a professional magician, and tries to poison the prasad to prove the newcomer mortal.

relationship_to_protagonist: Brings Bachchan's Goga to the town, then cannot get him to leave
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Returned American NRI appalled to find his ex-convict father posing as a living god, who enlists the magician Goga to expose him and then asks him to go — only for Goga to keep the position.

relationship_to_protagonist: Top-billed opposite Bachchan's Goga
relationship_to_romance: Recorded as Minor with no pairing record: no fetched source establishes who romances whom in this film
character_gist: Leading female role. The Wikipedia plot summary follows the contest between the magician and the false godman and never describes her part in it.

relationship_to_protagonist: Figure in the town where Bachchan's Goga sets himself up
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Supporting role in Dharampur, the town whose whole population the false godman has convinced of his divine powers.

relationship_to_protagonist: The journalist who invents Azaad and hires Bachchan's drifter to be him
relationship_to_romance: No romance in the film; the relationship is author and creation
character_gist: Journalist known for articles against corrupt politicians, who invents a letter from a man called Azaad threatening public suicide on Republic Day, then finds a jobless drifter to embody him and builds him into a national figure.

relationship_to_protagonist: The proprietor who turns Bachchan's Azaad into a circulation campaign
relationship_to_romance: No romance in the film
character_gist: New owner of the newspaper who senses an opportunity in the sensation and coaxes the journalist into running an Azaad column and manufacturing a public figure. The article's plot calls him Seth Gokulchand while the cast list gives Gokuldas.

relationship_to_protagonist: The companion drifting through Rajnagar with Bachchan's nameless vaudevillian
relationship_to_romance: No romance in the film
character_gist: Fellow drifter accompanying the jobless performer who is recruited to impersonate Azaad.

relationship_to_protagonist: Figure in the newspaper and business world exploiting Bachchan's Azaad
relationship_to_romance: No romance in the film
character_gist: Businessman in the circle around the newspaper; the article's plot summary follows the journalist and the impostor and does not detail his part.

relationship_to_protagonist: Saves Bachchan's Vijay's life twice and becomes his one real friend
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance; he is hired as the sister's bodyguard
character_gist: Tamil coconut vendor who finds the ambushed gangster bleeding in the street and gets him to hospital, smuggles him out of his bed during a second assassination attempt, and takes employment as his sister's bodyguard.
performance_recognition: Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actor

relationship_to_protagonist: Destroyed Bachchan's Vijay's father and family, and is the object of his whole life
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Heroin smuggler who discredits the village schoolmaster in a staged scandal so the villagers lynch him, evicts the family and profits by it — the man whose name the grown Vijay exists to answer.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Vijay's mother, who refuses to live with what he has become
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Widow of the lynched schoolmaster, survivor of an attempted rape that went unpunished, who strongly disapproves of her son's criminal life and lives apart from him.
performance_recognition: Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actress

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Vijay's father, whose name he spends the film trying to clear
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Village schoolmaster who opposes the don's plan to base heroin smuggling in the village, is framed in a scandal by the don and the landlord, and is lynched to death by the villagers he taught.

relationship_to_protagonist: The nurse who cares for Bachchan's Vijay in hospital
relationship_to_romance: The film's romance, minor beside the revenge — romance centrality is scored 2
character_gist: Nurse who looks after the wounded gangster during his recovery from the ambush.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Vijay's younger sister, whose care he takes on as a boy
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Younger sister for whom the boy Vijay takes on responsibility after the family is evicted, and who is given a bodyguard once he becomes a target.

relationship_to_protagonist: The policeman who warns Bachchan's Vijay and reads him accurately
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Police commissioner, critical of the gangster but quietly sympathetic, who warns him of the coming assassination attempt and afterwards works out that he allowed it in order to elevate himself in his followers' eyes.

relationship_to_protagonist: The film's younger brother; Bachchan appears as himself in a guest turn
relationship_to_romance: His romance with Sonu runs beside his brother's with Matki
character_gist: Impulsive younger brother who takes to crime to hunt his mother's killer at his jailed brother's own urging, and becomes an underworld kingpin while that brother becomes a policeman.

relationship_to_protagonist: The film's elder brother; no connection to Bachchan's appearance as himself
relationship_to_romance: His romance with Matki is the film's second pairing
character_gist: Elder brother driven by justice rather than impulse, wrongly convicted of murder, reunited in jail with his own imprisoned father, and reformed into a police officer set against his brother.

relationship_to_protagonist: The brothers' father; no connection to Bachchan's guest appearance
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Policeman father who arrests his wife's murderer only to see him freed by a hostile witness, then goes to prison himself for killing his own brother, an advocate for criminals.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's guest appearance
relationship_to_romance: The elder brother's romance
character_gist: Ajay's girlfriend through his conviction, imprisonment and reform.

relationship_to_protagonist: The woman Bachchan's Bheema leaves his nephew with when he goes to prison
relationship_to_romance: Recorded as Minor with no pairing record: the article calls her the love of his life but describes no relationship
character_gist: The love of Bheema's life, to whom he hands his orphaned nephew when he is jailed for seven years, and whose brother helps him fight the Thakur on his return.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Bheema's sister, whose murder he avenges
relationship_to_romance: Her marriage is a ploy, not a romance
character_gist: The only educated person in the village, who leads the farmers against the landlord, is married by his son as a scheme to stop her mobilising them, overhears the truth, and is killed in the village centre as she runs to the police.

relationship_to_protagonist: The landlord Bachchan's Bheema returns from prison to break
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Tyrannical landlord seizing poor farmers' fields for an alcohol factory, who has his son marry the one educated woman in the village to neutralise her, and is finally brought to justice.

relationship_to_protagonist: Marries and betrays Bachchan's Bheema's sister, and is killed by him
relationship_to_romance: His marriage is the film's counterfeit romance
character_gist: The Thakur's son, who saves Laxmi and marries her with her brother's blessing as part of his father's scheme, and is killed by Bheema after her murder.

relationship_to_protagonist: Fights alongside Bachchan's Bheema against the landlord
relationship_to_romance: Brother of the woman Bheema loves
character_gist: Gauri's brother, who helps Bheema fight the Thakur's goons and bring him to justice after his release.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Tiger's younger half-brother, raised in ignorance of his past
relationship_to_romance: His marriage to Aarti is one of the film's domestic anchors
character_gist: Half-brother brought up by Tiger with no memory of Mumbai, grown into a police officer with a wife and daughter, who blames his brother when they are kidnapped and learns his real history only at the end.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Tiger's youngest half-brother
relationship_to_romance: His courtship of a general's daughter is the film's junior romance
character_gist: Youngest brother, a college student in love with the daughter of a general who wants her to marry a military officer, and equally ignorant of the family's Mumbai past.

relationship_to_protagonist: The woman Bachchan's Tiger loves, and the sister of his murdered best friend
relationship_to_romance: The film's romance, suspended for sixteen years by his obligation to his brothers
character_gist: Sister of the dock worker Bhaktawar kills, who refuses to leave with Tiger because his brothers must come first, promises to reunite with him later, becomes a successful actress, and finally explains the past to the brothers herself.

relationship_to_protagonist: The dock boss Bachchan's Tiger first serves and then sets out to kill
relationship_to_romance: Kills the friend whose sister is the romance
character_gist: Ruler of the Mumbai docks who treats his workers as slaves, kills Gonsalves, is jailed for the murder of Tiger's family that another man committed, and is released and manipulated into hunting Tiger down.

relationship_to_protagonist: The policeman who stops Bachchan's Tiger, then commits the murders blamed on the villain
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Inspector who talks Tiger out of revenge in the name of his brothers, then robs the don's safe, burns his house with his wife and daughter inside, bombs the train carrying the boys to kill the witnesses, and lives richly on the proceeds.

relationship_to_protagonist: Father of the woman Bachchan's youngest brother loves
relationship_to_romance: The obstacle to the junior romance
character_gist: Retired general who insists his daughter marry a military officer, and the film's principal comic figure.
performance_recognition: Filmfare Best Comedian Award nomination

relationship_to_protagonist: Sister-in-law of Bachchan's Tiger, kidnapped to draw him out
relationship_to_romance: Part of the settled family life the past comes to destroy
character_gist: Wife of the policeman brother and mother of their daughter Jyoti, kidnapped with the child in Bangalore and told the truth about Tiger by her captor.
performance_recognition: Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actress nomination

relationship_to_protagonist: The woman Bachchan's Ali courts, and the daughter of his father's imprisoned friend
relationship_to_romance: The film's romance, running alongside the masked hero's campaign
character_gist: Daughter of the court magician Ameer Baba, returned from India to rescue her imprisoned father, and wooed by the restaurateur Ali who is secretly the masked Ajooba.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Ali's companion in foiling the usurper's schemes
relationship_to_romance: His courtship of the princess parallels Ali's of Rukhsana
character_gist: Ali's friend, with him in raiding the Vazir's caravans and wrecking his plans, and in love with the princess on the other side of the palace.

relationship_to_protagonist: Usurped the throne of Bachchan's Ali's father and tried to have him killed at birth
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance; his household holds both the imprisoned father-figure and the princess
character_gist: Devil-worshipping minister who has every child born to the Sultan strangled, revives a stone demon to conquer the world, steals the magician's Necklace of Immortality, and seizes the throne under the slogan Shaitan Zindabad.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Ali's father, lost to him in the escape by sea
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Kind ruler of Baharistan whose heirs are murdered at birth until divine intervention protects one, and who goes missing after the sea battle that scatters the family.

relationship_to_protagonist: The court magician whose daughter Bachchan's Ali loves, imprisoned by the usurper
relationship_to_romance: His imprisonment is what brings the heroine back to the kingdom
character_gist: Good court magician and the Sultan's close friend, who brings the magic sword drawable only by the royal family, is tricked out of his Necklace of Immortality, thrown into the dungeon and blamed for the Sultan's murder.

relationship_to_protagonist: Belongs to the friend's romance rather than Bachchan's
relationship_to_romance: The second of the film's two courtships
character_gist: Princess on the usurper's side of the palace, the object of Hassan's affections.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Inderjeet's love, whose father he arrests and whose brother destroys his family
relationship_to_romance: The film's romance, broken by his duty and then poisoned by her family
character_gist: Woman the honest policeman loves, until he has to arrest her father for murder and is transferred; years later her brother and his friends kill the daughter Inderjeet had just married off.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Inderjeet's adopted daughter, whose murder turns him vigilante
relationship_to_romance: Her marriage is the film's second, doomed pairing
character_gist: Adopted daughter whose marriage the retired policeman arranges, and who is killed with her husband days later — the deaths the police refuse to act on.

relationship_to_protagonist: Husband of Bachchan's Inderjeet's adopted daughter
relationship_to_romance: The younger couple, killed almost immediately after the wedding
character_gist: Young man married to Neelu with Inderjeet's blessing, murdered alongside her by the brother of the woman Inderjeet once loved.

relationship_to_protagonist: The man Bachchan's Inderjeet arrests, at the cost of his romance and his posting
relationship_to_romance: His arrest is what ends the romance
character_gist: Shanti's father, arrested for murder by the policeman courting his daughter — the arrest that costs Inderjeet both the woman and his position.

relationship_to_protagonist: Part of the political protection that makes Bachchan's Inderjeet abandon the law
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Minister in the network whose influence keeps the killers untouched and the police inactive.

relationship_to_protagonist: The woman Bachchan's Vijay finally lets himself love
relationship_to_romance: The film's surviving romance, arrived at only after he has given up the first one
character_gist: Nightclub dancer who grows close to the lonely inspector, comforts him after his friends are murdered, and is the one person the killer cannot take from him.

relationship_to_protagonist: The woman Bachchan's Vijay renounced for his friend, without knowing she wanted him
relationship_to_romance: The sacrificed romance — she was interested in him, and he never learns it in time
character_gist: Woman Vijay gives up for his friend Shekhar, unaware that her feelings were for him; she and Shekhar are murdered by the criminal they try to report.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Vijay's closest friend, for whom he gave up Seema
relationship_to_romance: The man the renunciation was for
character_gist: Friend who unknowingly receives the woman Vijay loved, shelters the fugitive Tony without knowing who he is, and is killed with his wife when he tries to warn the police.

relationship_to_protagonist: The criminal whose twin alibi defeats Bachchan's Vijay, and who kills everyone he loves
relationship_to_romance: Destroys both of the film's relationships
character_gist: Criminal mastermind freed by videotape evidence placing him elsewhere, a trick worked by his mentally handicapped twin Jojo; he kills Shekhar, Seema, and Vijay's brother and sister-in-law in turn.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Vijay's younger brother, his only family
relationship_to_romance: His marriage is the third relationship the killer destroys
character_gist: Younger brother studying abroad, Vijay's only family, tracked down and killed with his new wife.

relationship_to_protagonist: The superior who warns Bachchan's Vijay against taking the law into his own hands
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Police commissioner who tells the bereaved inspector not to become a killer himself — the warning Vijay resigns rather than obey.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Badshah Khan's wife, and in a second role their daughter
relationship_to_romance: The film's central romance, opened by a demand for a severed head and closed by two decades of separation
character_gist: Afghan woman who agrees to marry Badshah Khan only if he brings her the head of her father's killer, waits through his imprisonment, and goes mad on being told he is dead. She also plays their grown daughter Mehndi, who comes to India to find him.
performance_recognition: Filmfare Award for Best Actress nomination

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Badshah Khan's childhood friend, who guards his wife for twenty years
relationship_to_romance: The custodian of the marriage during the husband's absence
character_gist: Childhood friend who becomes Benazir's guardian while Badshah Khan is imprisoned, is made to promise to raise his daughter and to tell his wife he is dead, and is finally kidnapped with Benazir by the crime lord.
performance_recognition: Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actor

relationship_to_protagonist: Son of the officer Bachchan's Badshah Khan confessed to killing, and suitor to his daughter
relationship_to_romance: In love with the daughter of the man he means to kill
character_gist: Police inspector whose father Badshah Khan took the blame for killing, hunting him for vengeance while in love with his daughter Mehndi.

relationship_to_protagonist: Brother of the man Bachchan's Badshah Khan beheaded, and the film's crime lord
relationship_to_romance: Kidnaps the wife and the friend to force the hero out
character_gist: Brother of the beheaded Habibullah, who kidnaps a jailer's daughter to ransom Badshah Khan, and rises to major crime lord before abducting Benazir and Khuda Baksh.
performance_recognition: Filmfare Award for Best Villain nomination

relationship_to_protagonist: The jailer's daughter Bachchan's Badshah Khan went back to prison to save
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Daughter of the jailer Ranveer Sikhri, kidnapped as ransom for Badshah Khan, who grows up into the police force and respects him as an uncle.
performance_recognition: Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actress nomination

relationship_to_protagonist: The jailer Bachchan's Badshah Khan surrenders to, and is later blamed for killing
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Jailer whom Badshah Khan addresses as Rajput Khan and returns to voluntarily after a month, and whose murder by another man Badshah takes the blame for to protect his daughter.

relationship_to_protagonist: The film's opening protagonist; Bachchan contributes narration only
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance; the film is a brothers' revenge story
character_gist: Mafia boss living with his wife and two brothers, who refuses a rival's drug business and is killed for it, setting the revenge plot in motion.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: His marriage to Kiran sits beside the revenge plot
character_gist: The brother who chose a different path and lived apart, who takes his dead brother's place and joins the rival's operation purely to avenge him — and is left the last Koli standing.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Rival crime boss whose drug offer is refused, who has one brother killed and another gunned down, and abducts the family's sister to trap the last of them.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: The third Koli brother, seriously injured in the attack that kills Pitamber and gunned down when he goes to rescue their kidnapped sister.

relationship_to_protagonist: The film's title role; Bachchan contributes narration only
relationship_to_romance: Unrecorded; the article carries no plot section
character_gist: Title professor of the film. The Wikipedia article has no plot summary, so the part is recorded from the cast list alone.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: Unrecorded; the article carries no plot section
character_gist: Leading female role, credited second. No plot summary survives in the article to describe the part.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: Unrecorded; the article carries no plot section
character_gist: Credited third in the cast list; the article gives no plot from which to describe the role.

relationship_to_protagonist: One of the two warring gangsters Bachchan's Amar unites, and who calls him elder brother
relationship_to_romance: His romance with Salma runs beside Amar's with Shalu
character_gist: Gang leader whose identity is built on a religious feud with Hariharan, persuaded by Amar that the don Brijbhan is the greater enemy, and who sets the rivalry aside to fight him.

relationship_to_protagonist: The second gangster Bachchan's Amar reconciles
relationship_to_romance: His romance with Radha is the third of the film's pairings
character_gist: The rival gang leader, locked into the same religious feud, who also regards Amar as an elder brother and joins the alliance against Brijbhan.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Amar's childhood sweetheart, held captive by the film's villain
relationship_to_romance: The film's romance for Bachchan's character, conducted through her captivity
character_gist: Amar's childhood sweetheart, kept by the don Brijbhan as his mistress — the personal stake in an otherwise political fight.

relationship_to_protagonist: The don Bachchan's Amar unites two gangs to destroy
relationship_to_romance: Holds the woman Amar loves
character_gist: Son of the criminal Goga, now a high-profile don working with corrupt police and army officers to spread terrorism, and holding Amar's sweetheart captive.

relationship_to_protagonist: Attached to one of the gangsters Bachchan's Amar reconciles
relationship_to_romance: The second of the film's three romances
character_gist: The woman Karim loves, on his side of the religious divide the film sets out to close.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Amar's mother, separated from him by the villain's father
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Mother from whom Amar was separated in childhood by the criminal Goga, whose arrest opens the film.

relationship_to_protagonist: The film's protagonist; Bachchan appears as himself in a guest turn
relationship_to_romance: Carries the film's romance with Gauri
character_gist: Kind-hearted Banaras wrestler who brings his dying adoptive father to Mumbai, refuses to join the local gangster, watches that man humiliate his father and kill his brother, and destroys the gang one brother at a time.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's guest appearance
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Freedom fighter awarded the Tambra Patra and the hero's honoured adoptive father, dying of throat cancer, whom the gangster forces to bark like a dog before the whole locality.
performance_recognition: Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actor; Screen Award for Best Supporting Actor

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's guest appearance
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Tyrannical gangster ruling the locality with six brothers, who humiliates the dying freedom fighter and is finally made to bark like a dog and beaten to death in front of the residents.
performance_recognition: Filmfare Award for Best Villain nomination

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's guest appearance
relationship_to_romance: The film's romance, and the voice that turns the locality
character_gist: Woman the wrestler comes to love in Mumbai, who stands up during his public humiliation and rouses the crowd to attack the gang.

relationship_to_protagonist: The film's protagonist; Bachchan contributes narration only
relationship_to_romance: His romance with Paro is one of the film's two courtships
character_gist: Heir raised in England who comes to India against his grandfather's wishes, swaps lives with a taxi driver born the same day, falls in love with the driver's sister, and offers to become a Brahmin to marry her.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: His romance with Pooja is the second of the two
character_gist: Middle-class Brahmin taxi driver who curses the rich man born on his own day, then takes his place, is groomed to pass as him, and reopens the family's failing company with equal profit-sharing for the workers.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: The romance the film's religious objection is raised against
character_gist: Balu's sister, loved by the heir living as a taxi driver; her father is enraged to learn the young man is a Christian.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: Opposes the trip that produces the romance
character_gist: Grandfather who raised Rahul after his parents' death and refuses to let him visit India, fearing he will fall in love and ruin himself as his parents did.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Dr Ram's wife, who dies of grief
relationship_to_romance: An established marriage ended by bereavement rather than a courtship
character_gist: Wife of the celebrated surgeon, whose death follows the killing of his younger brother and leaves him desolate and alcoholic.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Dr Ram's younger brother, whose murder drives the film
relationship_to_romance: His love for Renuka is the romance the villains destroy
character_gist: Engineer who refuses to approve a corrupt minister's power project and resists a thug's advances on the woman he loves, is framed for a woman's murder, and is tortured to death in jail and passed off as a suicide.

relationship_to_protagonist: Marries the man whose gang killed Bachchan's Dr Ram's brother, and files the case against him
relationship_to_romance: The romance transferred from the murdered brother to his killer's brother
character_gist: Woman Bharat loves, who marries his tormentor Raja without apparent regret after his death, then accuses the surgeon of killing Raja on the operating table — the charge that sends him to prison.

relationship_to_protagonist: Among the forces Bachchan's Dr Ram is set against
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Criminal styled the Terror of Terrors, in the network around the power project and the Tonga brothers.

relationship_to_protagonist: Engineers the framing and death of Bachchan's Dr Ram's brother
relationship_to_romance: Destroys his brother's romance to clear the way for his own brother
character_gist: Strongman who plots to wipe out Bharat so that his brother Raja can have Renuka, using a subordinate inspector to frame and imprison him.

relationship_to_protagonist: The fellow prisoner who tells Bachchan's Dr Ram how his brother really died
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Atomic-energy scientist jailed on a false charge of passing nuclear formulae abroad, prisoner number 92, who witnessed Bharat being tortured to death and tells his brother so.

relationship_to_protagonist: The cadet Bachchan's Major Rana refuses to discharge, and then rebuilds
relationship_to_romance: Carries the film's romance with Nisha
character_gist: Playboy forced into a military academy by a clause in his father's will, whose attempts to get discharged the Major blocks; beaten and crippled by his lover's gangster brother, he is trained back to strength by the same Major.

relationship_to_protagonist: The woman the cadet under Bachchan's Major loves
relationship_to_romance: The film's romance, opposed by her gangster brother
character_gist: Sister of the gangster Shankar, in love with Vir and promised by her brother to the son of his friend Bihari.

relationship_to_protagonist: The gangster Bachchan's Major and his cadet finally face
relationship_to_romance: The external opposition to the romance, later withdrawn
character_gist: Gangster who pretends to accept his sister's suitor and then has him beaten and his limbs broken, relents once Vir returns strong enough to face him, and is killed by his own friend Bihari.

relationship_to_protagonist: Wife of Bachchan's Major Jasbir Singh Rana
relationship_to_romance: A spouse-only role: the marriage is established rather than courted, which is why the film carries no pairing record
character_gist: The Major's wife, a doctor, in the household beside the academy where he trains and later rebuilds the cadet.

character: Sunil Nigam (Chote Miyan) / Inspector Pyare Mohan Bhargava
relationship_to_protagonist: Plays the double pair opposite Bachchan's two roles — the petty thief and the inspector he is mistaken for
relationship_to_romance: His inspector's romance with Seema is the film's main courtship
character_gist: In a dual role matching Bachchan's: an inspector dating his colleague's sister, and the petty thief whose crimes are blamed on him. The two thieves finally clear the policemen and take their jobs.
performance_recognition: Zee Cine Award for Best Actor in a Comic Role; Filmfare Award for Best Actor nomination

relationship_to_protagonist: Sister of Bachchan's inspector role, and kidnapped by the villain
relationship_to_romance: The film's romance, attached to the other inspector
character_gist: Arjun's sister, dating his colleague Pyare, mistaken by her own family for a thief's girlfriend, and kidnapped by the smuggler to force the policemen's hand.

relationship_to_protagonist: The witness Bachchan's Inspector Arjun takes into protection
relationship_to_romance: Recorded as Minor with no pairing record: the article establishes her as Arjun's love interest but develops nothing
character_gist: Woman who witnesses her friend Madhu's murder and calls the police, and is taken to safety by the inspector.

relationship_to_protagonist: The smuggler Bachchan's two roles finally converge to catch
relationship_to_romance: Kidnaps the woman at the centre of the romance
character_gist: Smuggler working under cover as a hotel sculptor, who has an eyewitness killed, kidnaps the inspector's sister, and is finally arrested when his own van hijacking is foiled.

relationship_to_protagonist: The superior who demotes Bachchan's inspector over the doubles' crimes
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Police commissioner thrashed by the two look-alike thieves, who ends the film demoting the inspectors to traffic duty and giving their jobs to the thieves.

relationship_to_protagonist: The film's protagonist; Bachchan contributes narration only
relationship_to_romance: Carries the film's romance, which begins as a staged marriage
character_gist: Tourist guide hired to fake a marriage and then behave badly enough to change a grandfather's mind about Indian grooms — and who wins the old man over with every attempt.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: The film's romantic lead, whose scheme becomes a real courtship
character_gist: London-raised granddaughter in love with another man, who moves to India and stages a marriage to a guide to defeat her grandfather's insistence on an Indian groom.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: The obstacle the whole deception is built against
character_gist: Grandfather who moved to London for a better life and insists his granddaughter respect Indian culture and marry an Indian man.

relationship_to_protagonist: The woman who sets out to marry Bachchan's Lal Baadshah
relationship_to_romance: Recorded as Minor with no pairing record: the article establishes her intent and nothing of the relationship
character_gist: Insurance agent who falls in love with the basti's protector and is determined to become his wife.

relationship_to_protagonist: The man who murdered the Maharaja Bachchan's second role served
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Castle-dwelling patriarch still hunting the treasure of the Maharaja he murdered years earlier with his brother, and father of the don who rules the city.

relationship_to_protagonist: The don Bachchan's Lal Baadshah is permanently at odds with
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Don of the city, Dayal Singh's son, who with his corrupt policeman brother intends to rule it and clashes constantly with the basti's champion.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Lal Singh's foster mother
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Foster mother with whom Lal lives in the Mumbai basti among the poor he grew up with.

relationship_to_protagonist: Figure in the world around Bachchan's Lal Baadshah
relationship_to_romance: Outside the film's recorded romance
character_gist: A lawyer's daughter in the film's supporting cast.

relationship_to_protagonist: The woman who proposes to Bachchan's illiterate Heera and elopes with him
relationship_to_romance: The film's romance, and the cause of the final break with the father
character_gist: Lawyer's daughter who mistakes Heera for a servant, hears his story, proposes marriage herself, and elopes with him when her mother's alliance with a rival zamindar threatens it. Her voice was dubbed by Rekha.

relationship_to_protagonist: Wife of Bachchan's Bhanu Pratap and mother of his Heera — the one affection the son has at home
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: The sarpanch's wife, and with the servant Mindra the only source of affection for the son her husband treats as a servant. Her voice was also dubbed by Rekha.

relationship_to_protagonist: The servant who is Bachchan's Heera's only friend, and who narrates his past
relationship_to_romance: Tells Radha the story that makes her propose, and urges Heera to choose her
character_gist: Household servant and Heera's sole friend, who recounts his history to Radha, encourages him to choose her over his father's approval, and shelters the couple on the village outskirts.

relationship_to_protagonist: The girl Bachchan's Bhanu Pratap adopted and tried to marry to his son
relationship_to_romance: The failed first match, and the source of the father's lasting hatred
character_gist: Orphan adopted by Bhanu Pratap, for whose sake the young Heera quit school. Unwilling to marry an illiterate man she attempts suicide; Heera saves her and takes the blame, and his father concludes he lusted after her.

relationship_to_protagonist: The rival zamindar working to ruin Bachchan's Bhanu Pratap's family
relationship_to_romance: Tries to take Radha out of the romance and into his own son's marriage
character_gist: Rival zamindar of Bharatpur who schemes to marry Radha to his son Arjun so that her lawyer father will act in his favour against Bhanu Pratap.

relationship_to_protagonist: The relative whose loan lets Bachchan's Heera start his business
relationship_to_romance: Supports the couple after the elopement
character_gist: Radha's uncle, who lends the disowned couple the money with which Heera starts the transport company he names after his father.

relationship_to_protagonist: The film's protagonist; Bachchan appears in a special appearance as himself
relationship_to_romance: The wronged wife whose campaign to win her husband back is the plot
character_gist: Devoted traditional wife who, on discovering her husband's affair, remakes herself as a model and sends the children and mother-in-law to live with him and his mistress until the new household collapses.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's special appearance
relationship_to_romance: The husband whose affair drives the film
character_gist: Advertising executive who leaves his wife and children for an aspiring model, and comes to see that she was drawn to his wealth and status while his wife had supported him unconditionally.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's special appearance
relationship_to_romance: The mistress, displaced by the wife's campaign
character_gist: Aspiring model who meets the executive at an office interview, takes him from his family, and is worn down by the children and mother-in-law he is sent before returning to her old boyfriend.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's special appearance
relationship_to_romance: Runs the campaign that restores the marriage, and nearly wrecks his own
character_gist: Friend who helps the abandoned wife remake herself, and whose platonic bond with the mistress — he calls her his sister — is misread by his own wife until he clears it up.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's special appearance
relationship_to_romance: The film's second marriage, briefly broken by a misunderstanding
character_gist: Lakhan's wife, who walks out after seeing him embrace the mistress and is won back with the declaration that gives the film its title.

relationship_to_protagonist: The film's dual protagonist; Bachchan's Kabeera is a supporting patriotic figure
relationship_to_romance: Both romances belong to his two roles
character_gist: Twin brothers separated in childhood at the end of a war — one raised in India as a novelist, the other raised in Pakistan by a terrorist as Tauheed and told his mother died in an Indian army attack.

relationship_to_protagonist: Belongs to the twins' story rather than Bachchan's Kabeera
relationship_to_romance: One of the film's two romances
character_gist: Woman attached to the Indian brother's side of the story; the article's long plot summary does not develop the relationship.

relationship_to_protagonist: Belongs to the Pakistan-raised twin's story
relationship_to_romance: The second of the film's romances
character_gist: Woman in the world of the brother raised across the border as Tauheed.

relationship_to_protagonist: Mother of the twins whose story Bachchan's Kabeera frames
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Mother of the separated twins, widow of an Indian Army officer killed in the war during which the boys were lost.

relationship_to_protagonist: Sent to uncover the identity Bachchan's Colonel Sodhi is hiding behind, then joins him
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Army major sent in the guise of a Bengali journalist to discover who the Mumbai figure Dadabhai really is, and who allies with him once he learns the truth.

relationship_to_protagonist: The politician Bachchan's Colonel Sodhi fakes his own death to expose
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Minister discovered to be part of the conspiracy behind an army officer's killing, and the target of the colonel's undercover campaign.

relationship_to_protagonist: Head of the terrorist group Bachchan's Colonel Sodhi is sent after
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Leader of the terrorist group believed responsible for the murder of an army officer, whom the colonel stages his own death in order to reach.

relationship_to_protagonist: Wife of Bachchan's Colonel Sodhi
relationship_to_romance: A spouse-only role, scored Minor with no pairing record
character_gist: The colonel's wife, on the family side of a life he abandons by faking his own death.

relationship_to_protagonist: Police officer in the investigation around Bachchan's undercover colonel
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Police inspector in the Mumbai half of the story, where the colonel lives under the name Devraj Hathoda.

relationship_to_protagonist: The film's protagonist; Bachchan supplies the voice of God
relationship_to_romance: His unreturned love for Rani is the film's romance, resolved after his death
character_gist: Courier company employee in love with a woman who thinks of him only as a friend, shot dead by his own boss, whose heart is transplanted into the wounded inspector — after which he appears as a ghost only that inspector can see.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's voice role
relationship_to_romance: Inherits both the heart and the romance
character_gist: Narcotics inspector who receives the dead man's heart, is haunted by his ghost, agrees to avenge him, and falls in love with the woman the dead man loved.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's voice role
relationship_to_romance: The woman both men love, in life and after death
character_gist: Woman who thinks of Hero only as a good friend, falls in love with the inspector carrying his heart, and recognises the dead man's fighting moves in her rescuer.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's voice role
relationship_to_romance: Kidnaps the woman at the film's climax
character_gist: Courier company owner running a drug ring, who shoots his own loyal employee dead, kidnaps the heroine, and is finally shot by the ghost guiding the inspector's hand.

relationship_to_protagonist: The music teacher who returns to break Bachchan's Narayan Shankar's regime
relationship_to_romance: The film's advocate of love, and the lover of the principal's dead daughter
character_gist: Music teacher revealed to be a former Gurukul student expelled for loving the principal's daughter, who killed herself afterwards. He returns to honour her memory by spreading love through the school against the principal's tradition, honour and discipline.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Narayan Shankar's only daughter, who killed herself after he expelled her lover
relationship_to_romance: The romance the whole film is an argument about
character_gist: The principal's daughter, in love with a student her father expelled, who took her own life — the loss that hardened him and the memory the teacher returns to honour.

relationship_to_protagonist: One of the three students whose romances defy Bachchan's principal
relationship_to_romance: One of three parallel courtships the film runs
character_gist: Student who falls in love with a widow, Kiran, and wins her slowly while working as a piano teacher for her nephew.

relationship_to_protagonist: Second of the three students defying Bachchan's principal
relationship_to_romance: The second parallel courtship
character_gist: Student in love with his childhood sweetheart Sanjana, already attached to another man, who takes a job in a cafe outside the school to be near her.

relationship_to_protagonist: Third of the three students whose love affairs the principal moves to punish
relationship_to_romance: The third parallel courtship, which begins in harassment
character_gist: Student who harasses and blackmails Ishika into a hug and a date, falls in love with her during a dance competition, lies about his family's class, and is accepted after confessing.

relationship_to_protagonist: No direct connection to Bachchan's principal; a student at the neighbouring girls' school
relationship_to_romance: Half of the third courtship
character_gist: Student from the neighbouring school, pursued and blackmailed into a date, who comes to love him and forgives the lie about his background.

relationship_to_protagonist: A figure of the same authority as Bachchan's principal
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romances
character_gist: Senior figure in the film's world of tradition and discipline. A special appearance.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Vijay Kapoor's only son, thrown out and finally reconciled
relationship_to_romance: His marriage to Nisha is the film's romance, strained by the reconciliation
character_gist: Son returned from abroad with an IT degree, thrown out for taking a loan to start his own business, who wins back the family fortune by forcing the fraudulent son-in-law to sign it over.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Vijay Kapoor's wife
relationship_to_romance: A spouse-only role, scored Minor with no pairing record
character_gist: Wife and mother of four in the household the film is built around, through its bankruptcy and its reconciliation.

relationship_to_protagonist: The son-in-law who strips Bachchan's Vijay Kapoor of his fortune
relationship_to_romance: Marries into the family in order to rob it
character_gist: Business graduate who idolises his prospective father-in-law in public, marries his eldest daughter, obtains power of attorney, bankrupts him, and mistreats his wife until she leaves.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Vijay Kapoor's eldest daughter, married to the man who ruins him
relationship_to_romance: The marriage that turns out to be the family's undoing
character_gist: Eldest daughter charmed into marrying Rajesh, mistreated by him once the fortune is his, who returns home and tells him she can never forgive what he did to her family.

relationship_to_protagonist: Wife of the son Bachchan's Vijay Kapoor disowns
relationship_to_romance: The younger marriage, strained by her husband's return to his father
character_gist: Woman Ajay marries after being thrown out of the family home, displeased by his reunion with his father; the couple separate and reunite when she finds she is pregnant.

relationship_to_protagonist: The film's protagonist; Bachchan contributes the voice-over narration
relationship_to_romance: Carries the film's romance with Gauri, and is the object of Elizabeth's unspoken one
character_gist: Young farmer of Champaner who accepts a British officer's wager — a cricket match against three years of cancelled land tax, or triple tax if the villagers lose — and assembles a team of eleven, including the untouchable spin bowler Kachra.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: The film's romance, and the cause of the informer's betrayal
character_gist: The village medic's daughter, courted by Bhuvan; a jealous villager who covets her turns informer and saboteur for the British captain.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: The unspoken second romance, never returned
character_gist: The captain's sister, horrified by her brother's cruelty and secretly in love with Bhuvan, who covertly coaches the village team in the rules and strategies of cricket.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Arrogant regiment commander who intercepts the villagers' petition and proposes the wager, and is reprimanded by his superiors and threatened with court-martial for gambling the government treasury.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: His jealousy over Gauri is what makes him an informer
character_gist: Villager who covets Gauri and agrees to spy and sabotage for the British, is exposed by Elizabeth, and is given a chance at redemption by Bhuvan — taking the catches that trigger the British collapse.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Low-caste villager whose withered arm gives him lethal spin bowling, recruited into the team over the village's caste objections.

relationship_to_protagonist: The killer whose spirit possesses Bachchan's Inspector Manu Verma
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance; the possession is what threatens the marriage
character_gist: Sociopathic contract killer who murders the defence minister in Budapest, is caught and hanged, and whose spirit passes into the investigating officer's body to make him act out what he wanted. Listed in the film's Filmfare table for Best Actor in a Negative Role, where the article leaves the result column blank.

relationship_to_protagonist: Wife of Bachchan's Manu Verma, living with the man he becomes
relationship_to_romance: A spouse-only role, scored Minor with no pairing record
character_gist: The inspector's wife, who has to live alongside the behaviour the possessing spirit produces in him.

relationship_to_protagonist: Figure drawn into the possessed officer's orbit
relationship_to_romance: Adjacent to the marriage the possession endangers
character_gist: Woman in the world the possessed inspector moves through. The film's Filmfare table lists her for a Special Award with the result column left blank.

relationship_to_protagonist: The assassination that starts the case Bachchan's Manu Verma investigates
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Defence minister murdered during a conference in Budapest — the killing that brings the inspector and the assassin together.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Yash Raichand's wife, who cannot overrule him and loses her son for it
relationship_to_romance: The film's one marriage, recorded as a pairing: deferential in public, reproachful in private
character_gist: Wife of the industrialist, heartbroken when he disowns their adopted elder son, who sends the family nanny to London with the exiles and waits ten years for a reconciliation she is not permitted to force.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Yash's adopted elder son, disowned for marrying against his wishes
relationship_to_romance: His marriage to Anjali is the rupture the whole film turns on
character_gist: Adopted son who learns at eight that he is not their natural child and grows up determined to meet his parents' expectations, then marries a Chandni Chowk girl after her father's death and is disowned and exiled to London.

relationship_to_protagonist: The daughter-in-law Bachchan's Yash rejects on grounds of class
relationship_to_romance: The romance the patriarch refuses to accept
character_gist: Lively young woman from Chandni Chowk whose marriage to the Raichand heir costs him his family, and who raises her son in London with her younger sister and the family's old nanny.
performance_recognition: Best Actress at the 13th Valenciennes International Film Festival

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Yash's natural son, who works secretly to undo his father's decision
relationship_to_romance: His courtship of Pooja runs alongside the reconciliation plot
character_gist: Younger son sent to boarding school after the rupture, who returns ten years later, uses an MBA in London as a pretext to find his brother, and lives in his house under a false name to bring him home.

relationship_to_protagonist: Sister-in-law of the son Bachchan's Yash disowned
relationship_to_romance: The younger romance, and the engine of the reunion
character_gist: Anjali's younger sister, raised in London into a popular university student and fashion diva, who conceals Rohan's identity from her brother-in-law and pushes the family back together.

relationship_to_protagonist: The bride Bachchan's Yash chose for his son
relationship_to_romance: The arranged match that quietly steps aside for the love match
character_gist: Family friend whom Yash wants Rahul to marry and who quietly loves him, and who withdraws once she understands his feelings for Anjali. An extended guest appearance.

relationship_to_protagonist: The household's nanny, sent after the son Bachchan's Yash exiled
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Nanny who raised both Raichand sons, sent to London by Nandini to accompany the exiled couple.

relationship_to_protagonist: One of the three blind men Bachchan's Rajput recruits and abuses
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance; the film has none for Bachchan's role
character_gist: Blinded in an accident and left with a powerful sixth sense, trained for the heist and sensing from a distance when a fellow robber is in danger.

relationship_to_protagonist: Second of the blind trio Bachchan's Rajput trains for the robbery
relationship_to_romance: His declared love for Neha is the film's romance
character_gist: One of the three blind men recruited for the bank robbery, who falls in love with their trainer and learns why she is really working for their employer.

relationship_to_protagonist: Blackmailed by Bachchan's Rajput into training the blind men
relationship_to_romance: The film's romance, conducted under coercion
character_gist: Teacher at a school for the blind, blackmailed into training the trio because her younger brother is being held hostage, and increasingly resistant to her employer's abuse of them.

relationship_to_protagonist: The one member of the trio who knows where the loot is, and whom Bachchan's Rajput tortures for it
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Third of the blind robbers, the only one who knows the location of the jewels, whose face is caught on camera and who is beaten and tickled by his employer to make him talk. Listed in the film's Filmfare table for Best Comedian, where the article leaves the result column blank.

relationship_to_protagonist: The gangster Bachchan's Dr Rastogi diagnoses and unwittingly sets after his own sister
relationship_to_romance: One of the two men in love with the doctor's sister
character_gist: Dreaded Mumbai goon told by the doctor that he is suffering from a love virus curable only by love, and advised to woo the girl he is smitten by — who is the doctor's own sister.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Dr Rastogi's younger sister, whom he takes abroad to marry off
relationship_to_romance: The woman both men love, and the one shot in the crossfire
character_gist: Dance teacher who stops a goon beating a man in her class, is loved by that goon without knowing it, and is taken abroad by her brother to be married — unaware to him, in love with the bowling instructor.

relationship_to_protagonist: The man Bachchan's Dr Rastogi's sister actually loves
relationship_to_romance: The successful half of the rivalry
character_gist: Bowling instructor in love with Komal, who follows the family abroad in disguise, saves the goon's life, is beaten when the doctor sets the two men against each other, and marries her at the end.

relationship_to_protagonist: The law circling the gangster in Bachchan's doctor's orbit
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Police commissioner pursuing Munna Bhai's crime world through the film's comic plot.

relationship_to_protagonist: Conducts the seven-year fire sacrifice to the god Bachchan plays
relationship_to_romance: His marriage to Vishakha is the relationship the film destroys
character_gist: Brahmin who has conducted the yajna to appease the rain god for seven years, whose wife confesses her adultery to him and begs him to kill her.

relationship_to_protagonist: Belongs to the human drama beneath the god Bachchan plays
relationship_to_romance: The film's central adultery, revived after ten years
character_gist: Paravasu's wife, who loved Yavakri before he left for ten years of penance and resumes the affair on his return, is accused by her father-in-law, and pleads for her lover's cremation.

relationship_to_protagonist: Worshipped the god Bachchan plays for ten years to obtain divine power
relationship_to_romance: The lover whose return restarts the adultery
character_gist: Man who spent ten years worshipping Devraj Indra in the jungle to attain Brahma Jnana, returns to pursue his old love, curses a tribal girl with death, and is slain by a demon his lover's father-in-law summons.

relationship_to_protagonist: The film's other brother, in the human story below Bachchan's god
relationship_to_romance: His love for the tribal girl is the film's tender relationship, ruined by a delay
character_gist: Young Brahmin in love with a tribal girl, who is delayed from meeting her father and the village elders because he stays to cremate his brother's rival — so she is married to a fellow tribesman instead.

relationship_to_protagonist: Belongs to the human story beneath Bachchan's Devraj Indra
relationship_to_romance: Half of the romance the film treats most sympathetically
character_gist: Tribal girl who seeks her father's and her elders' approval before marrying Arvasu, witnesses the adultery and speaks of it frankly, is cursed with death within a month, and is married off when her suitor fails to appear.

relationship_to_protagonist: The father whose curse drives the mortal tragedy under Bachchan's god
relationship_to_romance: Summons the demon that kills his daughter-in-law's lover
character_gist: Brahmin father who dislikes both his sons and suspects his daughter-in-law, and who summons a Brahma Rakshas to kill her lover — on terms that would cost his own life if the man survived.

relationship_to_protagonist: Conceives the robbery Bachchan's Major seconds and helps plan
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: The man who sparks the plan to rob the bank holding the Los Angeles police department's funding, who stole and sold the truck that got them all arrested, kidnaps the police chief, and conceals that he speaks English.
performance_recognition: Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actor nomination

relationship_to_protagonist: One of the six in the robbery Bachchan's Major helps lead
relationship_to_romance: His girlfriend is the film's only romantic thread
character_gist: Bouncer with a girlfriend working as a club dancer, one of the six Indians detained without evidence whose resentment becomes the plan.

relationship_to_protagonist: Member of the crew Bachchan's Major plans the robbery with
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Drug peddler living off the street with a mentally disabled sister in an asylum, who brings Mak into the group and is shot dead by him for his brutal interrogation of the kidnapped police chief.
performance_recognition: Filmfare Best Comedian Award nomination

relationship_to_protagonist: Takes a bullet saving Bachchan's Major during the robbery
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Man saved from drug dealers on condition he split his loot, who is hit by a bullet shielding the Major outside the bank and later kills Bali over the treatment of their hostage.

relationship_to_protagonist: The reluctant member of Bachchan's Major's crew
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Jobless software engineer in the middle of a divorce and a custody fight, who walks away with his share and comes back when his lawyer tells him it is not enough.

relationship_to_protagonist: Wife of Bachchan's Major, whose illness is his reason for the robbery
relationship_to_romance: A spouse-only role, scored Minor with no pairing record
character_gist: The Major's sick wife, whom he lives with and cannot support; he learns of her death on returning to the hideout after the robbery.

relationship_to_protagonist: The film's protagonist; Bachchan contributes narration only
relationship_to_romance: Half of the romance the film is built on
character_gist: Kolkata-raised student forced by an accident to attend university in Mumbai rather than go to Canada, who falls in love and cannot say so because of his own pride.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: The other half of a romance stalled by two egos
character_gist: Young woman from a village in Uttarakhand who insists on studying in Mumbai, brings two friends together with Karan, and falls in love with him without either of them admitting it.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: The paternal authority around the heroine
character_gist: Senior figure of the heroine's family in the film's Uttarakhand strand.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Dr Siddharth Sinha's adopted son, who inherits his unfinished hospital
relationship_to_romance: His two relationships — with Neha and with Sonia — are the film's subject
