character_gist: Doctor at his adoptive father's hospital, in love with a colleague, who marries a rich man's manipulative daughter to fund the hospital after his father's death and operates on her when a crash leaves her brain-damaged.

relationship_to_protagonist: Buys the hospital Bachchan's Dr Sinha founded, and the man who runs it
relationship_to_romance: The purchased marriage against which the real romance is measured
character_gist: Spoilt heiress who decides she wants Akash and secures him with a financial agreement to fund the hospital, then proves jealous, mistrustful and controlling — and, after he saves her life, asks forgiveness and divorces him. Listed in the film's award tables for a negative role, with the result columns left blank.

relationship_to_protagonist: Doctor at the hospital Bachchan's Dr Sinha founded
relationship_to_romance: The film's genuine romance, set aside and finally resumed
character_gist: New doctor who falls for Akash, understands why he must marry elsewhere, agrees to break it off, and keeps working at the same hospital out of professionalism until he is free.

relationship_to_protagonist: Funds the hospital Bachchan's Dr Sinha died trying to complete
relationship_to_romance: His money is the price of the marriage
character_gist: Wealthy father who agrees to finance the hospital on condition that Akash marries his daughter.

relationship_to_protagonist: The film's protagonist; Bachchan contributes narration only — father narrating a film his son leads
relationship_to_romance: Carries the film's romance with the Thakur's sister
character_gist: Grandson working in Mumbai who returns to the newly electrified village with a satellite dish and a television, transforming its life — and whose love for the Thakur's sister brings the landlord down on the whole village.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: The film's romance, and the cause of the landlord's fury
character_gist: The Chotey Thakur's sister, in love with the young man from Mumbai — a match her brother threatens to destroy the village over.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: The opposition to the romance
character_gist: Village landlord untroubled by television until the priest tells him his sister is in love with the man who brought it, whereupon he threatens to destroy them both in front of a live broadcast.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Companion in the village comedy that follows the arrival of satellite television.

relationship_to_protagonist: One of the three gangsters Bachchan's Bade Mia leads
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance; the film has none for Bachchan's role
character_gist: The brother who stole the diamonds bound for Dubai, whose failed handover sets the whole hunt in motion.

relationship_to_protagonist: The second of the trio under Bachchan's Bade Mia
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: The middle brother of the gangster trio pursuing the models for the scattered diamonds.

relationship_to_protagonist: One of the three models Bachchan's Bade Mia plays cat and mouse with
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: One of India's three most successful models, blamed with her friends for the failed diamond heist and ordered to recover the stones.

relationship_to_protagonist: Second of the three models pursued by Bachchan's Bade Mia
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Model tripped on the catwalk by a rival, whose ensuing fight shakes hundreds of stolen diamonds out of the other woman's hair.

relationship_to_protagonist: Third of the models Bachchan's gangster hunts
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: The third of the model trio who confront the woman who tripped their friend and are then held responsible for the diamonds lost in the chaos.

relationship_to_protagonist: Figure in the underworld around Bachchan's Bade Mia
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Character who gives the film its title, in the criminal world pursuing the scattered diamonds.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Raj Malhotra's wife of forty years, separated from him by their sons
relationship_to_romance: The film's romance is this marriage, and the separation is what proves it
character_gist: Wife of forty years, split from her husband when the four sons agree to take one parent each for six months. Abused by one household, she is repaid with love by the granddaughter she saves from an attempted rape, and refuses her sons' apology at the end.

relationship_to_protagonist: The orphan Bachchan's Raj educated, and the only son who repays him
relationship_to_romance: Outside the marriage plot
character_gist: Orphan given money and education by Raj and raised as his own, who venerates him, takes the couple into his home when he meets them changing trains, and is declared their only son at the end.

relationship_to_protagonist: The eldest of the four sons who split Bachchan's Raj from his wife
relationship_to_romance: Part of the arrangement that separates the couple
character_gist: Eldest son, in whose household Pooja is abused by his wife and daughter, and one of the four who come to the book launch to ask forgiveness and are disowned.

relationship_to_protagonist: Wife of the adopted son who takes Bachchan's Raj in
relationship_to_romance: Part of the household that treats the couple as the sons would not
character_gist: Alok's wife, who with him cares for the elderly couple far better than their own sons did, and is declared their only daughter-in-law.

relationship_to_protagonist: The friend who publishes what Bachchan's Raj writes
relationship_to_romance: Publishes the account of the marriage that restores the couple's independence
character_gist: Cafe owner befriended during Raj's stay with one son, who has his writings published as the novel Baghban — the success that frees the couple from their children.

relationship_to_protagonist: The granddaughter who turns from contempt to devotion
relationship_to_romance: Outside the marriage plot
character_gist: Granddaughter who joins in mistreating Pooja and repents completely after Pooja saves her from a rape attempt by her boyfriend; she and her cousin refuse to attend the sons' apology.

relationship_to_protagonist: The film's protagonist; Bachchan contributes narration only
relationship_to_romance: Outside the two younger romances
character_gist: Accomplice of the two security guards suspected of stealing the emperor's crown, who flees with them, crashes into a wall and is transported to the 10th century and the palace of Emperor Babushah.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: Father of the two princesses in the film's romances
character_gist: In a double role: the notorious Mumbai thief who challenges an exhibitor and steals the crown, and the 10th-century emperor whose daughters the time travellers fall in love with.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: One of the two romances with the emperor's daughters
character_gist: Security guard suspected of the theft, thrown back a thousand years, who falls in love with a princess and loses her when her father takes her home.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: Half of one of the two time-crossed romances
character_gist: The emperor's second daughter, who travels to the 21st century with the men and is taken back to the 10th by her father.

relationship_to_protagonist: The corrupt officer on Bachchan's DCP's team, who tries to hand over their prisoner
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Morally corrupt senior inspector assigned to the escort, who attempts to surrender the prisoner to the attackers and is overruled at gunpoint by a rookie, then escapes with him when the revelation comes.
performance_recognition: Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actor nomination

relationship_to_protagonist: The ex-policeman Bachchan's DCP once jailed, now hunting his convoy
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Ruthless ex-inspector suspended and imprisoned after the DCP caught him killing five innocent men in a fake encounter, who now tracks the team across the state and beats him when he corners them.
performance_recognition: Filmfare Award for Best Villain nomination; IIFA Best Performance in a Negative Role nomination

relationship_to_protagonist: The witness who joins Bachchan's DCP's convoy
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance; the film scores 1 for centrality
character_gist: Schoolteacher who tells the police team about the terrorists who stayed incognito on her school premises, and travels to Mumbai with them.

relationship_to_protagonist: The prisoner Bachchan's DCP is escorting, and the film's central reversal
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Doctor framed as an ISI agent by corrupt police, who breaks down mid-journey and reveals that the terrorists are there to kill him, not free him — because he refused to suppress post-mortem reports exposing a minister's engineered riots.

relationship_to_protagonist: The superior who assembled Bachchan's DCP's team and betrayed it
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Deputy Inspector General who picks the five-man escort and is revealed by a phone call to be in league with the minister and the ex-policeman hunting them.

relationship_to_protagonist: Wife of Bachchan's DCP Anant Kumar Shrivastav
relationship_to_romance: A spouse-only role, scored Minor with no pairing record
character_gist: The veteran DCP's wife, at home while he takes what is meant to be a routine escort assignment.

relationship_to_protagonist: The man Bachchan's Dr Malhotra tries to keep away from his daughter
relationship_to_romance: The film's romance and its threat are the same person
character_gist: Obsessive young man who pursues Ria from the night his gang runs her over, burns the portrait he made of her to prove nothing is more beautiful than she is, beats a prostitute who teases him, and turns out to have burnt his own alcoholic father alive for killing his mother.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Dr Malhotra's daughter, whom he protects to the point of estrangement
relationship_to_romance: The film's romance, and the reason father and daughter break
character_gist: College student terrified and then captivated by her pursuer, who defends his innocence to her parents, accuses her father of being overprotective because of her dead brother, and tells them she hates them.

relationship_to_protagonist: Wife of Bachchan's Dr Malhotra
relationship_to_romance: A spouse-only role, scored Minor with no pairing record
character_gist: Ria's mother, impressed by the young man at first meeting where her husband is not, and who slaps her daughter when she turns on them.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Dr Malhotra's friend and colleague in Goa
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Fellow doctor and friend in the Goa practice where Ranveer treats the woman who later identifies Aryan as her attacker.

relationship_to_protagonist: The film's protagonist; Bachchan contributes narration only
relationship_to_romance: His partnership with the researcher is the film's central relationship
character_gist: Man with intuitive and healing powers developed through meditation, a devotee of Hanuman who trains by day and works as a club bouncer by night, and becomes the subject of a paranormal researcher's study.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: The film's pairing, professional before it is romantic
character_gist: Indian American paranormal researcher at the University of California studying possession, magic and healing, who brings her team to India, makes Varun her subject, and sets out with him for Ravana's ruins in Sri Lanka.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Labour contractor on the excavation team who is transformed into a Rakshasa by the Rudraksha's power, and who communicates mentally with Varun trying to join their abilities.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Saint and Varun's father, on the spiritual side of a story about a seed carrying powers that can transmute humans into a new species.

relationship_to_protagonist: The film's first protagonist; Bachchan contributes narration only
relationship_to_romance: His marriage is the relationship the assault destroys
character_gist: IAS officer whose wife is sexually assaulted by a minister's son, who is refused an FIR by the police, turned away by the Governor, and offered only an apology by the Chief Minister — and who kills himself when the goons begin terrorising his family.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: The marriage at the centre of the injustice
character_gist: Wife whose assault, and her naming of the culprit, sets off a case that the police, the Governor and the Chief Minister all refuse to pursue.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: His girlfriend's evidence reopens the case
character_gist: Young IPS officer assigned with a colleague to the suicide case, who learns how hard justice is to obtain when the accused is the son of an influential Home Minister.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Home Minister whose son commits the assault, and whose influence shields him through a dismissed case until fresh evidence reopens it and a warrant is issued for them both.

relationship_to_protagonist: The young man Bachchan's Dev unwittingly wounds, who then tries to kill him
relationship_to_romance: His relationship with Aaliya is the film's romance
character_gist: Law graduate raised on non-violence who watches his father die at a peace demonstration, is taken up by a communal politician, trained with guns and sent to kill the police commissioner — and later delivers the package that explodes near a Hindu temple.

relationship_to_protagonist: The witness who dares to testify in the case Bachchan's Dev pursues
relationship_to_romance: The film's romance, overtaken by the riots
character_gist: Young woman described as the light in Farhaan's life, caught in extraordinary circumstances that transform her and who stands up for the truth.
performance_recognition: Filmfare Award for Best Actress (Critics)

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Dev's lifelong friend, and his opposite on where the law should bend
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Special Commissioner who acts as the balancing force between the Chief Minister's political interests and his friend's commitment to the law — the two men lifelong friends with irreconcilable ideals.

relationship_to_protagonist: The political power Bachchan's Dev answers to and resists
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Chief Minister who treats an assassination attempt as licence to root out terrorist elements, and whose ruthless instruction is carried out against a whole community.

relationship_to_protagonist: Wife of Bachchan's Dev Pratap Singh
relationship_to_romance: A spouse-only role, scored Minor with no pairing record
character_gist: The commissioner's wife, at home through the riots and the killings his force is instructed not to prevent.

relationship_to_protagonist: The officer Bachchan's Colonel Damle commands at Kargil
relationship_to_romance: His relationship with Romi is the film's romance, broken by his own drift
character_gist: Aimless Delhi youth who applies to the army on a friend's suggestion, deserts the academy in the night, is shamed by his father's disappointment and his girlfriend's contempt, returns to accept his punishment, and is commissioned and posted to Kargil.

relationship_to_protagonist: No direct connection to Bachchan's Colonel; attached to the officer he commands
relationship_to_romance: The film's romance, ended by her and unresolved when war breaks out
character_gist: Focused, aspiring journalist who urges her boyfriend toward a direction in life and breaks with him over his lack of conviction; the cast list records the character as based on Barkha Dutt. She is about to be engaged elsewhere when the fighting starts.

relationship_to_protagonist: Senior soldier in the battalion Bachchan's Colonel Damle commands
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Subedar major of 3 Punjab, among the experienced soldiers around the young officer at the Line of Control.

relationship_to_protagonist: Father of the officer Bachchan's Colonel commands
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Wealthy father who disapproves of his son joining the army and, when he deserts, tells him to give up and join the family business.

relationship_to_protagonist: Company commander under Bachchan's Colonel Damle
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Officer commanding A Company of 3 Punjab in the assault on Point 5179, the peak dominating the army's supply route on National Highway 1D.

relationship_to_protagonist: Son of Bachchan's Major Ranvir Kaul, and the film's active protagonist while his father is imprisoned
relationship_to_romance: Carries the film's only romance, with Jabbar's daughter Radhika
character_gist: Son who sets off into Pakistan to find the father held for 33 years, infiltrates an army office block in a stolen courier uniform, steals the plans showing a water main under the prison, and coordinates the escape date with his father by code.

relationship_to_protagonist: Fellow prisoner who escapes, meets the son, and deliberately gets himself re-arrested to carry word back to Bachchan's Kaul
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: The one prisoner who clears the minefield alive. Rescued by Gaurav, he chooses with great reluctance to be captured again so he can tell Kaul his son is in Pakistan and that a water main runs beneath the jail.

relationship_to_protagonist: Warden of Saran Jail and Bachchan's direct captor and tormentor
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Cunning and sadistic camp warden who sighs with amusement as escaping prisoners are blown apart on his minefield, runs a planted spy among the POWs, and correctly reads Khan's voluntary return as a signal that something is coming.

relationship_to_protagonist: Daughter of the sympathetic Pakistani friend who first carries a letter out for Bachchan's Kaul
relationship_to_romance: The film's romantic lead, opposite the son rather than opposite Bachchan
character_gist: Jabbar's daughter and Gaurav's love interest, placing the film's romance one generation below its protagonist and on the Pakistani side of the border the escape has to cross.

relationship_to_protagonist: Wife of Bachchan's Major Ranvir Kaul and mother of Gaurav
relationship_to_romance: Half of the film's established off-screen marriage; no courtship is dramatised
character_gist: Wife who petitions the Indian Army for the return of a husband missing since 1971 and is told the General's hands are tied. The film's cast list identifies her only by these relationships and gives her no character name, so Character is left blank.

relationship_to_protagonist: Sympathetic Pakistani who smuggles the prisoners' first letter home and later guides the son
relationship_to_romance: Father of the woman the son loves
character_gist: The Pakistani friend through whom a fleeing prisoner sends word to India, and who tells Gaurav his father has been moved to Saran Jail. Radhika's father.

relationship_to_protagonist: Plant inside Bachchan's own group of prisoners
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Passes as a captured Indian captain until the diggers find the real Captain Jatin's body in the debris beneath the prison. Exposed as Sohail's informer, he reports the tenth as the escape date, so Kaul and Khan move it to the ninth.

relationship_to_protagonist: Niece-figure who calls Bachchan's Raj Chauhan "Uncle" and works beside him at his Coorg orphanage
relationship_to_romance: The film's romantic lead
character_gist: University student with firm convictions about love and marriage who spends her time at the orphanage, falls for Arjun, is left heartbroken when he denies loving her, and finally marries him after a staged engagement forces his hand.

relationship_to_protagonist: The young man Bachchan's Raj sets out to teach a lesson about love
relationship_to_romance: The film's romantic lead
character_gist: Free-spirited introvert whose views on love are the opposite of Diya's. He refuses to admit his feelings, loses her, travels to the orphanage to apologise, and is manoeuvred into declaring himself by a marriage that turns out to be a fiction.

relationship_to_protagonist: Instrument of Bachchan's Raj Chauhan's plan
relationship_to_romance: Poses as Diya's fiancé to force Arjun to declare himself; the engagement is a device, not a rival romance
character_gist: Childhood friend Diya appears to be about to marry. The marriage is revealed as a ruse designed by Raj to teach Arjun to be honest about love and follow his heart.

relationship_to_protagonist: Father of the young man Bachchan's character is educating
relationship_to_romance: Head of the household where the romance begins
character_gist: Arjun's father and the friend of Diya's father with whom she stays in Mumbai, which is how the couple meet.

relationship_to_protagonist: No direct connection to Bachchan's Raj Chauhan
relationship_to_romance: Peripheral to the central pairing
character_gist: Figure in the Mumbai circle around Arjun and Diya; the article gives her no developed function in the main romance.

relationship_to_protagonist: Wife of Bachchan's Major Frank Williams and the film's point-of-view character
relationship_to_romance: Half of an established marriage; the film is a ghost story, not a romance
character_gist: Mother keeping a candle-lit house with the curtains permanently drawn because her children's eyes cannot bear sunlight. She hires three servants, senses a presence, then finds her letter to the employment agency still lying unposted in the mailbox.

relationship_to_protagonist: Separate strand from Bachchan's Frank Williams
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: The film's other veteran presence, in a strand away from the Williams house. Pairs Dharmendra with Bachchan again, three decades after their 1970s multi-starrers.

relationship_to_protagonist: One of the three servants whose arrival unsettles Bachchan's household
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Applies to be the butler and is hired, though no vacancy was ever advertised — the question of how she learnt of the post is the thread Sandra pulls.

relationship_to_protagonist: Daughter of Bachchan's Frank Williams
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Child who alone sees the house's other occupants and draws them — a man, his wife, their son Vicky and an old woman with magical powers — while her mother disbelieves her.

relationship_to_protagonist: Servant in Bachchan's household
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: The mute maid, one of the three who answer a vacancy that was never posted.

relationship_to_protagonist: Foster son of Bachchan's Chaudhary Sumer Singh, who with his wife raised him as their own
relationship_to_romance: The film's romantic lead; the love story is his
character_gist: Indian Air Force pilot who rescues Zaara after her bus crashes, brings her home for Lohri, then gives up his freedom rather than let Raza make her life a misery — serving twenty-two years as prisoner 786 without speaking his own name.

relationship_to_protagonist: The woman Bachchan's Bauji welcomes into his village home for Lohri
relationship_to_romance: The film's romantic lead
character_gist: Pakistani woman from a politically ambitious Lahore family who crosses to India to scatter her Sikh nanny's ashes, realises during her own wedding preparations that she loves Veer, and runs into his arms in front of her family.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's Bauji, who belongs entirely to the flashback
relationship_to_romance: The listener who recovers the love story and argues it in court
character_gist: Budding Pakistani lawyer given prisoner 786 as her first case. Addressing him by his real name breaks a twenty-two-year silence, and the film's whole romance is told to her.

relationship_to_protagonist: Wife of Bachchan's Chaudhary Sumer Singh
relationship_to_romance: Half of the film's settled older marriage, set against the young lovers; no courtship is dramatised and the workbook records no pairing row
character_gist: Veer's foster mother, who with Bauji took in an orphaned boy they could not have themselves and gave him the love the film treats as the source of his own capacity for sacrifice.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's Bauji
relationship_to_romance: The external opposition that destroys the romance
character_gist: Zaara's wealthy politician fiancé. Outraged and jealous, he has Veer arrested and offers him a choice: life imprisonment as a spy, or freedom bought by leaving Zaara to a life Raza promises to make hell.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's Bauji
relationship_to_romance: The family interest the marriage is meant to serve
character_gist: Zaara's father, whose political career the match with Raza is to advance, and who falls ill with shock when his daughter runs to Veer.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's Bauji
relationship_to_romance: Makes the appeal that separates the lovers
character_gist: Zaara's mother, who opposes the match and finally begs Veer to leave her daughter for her husband's health and reputation — a plea he honours, which is what puts him in Raza's hands.

relationship_to_protagonist: No connection to Bachchan's Bauji
relationship_to_romance: Sets the reunion in motion
character_gist: Zaara's friend, who secretly telephones Veer and begs him to come and take her away — the call that brings him to Pakistan.

character: Capt. Kunaljeet "Kunal" Singh / Lt Cdr. Vikramjeet "Vikram" Singh
relationship_to_protagonist: In a dual role as both the son and the grandson of Bachchan's Major General Amarjeet Singh
relationship_to_romance: Carries the film's romance, as Kunal
character_gist: As Vikram, the naval officer who saves a hundred trapped soldiers as his ship sinks. As his son Kunal, an officer who joins for a passport to America, fakes heroism for a medal, loses the woman he stayed for, and finally earns his grandfather's regard.

relationship_to_protagonist: Officer of the army Bachchan's General embodies, and the man whose marriage breaks Kunal's last tie to it
relationship_to_romance: Marries the woman Kunal loves
character_gist: Senior officer presumed dead who was in fact a prisoner of war. His return, and his marriage to Shweta, severs the one thread keeping Kunal in uniform.

relationship_to_protagonist: Daughter-in-law of Bachchan's Amarjeet Singh
relationship_to_romance: Half of the widowed older marriage behind the plot
character_gist: Vikramjeet's wife, widowed when his ship goes down in the 1971 war, and mother of the grandson who inherits neither man's sense of duty.

relationship_to_protagonist: No direct link to Bachchan's General; her marriage reshapes his grandson
relationship_to_romance: The woman at the centre of the film's romance, for whom Kunal stays in the army and whom Rajeev marries
character_gist: The woman Kunal falls in love with and remains in uniform to be near, who is found at the end to be married to his senior officer. Her Hindi dialogue was dubbed by Mona Ghosh Shetty.
performance_recognition: Nominated for the Bollywood Movie Award for Best Female Debut (2005), the only award listed in the film's article

relationship_to_protagonist: No direct connection to Bachchan's General
relationship_to_romance: A second attachment for Kunal, described only as friend then girlfriend
character_gist: Army doctor listed as Kunal's friend and later girlfriend; the article gives the relationship no development.

relationship_to_protagonist: Opposite number to the army Bachchan's General represents
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Senior officer on the other side of the border, in a film whose climax is a plot by terrorists and rebel Pakistani officers to bomb the Amarnath temple and provoke communal strife.

relationship_to_protagonist: Pupil of Bachchan's Debraj Sahai, and in the present-day frame his carer as he loses his own mind
relationship_to_romance: The film's central relationship is teacher and pupil; the workbook records no romance for it
character_gist: Deafblind and mute woman of 42 who lost sight, hearing and speech at two, grew into an uncontrollable child, and is drawn into language by Debraj. When he is diagnosed with Alzheimer's she refuses the prognosis and sets out to return him to himself.
performance_recognition: The film's accolades summary states Black won all four major Filmfare awards — Best Film, Best Director, Best Actor and Best Actress — the fifth film to do so, and 11 trophies in all; the summary names the categories rather than the recipients

relationship_to_protagonist: The child Bachchan's Debraj takes on, and half of the film's long central flashback
relationship_to_romance: Outside romance entirely
character_gist: The eight-year-old Michelle: violent, raging against a world nothing reaches, and the pupil on whom Debraj gives up salary, allowance and alcohol in exchange for time and trust.

relationship_to_protagonist: The parent who keeps Bachchan's Debraj in the house against her husband's orders
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Michelle's mother, at her wits' end with a daughter she cannot control. She grudgingly lets Debraj stay on during Paul's twenty-day absence, fearing the alternative is a mental hospital.

relationship_to_protagonist: The opposition to Bachchan's methods inside the household
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Michelle's father, who disapproves of Debraj's harshness and orders him out of the house, believing him gone while the teaching continues behind his back.

relationship_to_protagonist: Sister of Bachchan's pupil
relationship_to_romance: Her wedding is a setting rather than a romance the film develops
character_gist: Michelle's younger sister, born while her parents are struggling to contain her, and one of the three who find the lost Debraj by the fountain in the present-day frame.

relationship_to_protagonist: Son of Bachchan's Ishwar Chandra Thakur; the film is the quarrel between them
relationship_to_romance: Carries the film's romance, with Pooja
character_gist: Spoilt son who wants to be a film actor, elopes with his father's rival's daughter, is thrown out of the house, takes work as a stuntman, and learns what his father was doing only when he discovers the lung cancer being hidden from him.

relationship_to_protagonist: Daughter-in-law of Bachchan's Ishwar, and daughter of his business rival
relationship_to_romance: The film's romantic lead, opposite the son
character_gist: Daughter of Ishwar's rival Nattu, secretly married to Aditya. Her pregnancy is what decides his parents to force him into responsibility, and she is turned out of the house with him.

relationship_to_protagonist: Wife of Bachchan's Ishwar Chandra Thakur and joint owner of the toy factory
relationship_to_romance: Half of the film's established marriage; the closing image is hers
character_gist: Wife who scolds Ishwar for indulging their son and joins the decision to turn him out. The film ends on her, as her dead husband's spirit touches the flowers in her hair. Billed in the cast list as Shefali Shetty Shah.

relationship_to_protagonist: Business rival of Bachchan's Ishwar and father of his daughter-in-law
relationship_to_romance: The family obstacle to the marriage, on the bride's side
character_gist: Pooja's father and Ishwar's rival, the man whose daughter the son elopes with — the conflict that sets the two households against each other.

relationship_to_protagonist: Servant in Bachchan's household
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Ishwar's servant, present through the campaign of small cruelties — the removed fuse, the food withheld — by which the father drives his son towards adulthood.

relationship_to_protagonist: Wife of Bachchan's rival
relationship_to_romance: Mother of the bride
character_gist: Pooja's mother, on the far side of the feud between the two families.

relationship_to_protagonist: The con man Bachchan's JCP Dashrath Singh spends the film pursuing, and finally lets go
relationship_to_romance: Half of the film's central couple, who marry and have a son mid-spree
character_gist: Small-town aspirant from Fursatgunj who runs from a railway job, has his business idea stolen, avenges it with an elaborate con, and becomes half of a celebrated pair of swindlers before deciding his son should not inherit the life.
performance_recognition: Won the Bollywood Movie Award and the Screen Award for Best Actor in a Comic Role; nominated for the Filmfare and Zee Cine Awards for Best Actor; shared the Screen Award for Jodi No. 1 with Rani Mukerji

relationship_to_protagonist: The other half of the pair Bachchan's policeman hunts
relationship_to_romance: Half of the film's central couple
character_gist: Would-be fashion designer from Pankinagar who runs from a queue of suitors, fails in Mumbai, and turns con artist with Rakesh. It is she who first weighs what their life will mean for their son.
performance_recognition: Nominated for the Filmfare, IIFA and Zee Cine Awards for Best Actress; shared the Screen Award for Jodi No. 1 with Abhishek Bachchan

relationship_to_protagonist: No direct dealings with Bachchan's policeman
relationship_to_romance: The pressure the hero runs from, and the home the couple return to
character_gist: Ticket-examiner father pressing his son towards a government railway job — the pressure that sends Rakesh out of Fursatgunj, and the household the couple come back to at the end.

relationship_to_protagonist: Appears opposite Bachchan and his son in the film's best-known song
relationship_to_romance: Outside the plot's romance
character_gist: Special appearance as the dancer in "Kajra Re", the number that put her on screen with both Bachchans and became the film's signature.
performance_recognition: Won the MTV Immies award for Best Performance in a Song – Female for "Kajra Re"

relationship_to_protagonist: No direct dealings with Bachchan's policeman
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: The man who pitches Rakesh's own business idea as his own and gets it approved. Duping him is the con that starts the spree.

relationship_to_protagonist: No direct dealings with Bachchan's policeman
relationship_to_romance: The marriage pressure the heroine runs from
character_gist: Vimmi's father, whose procession of prospective grooms drives her out of Pankinagar.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan narrates the film and does not appear in the story; Shekhar is its protagonist
relationship_to_romance: The film's romantic lead
character_gist: Rebellious musician son of a shrewd businessman, in love with Lalita and consumed by jealousy of Girish. Believing her married, he turns cold and bitter, and his self-hatred drives the second half.
performance_recognition: Nominated for the Filmfare Award for Best Actor

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan, whose role is the narration over the opening credits
relationship_to_romance: The film's romantic lead
character_gist: Orphaned girl raised in Gurcharan's household next door, a singer with unflinching love for Shekhar, who keeps her dignity through insult and resigns herself to circumstance when the haveli debt threatens her family.
performance_recognition: Won the Filmfare Award for Best Female Debut; nominated for the Filmfare Award for Best Actress

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narrator
relationship_to_romance: The third point of the triangle, and the man wrongly assumed to be Lalita's husband
character_gist: Straightforward steel businessman from London who supports Vasundhara's family after Gurcharan's death, is taken with Lalita, and quietly settles the debt on the ancestral haveli.
performance_recognition: Nominated for the Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actor

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narrator
relationship_to_romance: The arranged match set against the love story
character_gist: Beautiful and devious industrialist's daughter whom Shekhar's father wants him to marry, and whose wedding night opens the film with Lalita's voice running through the groom's head.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narrator
relationship_to_romance: The external opposition to the romance
character_gist: Shekhar's shrewd, conniving father, who holds the mortgage on Gurcharan's haveli and plans to take it over and sell it as a hotel — the scheme Lalita stumbles on at his own office.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan, though both appear in the same film for the first time since the 1980s
relationship_to_romance: A musical set piece outside the plot
character_gist: Special appearance in the song "Kaisi Paheli Zindagaani", staged as a 1960s Calcutta cabaret number.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's shepherd is the figure who resolves the riddle these two halves create
relationship_to_romance: The film's romance, on both sides of it, in a dual role
character_gist: In a dual role: the dutiful merchant's son who leaves his bride on their wedding night for a five-year business trip, and the ghost who takes his shape out of desire for her and becomes the husband she wants.
performance_recognition: Nominated for the Zee Cine Award and the Screen Award for Best Actor

relationship_to_protagonist: The woman whose choice Bachchan's Gadariya is finally asked to adjudicate
relationship_to_romance: The film's romantic lead and the one making its central choice
character_gist: Rajasthani bride abandoned on her wedding night, who knowingly takes the ghost wearing her husband's face as hers — the film's dilemma is her decision between the man she is married to and the one who wants her.

relationship_to_protagonist: No dealings with Bachchan's shepherd
relationship_to_romance: The paternal authority that causes the separation
character_gist: Wealthy merchant whose insistence that his son leave on an auspicious date empties the marriage bed, and who later accepts the impostor home for five gold coins a morning.

relationship_to_protagonist: No dealings with Bachchan's shepherd
relationship_to_romance: The parallel case of a wife left behind
character_gist: Kishanlal's aunt, who consoles the abandoned Lachchi out of her own experience: her husband Sunderlal vanished without a word to the family.

relationship_to_protagonist: No dealings with Bachchan's shepherd
relationship_to_romance: The flaw that threatens to expose the substitution
character_gist: Kishanlal's servant, and the ghost's one blunder: he cannot account for a letter arriving from a master who is supposedly at home.

relationship_to_protagonist: Frames the tale in which Bachchan appears
relationship_to_romance: Narrates the romance rather than taking part in it
character_gist: Voice of one of the two puppets who narrate the film — a voice-only credit, as Bachchan's own narration credits elsewhere in this filmography are.

relationship_to_protagonist: Frames the tale in which Bachchan appears
relationship_to_romance: Narrates the romance rather than taking part in it
character_gist: Voice of the second narrating puppet, opposite Naseeruddin Shah's.

relationship_to_protagonist: Younger son of Bachchan's Subhash Nagre, and the son who believes in him absolutely
relationship_to_romance: Carries the film's only romantic thread, with Pooja, and breaks it off over her doubts about his father
character_gist: Son returned from the United States who keeps faith in his father when everyone else believes the murder charge, takes over as Sarkar while he is imprisoned, and ends the film having killed his own brother to hold the house together.
performance_recognition: Won the Filmfare, IIFA and Zee Cine Awards for Best Supporting Actor; nominated for the Bollywood Movie Award and the Screen Award in the same category

relationship_to_protagonist: Elder son of Bachchan's Sarkar, expelled from the house and finally turned assassin against him
relationship_to_romance: His pursuit of the actress Sapna is the film's counter-image to romance: he is more interested in her than in his wife
character_gist: Sleazy producer son who murders the actor sleeping with Sapna, is thrown out, returns feigning repentance, and is talked into approaching his bedridden father in the dark with intent to kill.
performance_recognition: Nominated for the Filmfare Award for Best Performance in a Negative Role, the Zee Cine Award in the same category, the Screen Award for Best Actor in a Negative Role and the Bollywood Movie Award for Best Villain

relationship_to_protagonist: Wife of Bachchan's Subhash Nagre
relationship_to_romance: A spouse-only role: the marriage is established and undramatised, and the workbook records no pairing row for it
character_gist: Wife at the centre of the Nagre household through the arrest, the attempt on her husband's life in prison and the war between their two sons.

relationship_to_protagonist: Her doubts about Bachchan's Sarkar are what cost her the relationship
relationship_to_romance: The film's romantic interest, opposite the son
character_gist: Shankar's love, brought back from the United States with him, whose misgivings about his father's image lead him to break with her. Her voice was dubbed by Mona Ghosh Shetty.
performance_recognition: Nominated for the Zee Cine Award for Most Promising Debut – Female

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's most outspoken public critic, and the man whose murder is pinned on him
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Upright political leader of non-violent conviction and a declared opponent of Sarkar. He is assassinated precisely so that the killing can be laid at Sarkar's door.

relationship_to_protagonist: Former associate of Bachchan's Sarkar who turns on him
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Old associate who allies with Rasheed, is asked by Shankar for help against the plot to kill his father, and reveals the betrayal at the moment it costs Khansaab his life.

relationship_to_protagonist: The Dubai don whose deal Bachchan's Sarkar refuses on moral grounds
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Dubai-based don whose proposal Sarkar rejects and forbids him to pursue alone. He assembles the coalition that frames Sarkar and works on Vishnu to murder him.
performance_recognition: Nominated for the Bollywood Movie Award for Best Villain

relationship_to_protagonist: Described in the cast list as Bachchan's Sarkar's best friend and confidant
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Chief Minister and Sarkar's closest political ally, the relationship that shows how far the protagonist's authority reaches into the state.

relationship_to_protagonist: Wife of Bachchan's Vidhyadhar Patwardhan
relationship_to_romance: The film's one relationship, recorded in the workbook as PAIR-089 — a long middle-class marriage tested by the killing of their son
character_gist: Mother of the murdered Amar and the other half of the couple the film is built on: a middle-class marriage that has to absorb a son's death, a false drug charge against his name and a husband who decides to seek justice with a gun.
performance_recognition: Nominated for the Filmfare Award for Best Actress

relationship_to_protagonist: Son of Bachchan's Vidhyadhar, and the film's narrator in its opening
relationship_to_romance: His own engagement to Jenny is the household's happiness before the death
character_gist: Son working in London who comes home to announce his marriage to Jenny, is mortally wounded outside a pub trying to stop a killer, and dies in hospital on the night of his own surprise birthday party.

relationship_to_protagonist: The one ally Bachchan's Vidhyadhar has once the law fails him
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Reformed goon and mechanic known to the Patwardhans, who decides to help them and procures the gun Vidhyadhar carries into Harshwardhan's office.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Vidhyadhar bails her out and sends her to safety
relationship_to_romance: Half of the film's younger, interrupted romance
character_gist: Amar's girlfriend from London, whom the police try to implicate as his accomplice and threaten with rape. Carrying his child, she is bailed out by Vidhyadhar and sent back to London.

relationship_to_protagonist: The killer of Bachchan's son, and the man he shoots
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Minister's son who murders in front of a witness and walks free as the police bury the case. He confesses arrogantly to Vidhyadhar's face, not knowing a pocket recorder is running — the evidence that exonerates father and son both.

relationship_to_protagonist: Part of the world that closes against Bachchan's family
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: One of the figures around the cover-up, in a film whose subject is an ordinary family finding every institution ranged against it.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan appears as himself in a guest capacity; Ramji is the film's protagonist
relationship_to_romance: Carries the film's romance, by way of a marriage of convenience
character_gist: Bihari cook who goes to London to earn his sister's dowry, is left jobless when his employer dies before signing the papers, works illegally, and marries a British citizen for papers — converting to Christianity as Robert.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's guest appearance as himself
relationship_to_romance: The film's romantic lead, in a marriage that begins as a legal fiction
character_gist: The lawyer's girlfriend who marries Ramji over a weekend so he can stay in Britain, then prepares with him for the consulate interview by learning who he actually is.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's guest appearance
relationship_to_romance: Pushes the hero into the marriage of convenience
character_gist: Restaurant owner who employs Ramji without a work permit, prospers on his cooking, and presses him into the fake marriage so that he has a defence in the case over hiring illegal workers.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's guest appearance
relationship_to_romance: Owns the marriage scheme and is exposed by it
character_gist: Cunning lawyer who proposes that Ramji marry his own girlfriend, charges Guru heavily for it, and is undone when Ramji meets the ex-wife he abandoned along with their son.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's guest appearance
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Comic figure in the London Indian circle the film moves through.

relationship_to_protagonist: Wife of Bachchan's Shekhar Sinha
relationship_to_romance: A spouse-only role with no pairing record; her objection is the obstacle the romance has to clear
character_gist: Mother who disapproves of her son's Roman Catholic Franco-Mauritian beloved on grounds of faith and tells him to end it, and whose asthma is the reason he submits to an engagement he does not want. Billed in the cast list as Revathi Nair.

relationship_to_protagonist: Son of Bachchan's Shekhar Sinha
relationship_to_romance: The film's romantic lead
character_gist: Son who goes to Stockholm to study cookery, falls in love with Sophie, is rejected by her father on ethnic grounds and by his own mother on religious ones, and fails to appear at the church for their planned elopement.

relationship_to_protagonist: Betrothed to the son of Bachchan's Shekhar to satisfy his wife's wish
relationship_to_romance: The arranged match who chooses to dismantle her own engagement
character_gist: The woman Jai becomes engaged to for his mother's sake. Learning of his love for Sophie, she invents a false pregnancy for Sophie that forces both families to accept the couple, and leaves Mauritius as the film ends.

relationship_to_protagonist: The woman Bachchan's Shekhar is willing to accept and his wife is not
relationship_to_romance: The film's romantic lead
character_gist: Roman Catholic Franco-Mauritian woman who meets Jai in Stockholm, is refused by both families, waits at a church he never reaches, and returns to her parents to marry the man they have chosen.

relationship_to_protagonist: The counterpart to Bachchan's Shekhar on the other side of the match, and the harsher of the two fathers
relationship_to_romance: The external opposition to the romance
character_gist: Large Mauritian landowner who disapproves of Jai instantly because of his ethnicity — the film's sharpest statement of the communal and religious divisions it sets against the couple.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan appears as himself in a guest capacity in this Kannada film; Puru is its protagonist
relationship_to_romance: Half of the film's central marriage
character_gist: Husband who behaves like a suitor years into the marriage: a miser set against his spendthrift wife, wanting to build a house before they have a child.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's guest appearance as himself
relationship_to_romance: Half of the film's central marriage
character_gist: Wife who wants a child and a family before a house, against a husband who wants the reverse — the quarrel the film uses to look at modern marriage and the emptiness of a large home without a large family in it.
performance_recognition: Nominated for the Filmfare Award for Best Actress – Kannada at the 53rd Filmfare Awards South

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's guest appearance
relationship_to_romance: Peripheral to the marriage
character_gist: Puru's colleague, one of the circle of friends around the couple.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's guest appearance
relationship_to_romance: Family around the marriage
character_gist: Amritha's mother; the cast list gives her no name beyond the relationship.

relationship_to_protagonist: Friend and former comrade of Bachchan's Col. Suryaveer Singh, who hires him and is revealed as the enemy
relationship_to_romance: Outside romance; the film has none
character_gist: The former comrade who brings Surya to Bangkok to guard a child, and turns out to have staged the kidnappings — using Surya to eliminate his own enemies, and dying at his hands once the design is clear.

relationship_to_protagonist: The child Bachchan's Surya is hired to protect, and the one who breaks through his bitterness
relationship_to_romance: Outside romance; the film's central bond is guardian and child
character_gist: Girl whose swimming meet the alcoholic ex-officer is coaxed into helping her train for, and whose kidnapping he is injured trying to prevent. The film's whole plot runs on her. Billed as Baby Rucha Vaidya; she also plays the young Jodhaa in FILM-193.

relationship_to_protagonist: Mother of the child in Bachchan's charge; he spends the rest of his life with the two of them
relationship_to_romance: The film ends with Surya living with mother and daughter, but the article frames it as guardianship rather than romance, and the workbook records no pairing
character_gist: Mother of the kidnapped girl, in the NRI household in Bangkok that engages Surya.

relationship_to_protagonist: The father who cannot do what Bachchan's Surya does
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Father unable to raise the ransom for his own daughter, and whose lawyer Chang proves to be part of the conspiracy behind her abduction.

relationship_to_protagonist: Plays the grown woman Bachchan's Surya raised, in the closing scene
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: The adult Anamika of the epilogue, fifteen years on, now with a bodyguard of her own and Surya as his mentor.

relationship_to_protagonist: Special appearance as the bodyguard Bachchan's Surya mentors
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Special appearance as the new bodyguard in the epilogue — one of several films in this stretch that put father and son in the same frame.

relationship_to_protagonist: The innocent man Bachchan's Viren Sahi shoots, setting the plot going
relationship_to_romance: Half of the film's settled young marriage
character_gist: Kind-hearted canteen owner searching the city for his runaway younger brother. He stops to help the wounded at a cinema stampede, is shot by Viren as one of Khan's men, and dies after being struck by Viren's car.

relationship_to_protagonist: The antagonist of Bachchan's antagonist: he kidnaps the don's family to force him to justice
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Younger brother whose running away causes the death, and who forms a gang to abduct Viren's entire family — refusing to harm them because he knows what a family is worth, the film's moral counterweight to Bachchan's don.

relationship_to_protagonist: Son of Bachchan's Viren, and finally the man who orders his father's killing
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: The don's spoilt son, whose beating by a rival starts the revenge. He escapes captivity, accidentally shoots his own mother while aiming at Aryan, and arranges for corrupt police to kill his father in a staged encounter.

relationship_to_protagonist: Wife of Bachchan's Viren Sahi
relationship_to_romance: A spouse-only role with no pairing record
character_gist: The don's wife, held with the rest of the family and killed by a shot from her own son's gun. Her cremation is the point at which Viren decides to surrender.

relationship_to_protagonist: Widow of the man Bachchan's Viren kills
relationship_to_romance: Half of the film's settled young marriage
character_gist: Doctor married to Shekhar, widowed by the shooting outside the cinema.

relationship_to_protagonist: Arch-rival of Bachchan's Viren Sahi
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: The rival don who has Viren's son attacked, and whose nephew Viren travels from Bangkok to India to kill — the errand that kills Shekhar instead.

relationship_to_protagonist: The one actor in this anthology who plays opposite Bachchan: his biotechnology student, in the Ram Gopal Varma segment
relationship_to_romance: Outside romance; the segment is a two-hander
character_gist: Student taking tuition at Professor Sunil Khanna's home, increasingly unnerved as his teacher keeps pointing out someone in the kitchen, the dining room, on the sofa — until the professor walks him to the mirror.

relationship_to_protagonist: Frames the segment Bachchan appears in, without sharing scenes with him
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: The old woman in the deserted forest house who agrees to tell five lost children six scary stories — the framing device that contains Bachchan's story as its first.

relationship_to_protagonist: Leads a different segment and shares no scenes with Bachchan
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Lead of one of the film's six separately directed stories. The anthology structure means his and Bachchan's work never meet on screen.

relationship_to_protagonist: Leads a different segment and shares no scenes with Bachchan
relationship_to_romance: His segment has a wife; the main film has no romance
character_gist: Lead of another of the six stories, played opposite Sonali Kulkarni as his wife.

relationship_to_protagonist: Leads a different segment and shares no scenes with Bachchan
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Photographer, and a spirit, in his own segment of the anthology.

relationship_to_protagonist: Appears in a different segment and shares no scenes with Bachchan
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: One of the film's segment leads, in the same year she appeared as herself in Bachchan's Viruddh.

relationship_to_protagonist: No family tie to Bachchan's Sam; the two men's households are joined by the affair
relationship_to_romance: The film's romantic lead, in the adulterous central relationship
character_gist: Soccer player whose career ends under a car on the day he first meets Maya. Embittered, jealous of his wife's success and unable to reach his son, he finds in Maya a shared marital unhappiness that becomes an affair.

relationship_to_protagonist: Daughter-in-law of Bachchan's Sam Talwar, who on his deathbed tells her to leave his son
relationship_to_romance: The film's romantic lead
character_gist: Orphaned schoolteacher who marries her closest friend without loving him, struggles with infertility and emotional distance, and meets Dev by chance on her wedding day. A few of her lines were dubbed by Mona Ghosh Shetty.

relationship_to_protagonist: Son of Bachchan's Samarjit Talwar
relationship_to_romance: The husband displaced by the affair, and the one who finally forgives
character_gist: Son raised by a widowed, flamboyant father, married to a woman who cannot reach him. He divorces Maya after her confession, then visits her years later to say he has forgiven her and is marrying again.
performance_recognition: Won the Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actor; the film led the 52nd Filmfare Awards with 23 nominations

relationship_to_protagonist: No direct tie to Bachchan's Sam; her mother-in-law becomes his friend
relationship_to_romance: The wife the affair is conducted against
character_gist: Fashion magazine editor whose success her husband resents. She turns down a London promotion for her family's sake, and after the confession divorces Dev and keeps both her son and her mother-in-law.

relationship_to_protagonist: The friend Bachchan's Sam Talwar makes, and the person beside him when he discovers the affair
relationship_to_romance: The friendship between the two older parents runs parallel to the young couples' collapse; the article frames it as friendship and the workbook records no pairing for Bachchan's Sam
character_gist: Dev's widowed mother, who befriends Sam, and with him walks in on Dev and Maya embracing — the discovery that kills Sam that night. She stays with Rhea and her grandson afterwards.

relationship_to_protagonist: No direct tie to Bachchan's Sam
relationship_to_romance: The suspicion the husband's jealousy attaches to
character_gist: Rhea's boss, and the figure around whom Dev's insecurity about his wife's professional world gathers.

relationship_to_protagonist: The village woman whose marriage Bachchan's Thakur Vijay Singh proposes, and whose accuser is his son
relationship_to_romance: The film's romantic and marital centre
character_gist: Educated village woman accused of infidelity by her bridegroom on their wedding day. Cleared by Shankar's intervention, she marries him instead, and faces a hostile sister-in-law and a vengeful Ranjit in her new household.

relationship_to_protagonist: Set against Bachchan's Thakur household by defending Ganga twice
relationship_to_romance: The film's romantic lead
character_gist: Man who comes to Ganga's aid and is crippled for it, intervenes again to prove her innocent, and marries her — inheriting the enmity of the Thakur's son.

relationship_to_protagonist: Paired with Bachchan in the Thakur household of this Bhojpuri film
relationship_to_romance: No pairing record; the older couple's marriage is a given, not a story
character_gist: The senior woman of the Thakur family, in the first of two Bhojpuri films that put Bachchan and Hema Malini together under Deepak Sawant's production.

relationship_to_protagonist: Son of Bachchan's Thakur Vijay Singh, and the film's antagonist
relationship_to_romance: The failed bridegroom and the standing threat to the marriage that replaces his
character_gist: The Thakur's affluent son, chastised by Ganga at the river, then offered her hand by his own father. He accuses her of infidelity at the wedding and spends the rest of the film seeking revenge on the couple.

relationship_to_protagonist: Part of the village world around Bachchan's Thakur
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Bhojpuri star in a supporting turn; he also sings on the soundtrack of the sequel, Gangotri (FILM-192).

relationship_to_protagonist: Wife of Bachchan's Balraj Kapoor, and the household opposition to his plan
relationship_to_romance: A spouse-only role with no pairing record; her resistance is the obstacle to the remarriage her husband is arranging
character_gist: Mother who waits for her son's return from America and is broken by his death. She resists Balraj's proposal that their widowed daughter-in-law remarry, fearing she will lose her grandson.

relationship_to_protagonist: Only son of Bachchan's Balraj, whose death sets the film's argument going
relationship_to_romance: Half of the film's first romance, ended by his death
character_gist: Son who joins the family business, falls in love with and marries Millie, and is killed in a road accident returning from London on his own child's birthday. He reappears as a spirit at the end to bless his father's decision.
performance_recognition: Nominated, with Rani Mukerji, for the Screen Award for Jodi No. 1

relationship_to_protagonist: Widowed daughter-in-law of Bachchan's Balraj, whose future he makes his cause
relationship_to_romance: The centre of both romances — widowed from the first, remarried into the second
character_gist: Independent, spirited artist widowed young with an infant son. Her father-in-law's insistence that she has a right to happiness carries her into a second marriage with the friend who had stepped aside for her first.
performance_recognition: Nominated, with Salman Khan, for the Screen Award for Jodi No. 1

relationship_to_protagonist: The man Bachchan's Balraj seeks out in London and asks to marry his son's widow
relationship_to_romance: Half of the film's second romance
character_gist: Millie's childhood friend, who loved her silently and stepped aside when she chose Avinash. Called back from London by Balraj, he builds a bond with her son and marries her with the family's blessing.
performance_recognition: Nominated for the Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actor and the Bollywood Movie Award for Best Supporting Actor

relationship_to_protagonist: Elder brother of Bachchan's Balraj and the conservative voice against him
relationship_to_romance: The external opposition to the second marriage
character_gist: Conservative elder brother who holds widow remarriage unacceptable — the family authority Balraj has to argue down to get Millie married again.

relationship_to_protagonist: Widowed sister of Bachchan's Balraj and his brother Balwant
relationship_to_romance: A second widow in the same household, set silently against the one being given a new life
character_gist: The brothers' widowed sister — a presence that sharpens the film's argument, since she belongs to the generation for whom no second marriage was proposed.

relationship_to_protagonist: Revealed by his mother's letter to be the biological son of Bachchan's Eklavya, and the man Eklavya's oath finally requires him to face
relationship_to_romance: Carries the film's young romance, with Rajjo
character_gist: Heir who stayed away in London, brought home by his mother's death and the letter naming his real father. He orders the king's murder, confesses it to Rajjo and loses her, and ends the film opposite the guard sworn to kill the killer.

relationship_to_protagonist: The investigator moving through the fort Bachchan's Eklavya guards
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Irreverent police officer called in after the king receives a death threat over the telephone, and who arrives too late to prevent the shooting.

relationship_to_protagonist: Ordered to kill Bachchan's Eklavya, and killed by him
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: The king's brother, who pushes the atrocities against the farmers, is told to kill Eklavya and instead murders the king and his driver. Cornered, he tells Eklavya that the prince ordered the killing, and is killed for it.

relationship_to_protagonist: The king Bachchan's Eklavya exists to protect, and whose wife bore Eklavya's son
relationship_to_romance: Husband in the marriage the film's central secret betrays
character_gist: King without a kingdom, led by his brother into stripping the peasants of their land, who in a fit of rage orders Eklavya killed and is assassinated himself soon after.

relationship_to_protagonist: The queen whose letter names Bachchan's Eklavya as her son's father
relationship_to_romance: The film's buried romance: implied, never dramatised, and recorded in Films as forbidden love with no pairing row
character_gist: Queen whose sudden death opens the film and whose posthumous letter to her son discloses that his father is the royal guard — the secret the fort has been keeping for a generation.

relationship_to_protagonist: Daughter of the driver killed beside the king Bachchan's Eklavya serves
relationship_to_romance: The film's romantic lead, opposite the prince
character_gist: The prince's childhood love, delighted by his return, who leaves him once he confesses his hand in the king's murder — the murder in which her own father died.

relationship_to_protagonist: Daughter of the household Bachchan's Eklavya has guarded for nine generations
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: The prince's mentally challenged twin sister, one of the fort's protected secrets and part of what Eklavya's loyalty is keeping intact.

relationship_to_protagonist: Suspected by Bachchan's Eklavya of the king's murder, and killed by him
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Jyotiwardhan's son, whom Eklavya kills on the strength of his suspicion and whose body he then leads the father to — an execution carried out on the wrong conclusion.

relationship_to_protagonist: The eighteen-year-old guest with whom Bachchan's Vijay Anand falls in love
relationship_to_romance: One of the film's two recorded pairings with Bachchan — the forbidden attachment at its centre
character_gist: Free-spirited teenager, daughter of divorced parents and her host's schoolfriend, who spends the holidays in Kerala. Her professed affinity for Vijay becomes something neither controls, and she is ordered from the house.
performance_recognition: Nominated for the Filmfare Award for Best Female Debut (2007), the only award named in the film's article

relationship_to_protagonist: Wife of Bachchan's Vijay Anand
relationship_to_romance: The second of the film's two pairings with Bachchan — the marriage the affair breaks
character_gist: Homemaker whose husband confesses that he loves the girl staying in their house, and who is left shattered by it. She loses her faith in him entirely.

relationship_to_protagonist: Daughter of Bachchan's Vijay Anand, and the friend who brought Jia into the house
relationship_to_romance: The witness to the affair and its first casualty
character_gist: Daughter who invites her friend home for the holidays, sees her father and Jia kissing, tries to get Jia out of the house without telling her mother, and finally leaves for America.

relationship_to_protagonist: Brother-in-law of Bachchan's Vijay, and the one person who reasons with him
relationship_to_romance: The intervention that ends the affair
character_gist: Amritha's brother, who uncovers the truth, makes Vijay see how easily a helping gesture reads as love at Jia's age, and later recognises that Vijay is broken beyond repair.

relationship_to_protagonist: Peripheral to Bachchan's Vijay
relationship_to_romance: A young alternative to the film's central attachment, undeveloped in the article
character_gist: Young man in the circle around Jia and Ritu; the article gives the role no development.

relationship_to_protagonist: The woman Bachchan's Buddhadev Gupta humiliates, then courts and proposes to
relationship_to_romance: The film's recorded pairing with Bachchan, across a thirty-year age gap
character_gist: Thirty-four-year-old woman from India who sends back a sweet pulao and is publicly humiliated for it, then sends a better one from her own kitchen. She falls in love with the chef and holds to it through her father's hunger strike.
performance_recognition: Won the Filmfare Critics Award for Best Actress and the Screen Award for Best Actress (Critics); nominated for the IIFA, Producers Guild, Zee Cine and Stardust awards for Best Actress

relationship_to_protagonist: Father of the woman Bachchan's Buddha wants to marry, and younger than Buddha himself
relationship_to_romance: The whole external opposition to the romance
character_gist: Nina's father, horrified to find his prospective son-in-law is older than he is, who goes on a Gandhi-inspired hunger strike until she relents — and finally, grudgingly, gives way.

relationship_to_protagonist: The eighty-five-year-old mother Bachchan's sixty-four-year-old Buddha lives with
relationship_to_romance: Family on the groom's side; the generational comedy the age-gap romance turns on
character_gist: Buddha's mother, whose presence sets the film's arithmetic: a son of sixty-four still living with his mother while courting a woman thirty years his junior whose father is younger than he is.
performance_recognition: Nominated for the IIFA Award and the Stardust Award for Best Supporting Actress

relationship_to_protagonist: Described as the only friend and confidante of Bachchan's Buddhadev Gupta
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance, and the film's other loss
character_gist: Nine-year-old neighbour with leukaemia, the arrogant chef's one real friend. Her death lands on the same stretch of film as his break with Nina, and their reunion at the Qutub Minar is where he learns of it.
performance_recognition: Nominated for the Stardust Award for Breakthrough Performance – Female and the Zee Cine Award for Most Promising Debut Child Artist

relationship_to_protagonist: The officer Bachchan's former Chief Justice Dhingra interviews, and whose account is the film
relationship_to_romance: Outside romance; the film has none
character_gist: Additional Commissioner heading the Bombay Anti-Terrorism Squad, who recounts its formation on the LAPD SWAT model and its pursuit of Maya's gang. Exonerated at the inquiry Dhingra argues before. Based on Aftab Ahmed Khan.
performance_recognition: Won the AXN Action Award for Best Action Actor

relationship_to_protagonist: The gangster whose killing is the subject of the inquiry Bachchan's Dhingra argues
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Ambitious lieutenant of Dawood Ibrahim seeking control of Bombay's underworld, who targets an informant's family, kidnaps a builder's son, refuses every offer of surrender, and dies with his whole gang in the Lokhandwala flat.
performance_recognition: Won the IIFA Award for Best Villain, the Stardust Standout Performance of the Year and the AXN Action Award for Best Action Actor in a Negative Role; nominated for the Filmfare, Screen, Zee Cine and Stardust awards in negative-role categories

relationship_to_protagonist: One of the officers whose conduct Bachchan's Dhingra defends
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Khan's subordinate in the ATS, through the manhunt and the November 1991 gun battle at the Swati Building.

relationship_to_protagonist: One of the officers whose conduct Bachchan's Dhingra defends
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Head constable under Shamsher Khan in the ATS. Note a name collision in this film's own records: the IIFA and AXN Best Action awards went to Javed Sheikh and Ejaz, the action directors, not to this actor, whose character happens to carry the same name.

relationship_to_protagonist: Among the gangsters killed in the encounter Bachchan's Dhingra justifies
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Member of Maya's gang, one of those who dies in the Lokhandwala shootout.

relationship_to_protagonist: No dealings with Bachchan's Dhingra
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Maya Dolas's mother — the domestic side of a gangster the police are preparing to kill.

relationship_to_protagonist: Part of the public reckoning Bachchan's inquiry frame represents
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Journalist covering the events, a press presence alongside the film's inquiry structure.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan narrates the film and does not appear in it; Swami is its protagonist
relationship_to_romance: Half of the film's central marriage
character_gist: Poor jewellery-shop worker who moves to Mumbai after marrying Radha, saves for her kidney operation in a box at home, finds she has spent the money on the rocking chair he admired, and starts saving again.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan, whose contribution is the narration
relationship_to_romance: Half of the film's central marriage
character_gist: Wife who spends her husband's surgery savings on the chair he could not afford, and who dies of her untreated condition while asking him to sit in it — leaving him her wish that their son reach America.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narrator
relationship_to_romance: The child the marriage is organised around
character_gist: The couple's son, precociously intelligent, who talks his own way into a school that has refused him and carries his mother's ambition for America.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narrator
relationship_to_romance: Peripheral to the central marriage
character_gist: Figure in the family's later life; the article gives the role no development.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's street musician is the figure who watches him through the film and explains him at the end
relationship_to_romance: The film's romantic lead
character_gist: Punjabi from Southall waiting at Waterloo Station who invents a fiancée met at the Paris Ritz the night Princess Diana died, hires a prostitute to play her, and admits the truth only after he has lost the woman he actually wants.

relationship_to_protagonist: One of the two strangers Bachchan's musician observes and finally accounts for
relationship_to_romance: The film's romantic lead
character_gist: Upper-class Pakistani from Lahore who matches Rikki's invented engagement with one of her own — a lawyer who saved her from a falling Superman statue — and recruits a colleague to impersonate him.

relationship_to_protagonist: No dealings with Bachchan's musician
relationship_to_romance: The fictional fiancé who becomes a real couple with the other fiction
character_gist: Alvira's coworker, pressed into playing the invented lawyer, who confesses to Rikki that he has fallen for Laila and that Alvira was never engaged — the disclosure that unlocks the film.
performance_recognition: Nominated for the Zee Cine Award for Best Supporting Actor

relationship_to_protagonist: No dealings with Bachchan's musician
relationship_to_romance: The hired fiction who ends the film in a real pairing
character_gist: Prostitute hired to pose as the fiancée Rikki invented, who wins the dance competition with him and leaves at the end with Satvinder, the pair of them talking about Hollywood.
performance_recognition: Nominated for the Stardust Award, the Zee Cine Award and the Annual Central European Bollywood Award for Best Supporting Actress

relationship_to_protagonist: No dealings with Bachchan's musician
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Comic figure in the London world the two liars move through.

relationship_to_protagonist: Hired to capture or kill Bachchan's Babban Singh, and faces him at the end
relationship_to_romance: Carries one of the film's two romances, with Ghungroo
character_gist: Bodyguard turned fugitive turned police instrument, recruited with Raj for eight lakh rupees to take the bandit Babban Singh. He is about to kill him when Narasimha stops him, and is arrested at the close. The Films sheet credits this film as based on Sholay (FILM-038), where Bachchan played Jaidev, one of the two hired outlaws; in this version he plays the bandit they are hired to take.

relationship_to_protagonist: The man Bachchan's Babban Singh mutilated and whose family he slaughtered
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Police inspector whose wife and son Babban killed and whose fingers he cut off, in revenge for a brother's death. He recruits the two men to take Babban, then insists at the end that the law decide his fate.

relationship_to_protagonist: One of the pair sent against Bachchan's Babban Singh, and killed by his men
relationship_to_romance: Carries the film's second romance, with Durga
character_gist: Heero's partner from the bodyguard days, who falls in love with Subbu's widow and is killed fighting Babban's henchmen in an abandoned building.

relationship_to_protagonist: Widow of the son Bachchan's Babban Singh murdered
relationship_to_romance: Half of the film's second romance, with Raj
character_gist: Widow of Subbu, whom Babban killed along with Narasimha's wife. Raj gives his heart to her, and she is left widowed a second time over by the film's end.

relationship_to_protagonist: Lives in the town Bachchan's Babban Singh terrorises
relationship_to_romance: Half of the film's first romance, with Heero
character_gist: Auto-rickshaw driver in Kaliganj with whom Heero falls in love while he is there to hunt the bandit.

relationship_to_protagonist: Right-hand man of Bachchan's Babban Singh, killed by him for failing
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Babban's lieutenant, badly injured in the fight that kills Raj and then shot by his own leader for having failed — the clearest measure of the character Bachchan is playing.

relationship_to_protagonist: No direct dealings with Bachchan's Babban Singh
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: The Mumbai contact who places the two runaways with the gangster Shambhu, the first step in the chain that ends with them hunting Babban.

relationship_to_protagonist: Co-star of Bachchan's Harish Mishra on the film-within-the-film, and his pupil on the set
relationship_to_romance: No romance; the bond is master and apprentice
