character_gist: Actress who skips the premiere of her own film to sit with the comatose Harish. On location in Mussoorie he had befriended her and taught her about acting, life and Shakespeare, and she is the one who comes back for him.

relationship_to_protagonist: The director who coaxes Bachchan's Harish out of retirement, and is blamed for what happens to him
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Ambitious perfectionist director who realises he must win the old actor's trust before he can cast him, and does — the impatient young auteur set against a man who thinks cinema beneath theatre.

relationship_to_protagonist: The woman who has cared for Bachchan's Harish and who blames the film's cast and crew for his condition
relationship_to_romance: The film's closest thing to a domestic partnership for Bachchan's character; the article leaves its nature to be inferred and the workbook records no pairing
character_gist: The woman nursing the bedridden Harish in a cubbyhole in old Kolkata, who receives Shabnam with spite and then thaws over tea. Her relationship with Harish is one of the things the film gradually discloses.
performance_recognition: Won the National Film Award for Best Supporting Actress (2009)

relationship_to_protagonist: Nurse attending Bachchan's Harish in the present-day frame
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: The nurse sharing the care of the comatose actor with Vandana, part of the sickroom in which the film's flashbacks are told.

relationship_to_protagonist: The journalist who put Bachchan's Harish forward for the role in the first place
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Journalist and the director's younger brother, whose recollections form a second narration, and who suggested the retired Shakespearean for the lead.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan appears as himself in this film about the film industry; the two do not share a plot
relationship_to_romance: The film's romantic lead, in a love across two lifetimes
character_gist: In a dual role: the 1970s junior artist who adores the star Shantipriya, saves her from a fire and dies trying to save her from a murder; and the arrogant modern star born the same night, who avenges her thirty years later.
performance_recognition: Nominated for the Filmfare, IIFA and Zee Cine Awards for Best Actor and the Stardust Star of the Year – Male; shared the Screen Award for Best Pair of the Year with Deepika Padukone

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's appearance as himself
relationship_to_romance: The film's romantic lead, in a dual role across both eras
character_gist: The 1970s superstar secretly married to her producer, who tells him she is pregnant and is locked inside a burning set for it; and the aspiring actress of the present recruited to impersonate her ghost.
performance_recognition: Won the Filmfare Award for Best Female Debut, the IIFA Star Debut of the Year, the Producers Guild Award for Best Debut (Female), the Screen Award for Most Promising Newcomer and the Zee Cine Award for Most Promising Debut; nominated for Best Actress at the Filmfare, IIFA, Zee Cine and Asian Film Awards

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's appearance as himself
relationship_to_romance: The husband who murders his own wife to protect his career
character_gist: Egotistical producer secretly married to Shantipriya, who plans to marry a distributor's daughter instead, tells his pregnant wife he intends to kill her, sets the set alight and locks her in.
performance_recognition: Won the Zee Cine Award and the Stardust Award for Best Actor in a Negative Role; nominated for the IIFA Best Villain, the Screen Award and the Producers Guild Award in negative-role categories

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's appearance as himself
relationship_to_romance: Helps stage the courtship in the first era and carries the truth into the second
character_gist: Omi's closest friend, who sneaks him into the premiere and arranges his evening with Shanti, and who thirty years later is the old man trying to convince a star he is a reincarnation.
performance_recognition: Won the Stardust Award for Breakthrough Performance – Male; nominated for the Filmfare, IIFA and Zee Cine Awards for Best Supporting Actor

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's appearance as himself
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Omi's widowed mother in the chawl, who in the present day recognises the new star as her dead son and is dismissed as delusional.

relationship_to_protagonist: Second-billed after Bachchan in this Bhojpuri sequel; no source describes the relationship
relationship_to_romance: No source describes any relationship in this film
character_gist: The film's article lists its cast as names only, with no character names, and has no plot section, so Character is left blank and nothing is asserted about the role. This is the second of two Bhojpuri films pairing her with Bachchan under Deepak Sawant's production, after Ganga (FILM-180); her character there is not evidence for this one.

relationship_to_protagonist: Third-billed; no source describes the relationship
relationship_to_romance: No source describes any relationship in this film
character_gist: Bhojpuri star and singer, billed third. The article names no character and gives no plot; he also sings three songs on the film's soundtrack. Importance here reflects billing order alone.

relationship_to_protagonist: Fourth-billed; no source describes the relationship
relationship_to_romance: No source describes any relationship in this film
character_gist: Billed fourth, with no character name and no plot summary available. The article records only that Mithun Chakraborty was initially considered to play her character's elder brother, which is the sole hint of the role's shape.

relationship_to_protagonist: Fifth-billed; no source describes the relationship
relationship_to_romance: No source describes any relationship in this film
character_gist: Listed in both the infobox and the cast section with no character name, in an article with no plot. Importance reflects billing order alone.

relationship_to_protagonist: Last-billed, and the only cast member absent from the infobox; no source describes the relationship
relationship_to_romance: No source describes any relationship in this film
character_gist: Appears in the cast section but not the infobox's starring list, with no character name and no plot to place him in.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan narrates the film and does not appear in it; Akbar is its protagonist
relationship_to_romance: The film's romantic lead
character_gist: Mughal emperor raised to rule by the sword who chooses mercy and diplomacy instead, accepts a political marriage, grants his Rajput wife her faith and a Krishna shrine, and waits for her to accept him rather than claim her.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan, whose contribution is the narration
relationship_to_romance: The film's romantic lead
character_gist: Rajput princess who resents being made a political pawn, sets two conditions before the wedding — her own faith and a shrine to Krishna inside Agra Fort — and holds the marriage unconsummated until she chooses otherwise.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narrator
relationship_to_romance: The chief internal opposition to the marriage
character_gist: Akbar's powerful chief nanny, hostile to Jodhaa's growing influence, who finds her unsent letter to Sujamal, has it delivered, and persuades the emperor that his wife is meeting a lover.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narrator
relationship_to_romance: The cousin whose visit is made to look like adultery
character_gist: Rightful heir of Amber, passed over for the succession, who defects to Akbar's ambitious brother-in-law and is taken for a lover when he comes to the palace to see his cousin.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narrator
relationship_to_romance: External threat rather than a rival in love
character_gist: Akbar's brother-in-law, who wants the Mughal throne for himself and allies with the disinherited Sujamal against it.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narrator
relationship_to_romance: The father who offers the marriage as a treaty
character_gist: Ruler of Amber who names his son as heir over his nephew, then offers his daughter's hand to the emperor to avert invasion — shattering Amber's alliances with the other Rajput kingdoms.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narrator
relationship_to_romance: Precedes the romance
character_gist: The child Jodhaa. The same young actress plays the kidnapped Anamika in Ek Ajnabee (FILM-176), where she carries the plot opposite Bachchan.

relationship_to_protagonist: Second-billed opposite Bachchan's Dr Ajay Singh; the article has no plot section, so the relationship between them is not described anywhere
relationship_to_romance: No plot summary survives, so no romantic structure can be stated
character_gist: Named in the cast list as Thakur Vikram Singh. The film's article carries a cast list and a production history but no plot, so nothing can be said about the part. Shooting began in 1976 and the film was released in 2008, so this is a performance recorded 32 years before its release.

relationship_to_protagonist: Not described; the article has no plot section
relationship_to_romance: No plot summary survives, so no pairing can be assessed
character_gist: Credited in a double name, Radha / Heerabai, which suggests two identities or a disguise, though with no plot section the article does not say which. Billed by the lead as one of the film's two South Indian actresses.

relationship_to_protagonist: Not described; the article has no plot section
relationship_to_romance: No plot summary survives, so no pairing can be assessed
character_gist: Fourth-billed, and named in the lead paragraph with Sharada as the film's South Indian casting. The role itself is undescribed in any available source.

relationship_to_protagonist: Sister of Bachchan's Dr Ajay Singh — the only cast entry in this film that states a relationship to his character
relationship_to_romance: No plot summary survives
character_gist: Identified in the cast list only as Ajay's sister, with no character name of her own. Hers is the single row in this film whose connection to Bachchan's character is documented at all.

relationship_to_protagonist: Not described; the article has no plot section
relationship_to_romance: No plot summary survives
character_gist: Credited as Shankara Acharya in a cast assembled largely in the 1970s for a film not released until 2008. The article files it under rediscovered Indian films of that decade.

relationship_to_protagonist: The child who names Bachchan's ghost Bhoothnath and refuses to be frightened of him
relationship_to_romance: Outside romance; the film's central bond is between a child and a ghost
character_gist: Boy who moves into the haunted Goa villa, meets the ghost, decides on his mother's word that ghosts do not exist but angels do, and nicknames him Bhoothnath. Every attempt to scare him off becomes a prank war instead.

relationship_to_protagonist: Cannot see Bachchan's ghost, and disbelieves her son about him
relationship_to_romance: Half of the film's young marriage, largely conducted at a distance
character_gist: Mother who moves into Nath Villa with her son while her husband is at sea, slaps the boy for what she takes to be invention, and is reconciled with him after the accident on the stairs.

relationship_to_protagonist: Rents the villa Bachchan's ghost haunts, then leaves for work
relationship_to_romance: Half of the film's young marriage
character_gist: Engineer on a cruise line who takes the bungalow for a year and departs almost at once on work commitments — billed as an extended cameo, and the third film in this batch to put him and Bachchan in the same cast.

relationship_to_protagonist: Son of Bachchan's Kailash Nath — the family history that explains the haunting
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: The ghost's son, whose story accounts for why Kailash Nath is still in the house he built.

relationship_to_protagonist: Late wife of Bachchan's Kailash Nath
relationship_to_romance: A spouse-only role, and a posthumous one; no pairing record
character_gist: Kailash Nath's late wife and Vijay's mother, part of the household the ghost is still keeping.

relationship_to_protagonist: Target of the pranks Bachchan's ghost plays invisibly
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: School principal, pranked first by the boys and then by an invisible Bhoothnath in front of the whole school.

relationship_to_protagonist: Comic foil in the household around Bachchan's ghost
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Comic presence in the Goa villa, one of four films in this batch in which he plays the servant or fixer.

relationship_to_protagonist: Son and successor of Bachchan's Subhash Nagre, now running the organisation
relationship_to_romance: The film's one romantic thread, with Anita, unstated and cut short
character_gist: The son who now decides, persuading his father to back the power plant, campaigning in Thackerwadi with Anita, telling her that killing his own brother was the hardest thing he had done, and losing his pregnant wife to a car bomb.
performance_recognition: Nominated for the Filmfare, IIFA and Screen Awards for Best Supporting Actor and the Stardust Award for Actor of the Year – Male

relationship_to_protagonist: Brings the project that draws Bachchan's Sarkar into the plot
relationship_to_romance: The film's nearest approach to romance, with the son
character_gist: London-based CEO of Shepard Power Plant who proposes a multibillion-dollar plant in rural Maharashtra, is warned away from Qazi by Shankar, and tells him her father never saw her as a daughter, only as an employee.
performance_recognition: Nominated for the Stardust Award for Actor of the Year – Female

relationship_to_protagonist: Recommends Bachchan's Sarkar to the investors, then conspires against him
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Shady business facilitator who describes Sarkar to his clients as a criminal in the garb of a popular leader, then joins Kaanga and Vohra against the Nagres once the project goes ahead.
performance_recognition: Nominated for the Producers Guild Film Award for Best Actor in a Negative Role

relationship_to_protagonist: Wife of Bachchan's Subhash Nagre, reprised from Sarkar
relationship_to_romance: A spouse-only role with no pairing record, as in the first film
character_gist: The Nagre matriarch again, now through a daughter-in-law's murder and her husband's collapse.
performance_recognition: Nominated for the Producers Guild Film Award for Best Actress in a Supporting Role

relationship_to_protagonist: Among those ranged against Bachchan's Sarkar
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Political figure in the coalition working against the Nagres and their power project.
performance_recognition: Nominated for the Screen Award for Best Actor in a Negative Role

relationship_to_protagonist: Chairman on the other side of the table from Bachchan's Sarkar
relationship_to_romance: The father whose coldness his daughter describes to the son
character_gist: Anita's father and chairman of the company, who held the meeting that started the project and who, by her account, treated her as his employee rather than his child.

relationship_to_protagonist: Wants the office Bachchan's Sarkar controls from outside it
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Politician who cannot become Chief Minister while Sarkar is the power behind his party, and who therefore joins Qazi against him.

relationship_to_protagonist: Daughter-in-law of Bachchan's Sarkar, killed inside his own compound
relationship_to_romance: Half of the son's marriage, ended by the bombing
character_gist: Shankar's wife, who tells him she is two months pregnant and is then killed when her car is bombed within the grounds of Sarkar's villa — the shock that puts the old man in hospital.

relationship_to_protagonist: The man who blames Bachchan's God to his face and is handed his powers for ten days
relationship_to_romance: Carries the film's romance, with Alia
character_gist: Struggling news anchor who holds God responsible for his failures, argues with him in person, and is given power over all things to prove he could do better — using it first on his own career and his rival, then on everyone's prayers at once.

relationship_to_protagonist: The romance Bachchan's God first grants by fiat and then makes the hero earn
relationship_to_romance: The film's romantic lead
character_gist: Successful anchor at the same channel whom Arun has never been able to address. Won by borrowed omnipotence, married off to his rival when he grants every wish at once, shot at that wedding, and finally reconciled with him honestly.

relationship_to_protagonist: The rival whose exposure Bachchan's God leaves to the hero
relationship_to_romance: The rival for Alia
character_gist: Third anchor at the channel, in love with Alia and Arun's rival, who sabotages his show launch and steals his game-show idea before being tricked into exposing himself on air.

relationship_to_protagonist: No direct dealings with Bachchan's God
relationship_to_romance: Family around the romance
character_gist: Arun's father, in the household that absorbs his run of failures.

relationship_to_protagonist: No direct dealings with Bachchan's God
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Comic turn in the television world the film satirises.

relationship_to_protagonist: Grandson of Bachchan's Mr. Mehra
relationship_to_romance: The film's romantic lead
character_gist: American-raised grandson who brings his dying grandmother back to Old Delhi, is absorbed into the mohalla's feuds and affections, supports Bittu's Indian Idol ambition against her father, and falls in love with her.

relationship_to_protagonist: No direct dealings with Bachchan's Dadaji
relationship_to_romance: The film's romantic lead
character_gist: Madangopal's daughter, secretly preparing to audition for Indian Idol, pushed towards a marriage she does not want, and ready to elope with a man who is deceiving her in order to reach her own ambition.
performance_recognition: Nominated for the Stardust Award for Superstar of Tomorrow – Female and the Asian Film Award for Best Newcomer

relationship_to_protagonist: Wife of Bachchan's Mr. Mehra and the reason the film's journey happens
relationship_to_romance: A spouse-only role with no pairing record; her marriage is the film's older generation rather than one of its romances
character_gist: Dying grandmother who asks to be taken back to the ancestral property in Old Delhi. Her collapse from blood sugar, and the traffic stopped by a cow in labour, is the film's sharpest scene about the neighbourhood's habits of faith.

relationship_to_protagonist: Part of the mohalla Bachchan's Mehra family belongs to
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Caste-oppressed trash collector whom Roshan comes to sympathise with — the film's point of contact with the hierarchy underneath the neighbourhood's warmth.
performance_recognition: Won the IIFA Award for Best Supporting Actress; nominated for the Filmfare, Screen and Stardust awards in the same category

relationship_to_protagonist: Neighbour of Bachchan's Mehra household
relationship_to_romance: The paternal opposition to the romance
character_gist: One of the two feuding brothers, whose unwed sister and quarrel with his brother are part of the mohalla's fabric, and who fixes his daughter's marriage against her wishes — earning Roshan's intervention and his wrath.

relationship_to_protagonist: Neighbour and contemporary of Bachchan's Mehra generation
relationship_to_romance: Carries the film's unconsummated older romance
character_gist: The mohalla's renaissance man, who long ago loved Roshan's mother Fatima and has never married since — the film's quiet counterpart to the young romance it foregrounds.

relationship_to_protagonist: Part of the mohalla around Bachchan's family
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: The neighbourhood simpleton, one of the crowd of neighbours whose rush and noise first stuns the returning Roshan.

relationship_to_protagonist: The authority pressing on the neighbourhood Bachchan's family lives in
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Loutish inspector who stretches his authority to manhandle the locals, and whose collisions with Roshan run alongside the panic over the Kala Bandar.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan narrates this film and does not appear in it
relationship_to_romance: No romance; the film is about children and trees
character_gist: One of the group of children who set out to stop a construction company felling the trees in their neighbourhood.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan, whose contribution is the narration
relationship_to_romance: No romance in the film
character_gist: The beggar who helps the children save the trees — the adult ally in a film whose protagonists are all children.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narrator
relationship_to_romance: No romance in the film
character_gist: The film's antagonist, on the side of the construction that the children are resisting.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narrator
relationship_to_romance: No romance in the film
character_gist: Identified in the cast list only as Ram's mother, with no character name of her own.

relationship_to_protagonist: Rubs the lamp and releases Bachchan's Genius, then spends the film refusing to wish
relationship_to_romance: The film's romantic lead
character_gist: Orphaned, bullied young man given a lamp as a birthday joke. He declines to make wishes, has one extracted from him in his sleep, revokes it, and spends the third on being helped to court Jasmine without magic.

relationship_to_protagonist: The romance Bachchan's Genius is asked to bring about without magic
relationship_to_romance: The film's romantic lead
character_gist: Newcomer to the city of Khwaish who gives Aladin the lamp as a birthday present at his bully's suggestion, is briefly enchanted into loving him and then released, and is won honestly before being taken hostage by the Ringmaster.
performance_recognition: The film's article lists a Stardust Award for Best Female Debut and an IIFA Award for Star Debut of the Year – Female for her, but tags every entry in that list as needing a citation and does not say whether these were wins or nominations

relationship_to_protagonist: A former genie himself, and the enemy who strips Bachchan's Genius of his powers
relationship_to_romance: Attacks the romance by turning the hero against his ally, then seizing Jasmine
character_gist: Ex-genie who tells Aladin that Genius murdered his parents, steals the lamp, and wishes for Genius to kill the boy — knowing the refusal will cost him his powers, exactly as planned. He means to steal a comet's reflection to become a genie again.

relationship_to_protagonist: Taught a lesson by Bachchan's Genius
relationship_to_romance: The humiliation that sets the romance going
character_gist: The bully who has tormented Aladin since childhood and who stages the birthday party at which the lamp is given, meaning to embarrass him in front of Jasmine.

relationship_to_protagonist: Part of the world Bachchan's Genius enters
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Supporting figure in the fictional city of Khwaish; her second appearance in this batch, after voicing one of the narrating puppets in Paheli (FILM-170).

relationship_to_protagonist: Father of Bachchan's Auro — his real-life son playing the father of the twelve-year-old his father plays
relationship_to_romance: Half of the film's romance, with Vidya, broken years before the story and repaired across their son's deathbed
character_gist: Flamboyant young politician out to prove that politics is not a dirty word, who does not know the boy who emails him "I hate you" is his son. He had wanted the pregnancy ended; learning the truth, he proposes to Vidya and marries her in the hospital.
performance_recognition: Won the Stardust Award for Best Supporting Actor and shared the Star Screen Award for Jodi No. 1 with Amitabh Bachchan; nominated for the IIFA Award for Best Supporting Actor

relationship_to_protagonist: Mother of Bachchan's Auro, and the parent who raised him alone
relationship_to_romance: Half of the film's romance
character_gist: Gynaecologist who refused an abortion, raised her son alone and concealed his paternity from him and from Amol. Still hurt by what was asked of her, she resists reconciliation until her dying son engineers it.
performance_recognition: Won the Filmfare, IIFA, Star Screen, Producers Guild, Lines Gold and FICCI Frames awards for Best Actress; nominated for the Stardust Star of the Year – Female

relationship_to_protagonist: Maternal grandmother of Bachchan's Auro, in the household that raises him
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Vidya's mother, the third member of the household and the one who keeps its humour intact around a child who is ageing five times too fast.
performance_recognition: Won the National Film Award and the Star Screen Award for Best Supporting Actress; nominated for the Filmfare and IIFA awards in the same category

relationship_to_protagonist: Paternal grandfather of Bachchan's Auro
relationship_to_romance: Family on the father's side of the estrangement
character_gist: Amol's father, on the political side of the family the boy is kept away from.

relationship_to_protagonist: Classmate and closest friend of Bachchan's Auro
relationship_to_romance: A child's affection, not a romance
character_gist: Auro's classmate, the friendship that gives a boy in a rapidly failing body an ordinary school life.

relationship_to_protagonist: School friend of Bachchan's Auro
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: One of Auro's schoolfellows, in the classroom scenes that set the boy's mental age against his physical one.
performance_recognition: Won the Star Screen Award for Best Child Artist

relationship_to_protagonist: Narrates the opening of a film in which her husband plays a child and her son plays that child's father
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Cameo narration over the opening credits — the third Bachchan in a film whose casting inverts the family's real generations.

relationship_to_protagonist: Son of Bachchan's Vijay Harshvardhan Malik, and the man who feeds him the fabricated tape
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: US-educated son running his father's channel against his father's morals, ₹30 crore in debt to investors, who records a coerced conversation and persuades Vijay to broadcast it as news.

relationship_to_protagonist: The young journalist who holds Bachchan's Vijay to his own standard
relationship_to_romance: His relationship with Nandita is the film's only romantic thread
character_gist: Budding journalist who notices the channel prospering as it declines, is silenced mid-interview, and goes undercover as the dead man Khanna — discovering that Khanna had been Jay's friend.

relationship_to_protagonist: The politician whose conspiracy Bachchan's Vijay unwittingly broadcasts
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Corrupt politician who orchestrated the Muzaffarnagar blast, coerces two men into a recorded conversation framing the Prime Minister, has both assassinated, and emerges the frontrunner to replace him.

relationship_to_protagonist: Former employee of Bachchan's Vijay, now his rival
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Head of rival channel Headlines 24, once Vijay's own employee, thriving on aesthetic journalism while India 24x7 fails — and buying leaked programming plans from Vijay's COO.

relationship_to_protagonist: Son-in-law of Bachchan's Vijay
relationship_to_romance: Married into the family; no courtship is shown
character_gist: Vijay's son-in-law, who partners Pandey to bend industrial policy his way and become India's biggest industrialist — the corruption is inside the family before it reaches the newsroom.

relationship_to_protagonist: Wife of Bachchan's Vijay Harshvardhan Malik
relationship_to_romance: A spouse-only role with no pairing record
character_gist: Vijay's wife, in the household that splits along the same line as the channel.

relationship_to_protagonist: One of the newsroom faces around Bachchan's editor
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: An uncredited turn as a news reporter, per the film's cast list — among the earliest screen appearances of an actor who would become a lead in his own right.

relationship_to_protagonist: The younger colleague who talks Bachchan's Venkat out of the classroom and into the gambling dens
relationship_to_romance: Outside romance; the film has none
character_gist: Younger professor who hears Venkat's theory, recruits three students to test it, and then charismatically persuades the indifferent mathematician to take it into Mumbai's underground card rooms for money.

relationship_to_protagonist: The mathematician to whom Bachchan's Venkat confesses the whole story
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: British mathematician, called the world's greatest living, whose letter summons Venkat to a London casino and whose company frames the confession the film is told in. His voice was dubbed by Boman Irani.

relationship_to_protagonist: One of the three students Bachchan's Venkat tests his theory with
relationship_to_romance: Has a crush on Sid; the article develops it no further
character_gist: The studious member of the trio, carrying a crush on the college rockstar — an early role for an actress who became a lead soon after.

relationship_to_protagonist: One of the students recruited into Bachchan's experiment
relationship_to_romance: The object of Apu's crush
character_gist: The college rockstar of the three students who first play the professor's system online and then take it into the addas.

relationship_to_protagonist: One of the students recruited into Bachchan's experiment
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: The boy-next-door of the trio, drawn with the others out of a mathematics department and into gambling dens.

relationship_to_protagonist: Joins the group around Bachchan's Venkat and escalates its stakes
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: The rich, spoiled student who attaches himself to the gang and arranges its entry into casinos and private clubs — the point at which the experiment stops being academic.

relationship_to_protagonist: A cameo in the world Bachchan's professor enters
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Cameo appearance, one of several star turns dotted through the film's gambling milieu alongside Jackie Shroff and Shakti Kapoor.

relationship_to_protagonist: The officer who makes a soldier of the son of Bachchan's Lokanatha Sharma, and who consoles him at the funeral
relationship_to_romance: Outside romance; the film has none
character_gist: Jat Regiment major attached to the NSG who, after a hostile first meeting, sees potential in an unemployed graduate and sends him to the Military Academy. He storms the hijacked aircraft through the wheels and lands it himself.

relationship_to_protagonist: Son of Bachchan's Lokanatha Sharma, and the whole object of his hopes
relationship_to_romance: Engaged to Aishwarya; the article gives the relationship no development
character_gist: Educated and unemployed young man who apologises for his own rudeness, takes the major's advice, passes out of the Academy and joins the NSG — then dies of wounds taken retaking the hijacked plane, and is buried with honours.

relationship_to_protagonist: Wife of Bachchan's Lokanatha Sharma
relationship_to_romance: A spouse-only role with no pairing record
character_gist: Lokanatha Sharma's wife, the other parent of the son the film buries.

relationship_to_protagonist: Fiancée of the son of Bachchan's Lokanatha
relationship_to_romance: The film's only romantic attachment, left undeveloped in the article
character_gist: Surya's fiancée, named in the cast list; the film follows his soldiering rather than the engagement.

relationship_to_protagonist: Serves in the unit the son of Bachchan's character joins
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Havildar major in the NSG unit, played by the film's own director, a former army officer whose Mahadevan films this belongs to.
performance_recognition: Received the 2010 Asianet Film Award for Best Feature Film on National Integration for the film, credited to him as its maker rather than for this performance

relationship_to_protagonist: Estranged wife of Bachchan's Vijju Malhotra
relationship_to_romance: The film's recorded pairing with Bachchan: a marriage broken by his gangster years, reunited without being repaired
character_gist: The wife his violence drove him away from, who never told their son who his father was. She takes him back only at the hospital, and forbids him to reveal himself to Karan — sending him back to Paris to wait.

relationship_to_protagonist: Son of Bachchan's Vijju, who never learns it
relationship_to_romance: Carries the film's young romance, with Tanya
character_gist: Police officer who has sworn to clear Mumbai of gangsters in two months, unaware that the ageing hitman the gangsters have hired is his own father, come to protect him. He is shot by Tedha and survives.

relationship_to_protagonist: The don who hires Bachchan's Vijju to kill his own son
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: International don who decides to eliminate the ACP and engages Vijju to do it. Told at the last that Vijju is Karan's father, he kills his own man Tedha on a false suspicion and is shot in the head.

relationship_to_protagonist: Courted by the son of Bachchan's Vijju
relationship_to_romance: The film's young romantic lead
character_gist: Karan's former college friend, whom he woos through the film and wins along with her conservative father's approval.

relationship_to_protagonist: Suspects Bachchan's Vijju of an affair with her mother and sets out to prove it
relationship_to_romance: Drives the film's false romantic suspicion
character_gist: Tanya's friend, who reads her mother's warmth towards the visiting hitman as evidence of an old affair — a suspicion the film raises and Vijju explicitly denies.

relationship_to_protagonist: The woman Bachchan's Vijju is suspected of having loved
relationship_to_romance: The suspected affair is denied outright in the film, and the workbook records no pairing row for her
character_gist: Amrita's mother, whose overly friendly manner towards Vijju fuels her daughter's theory. Vijju states plainly that there was never an affair, which is why this pairing carries no Romances record.

relationship_to_protagonist: The gunman Bachchan's Vijju fails to stop, and then frames
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Kabir's man, who shoots Karan despite Vijju's attempt to prevent it, and is then denounced by Vijju as an undercover officer — a lie that gets him killed by his own boss.

relationship_to_protagonist: Protégé of Bachchan's Dr. Prabhakar Anand who turns on him publicly
relationship_to_romance: Carries the film's romance, with the principal's daughter
character_gist: MSc topper refused a job over his caste, given an interim post by his old principal, who then turns against him in the quarrel over reservations — losing Poorvi in the process.

relationship_to_protagonist: The minister's man installed to displace Bachchan's principal, and his successor
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Cunning, greedy board appointee who runs a coaching business on the side, uses the reservations headline to force Dr. Anand's resignation, takes the principal's chair, and turns his predecessor's own house into K.K. coaching classes.

relationship_to_protagonist: Daughter of Bachchan's Dr. Prabhakar Anand
relationship_to_romance: The film's romantic lead
character_gist: The principal's daughter and Deepak's girlfriend, who asks him to apologise to her father and breaks with him when he refuses — the romance carrying the film's caste argument inside one household.

relationship_to_protagonist: Student of Bachchan's principal who first opposes, then vindicates him
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Upper-caste friend who gathers a group to drive off the celebrating students and argues the anti-reservation case against Deepak, before recognising that Dr. Anand holds no caste feeling.

relationship_to_protagonist: Wife of Bachchan's Dr. Prabhakar Anand
relationship_to_romance: A spouse-only role with no pairing record
character_gist: The principal's wife, in the household that loses its position, its income and finally its own rooms to a coaching business.

relationship_to_protagonist: The minister Bachchan's principal refuses, which begins his downfall
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Education minister whose worthless nephew is refused admission, and who answers by putting his own man on the college board — his ambition a multi-billion-rupee education conglomerate.

relationship_to_protagonist: A central minister in the world pressing on Bachchan's principal
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Special appearance as a central minister — her third film with Bachchan in this stretch, after the two Bhojpuri films and Bbuddah in the same year.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's contribution is the voice-over narration for the game itself, with no scenes opposite the cast
relationship_to_romance: Half of the film's marriage, and its hero in both worlds
character_gist: In a dual role: the game designer who builds a villain more powerful than his hero at his son's suggestion, and is murdered by it; and G.One, the protagonist he lent his face to, who crosses into the real world to protect the family.

relationship_to_protagonist: The antagonist of the game Bachchan narrates
relationship_to_romance: Threatens the family rather than the romance
character_gist: The self-learning game villain, faceless and stronger than its hero, which refuses to end its turn with the player who beat it, enters the real world, and kills by shapeshifting into those it has scanned.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: Half of the film's marriage
character_gist: Shekhar's wife, at whose request he tries to impress their son, and who takes the family back to India after his murder — pursued there by the thing that killed him.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: The sceptical son whose idea makes the villain stronger than the hero, who plays under the alias Lucifer, reaches the last level, and becomes the target the game comes into the world to kill.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: The company programmer who demonstrates the technology that lets digital things enter the real world, and who helps bring G.One across to fight what came before him.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: The motion-capture artist for the game's characters, who notices the malfunctions and ignores them, and is the villain's first victim and first stolen shape.

relationship_to_protagonist: A guest turn in the film Bachchan narrates
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Appears as his Enthiran robot — and, unusually, as a computer-generated likeness rather than in person, the cast list recording that the actor was unavailable.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan narrates the film and does not appear in it; Vidya is its protagonist
relationship_to_romance: Her marriage is the film's premise and its final deception
character_gist: Pregnant software engineer searching Kolkata for a husband the National Data Center has no record of, who outlasts a contract killer, a rogue officer and the Intelligence Bureau — and whose own account of herself proves to be the film's last reversal.
performance_recognition: Won Best Actress at the Filmfare and Screen awards, Best Actress (Critics) at the Zee Cine Awards, and the Stardust Award for Best Actress in a Thriller or Action

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narrator
relationship_to_romance: His attachment to Vidya is left unspoken
character_gist: Young police officer who attaches himself to the search, breaks into a defunct records office and a serving officer's room with her, and is the one person in the city who believes her throughout.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narrator
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Intelligence Bureau deputy chief who flies in from Delhi, tells Vidya that the man she is looking for masterminded the metro gas attack, orders her to stop, and is left frustrated each time she gets to a witness first.
performance_recognition: Received a Special Jury award at the 60th National Film Awards

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narrator
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Contract killer working under cover of a life insurance agent, who murders the NDC's head of human resources on her doorstep, twice fails to kill Vidya, and dies under a truck mid-chase — his phone yielding the encrypted kill orders.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narrator
relationship_to_romance: The husband the search is ostensibly for
character_gist: The man whose face is the film's central ambiguity: the missing husband by one account, and by the Intelligence Bureau's, the elite operative who went rogue and gassed a metro compartment.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narrator
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Director of the Intelligence Bureau, revealed by a decrypted hard drive to have been the handler behind the poison-gas attack, and drawn into the open by a telephone call claiming evidence that does not exist.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narrator
relationship_to_romance: The marriage that turns out to be the film's real one
character_gist: The officer who died in the poison-gas attack, and Vidya's actual husband — the fact the film withholds until its last movement.

relationship_to_protagonist: Warns his protégé that Bachchan's Sarjerao Gaikwad is using him, while himself working for a don
relationship_to_romance: Outside romance; the film has none
character_gist: DSP ordered to raise an encounter squad against organised crime, who recruits a suspended officer and is revealed to be clearing Sawatya's gang on behalf of the underworld don Mohammad Ghouri.

relationship_to_protagonist: Forms a close bond with Bachchan's Sarjerao after the politician saves his life at a public rally
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Officer suspended over an encounter killing and brought back into the squad. Caught between a mentor who turns out to be corrupt and a politician who is cultivating him, he walks away from both.

relationship_to_protagonist: The crime boss the squad is formed against, in the world Bachchan's Sarjerao graduated out of
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Syndicate leader who, against the urging of his own deputy, refuses to retaliate against the police campaign that is dismantling him — a restraint that turns out to serve someone else's design.

relationship_to_protagonist: Leads the breakaway faction that the film's conflict finally turns on
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Sawatya's right-hand man, who presses for retaliation and then forms his own faction under the protection of the very inspector hunting the gang.

relationship_to_protagonist: Wife of the inspector who opposes Bachchan's politician
relationship_to_romance: A spouse-only role with no pairing record
character_gist: Mahadev's wife, one of the two domestic presences the film sets against its encounter squad.

relationship_to_protagonist: Wife of the officer Bachchan's Sarjerao befriends
relationship_to_romance: A spouse-only role with no pairing record
character_gist: Shivnarayan's wife, at home while her husband is drawn between the squad, the politician and the syndicate.

relationship_to_protagonist: Title character of a film in which Bachchan appears as himself; no source describes a scene between them
relationship_to_romance: No plot summary survives, so no romantic structure can be stated
character_gist: The title role. The film's article carries a cast list but no plot section at all, so nothing can be said about the part beyond the character's name.

relationship_to_protagonist: Not described; the article has no plot section
relationship_to_romance: No plot summary survives
character_gist: Credited as Katy in a cast list unaccompanied by any plot summary.

relationship_to_protagonist: Not described; the article has no plot section
relationship_to_romance: No plot summary survives
character_gist: Credited as Alice; the article gives no plot and no further detail.

relationship_to_protagonist: Not described; the article has no plot section
relationship_to_romance: No plot summary survives
character_gist: Credited only as a tourist, consistent with a holiday comedy, though no plot summary exists to place the role.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan appears as himself in the title song of a film whose running joke is that his son's character is passing under his son's own name
relationship_to_romance: Carries the film's romance, with Radhika
character_gist: Delhi man who loses a property case and a job, is renamed "Abhishek Bachchan" on the spot to hide that a Muslim broke a temple lock, and then invents an effeminate Kathak-dancing twin brother, a mother and a whole second life to sustain the lie.
performance_recognition: Won Best Comedian or Best Actor in a Comic Role at the Screen, Stardust, Zee Cine, BIG Star, Producers Guild, Times of India, IIFA and Bollywood Hungama awards

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's song appearance
relationship_to_romance: Courts and finally marries the hero's sister
character_gist: Eccentric, kind-hearted and mangling English at every turn, he hates liars and punishes them severely — which is the engine of the farce, since his new supervisor's entire identity is a fabrication.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's song appearance
relationship_to_romance: Half of the film's second romance, in a dual role
character_gist: In a dual role: the hero's sister, who resembles Prithviraj's earlier love and is eventually married to him, and Apeksha, that earlier love herself.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's song appearance
relationship_to_romance: The film's romantic lead
character_gist: Prithviraj's sister, taught Kathak by a twin who does not exist. She learns the truth and keeps it, then presses for marriage and leaves home — and is kidnapped for it.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's song appearance
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: The dancer recruited to play the hero's mother — one of the invented relatives the deception requires.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's song appearance
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Son of the family friend and member of the drama company, the man who supplies the false name "Abhishek Bachchan" in the first place.
performance_recognition: Nominated for the Producers Guild Award for Best Comedian

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's song appearance
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Prithviraj's sidekick, who begins to suspect the imposture after watching Gol Maal and noticing how closely its plot matches what he is living through, and who finally exposes it.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan appears as the kind fellow passenger who reassures her on the flight and gives her the confidence to go on alone
relationship_to_romance: Half of the film's marriage, and the object of Laurent's unreciprocated attraction
character_gist: Marathi homemaker running a laddoo business, mocked at home for her English, who flies to New York alone, is humiliated by a barista, and spends her secret savings on a four-week conversational English course she tells nobody about.
performance_recognition: Won the Stardust Award for Best Drama Actress, the Hello Hall of Fame Award and the IRDS Film Award for Best Female Character; nominated for Best Actress at the Filmfare, IIFA, Screen, Zee Cine and Star Guild awards

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's flight cameo
relationship_to_romance: Half of the film's marriage, and the condescension it has to survive
character_gist: Corporate-worker husband who takes his wife for granted and mocks her English, the casual belittlement the film is built to answer.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's flight cameo
relationship_to_romance: The film's one romantic temptation, declined
character_gist: French chef who comforts her in the street after the coffee-shop humiliation and shares her English class. When he tries to kiss her on a rooftop she pushes him gently away and flees, unable to say in English that she is married.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's flight cameo
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Teenage niece in New York who discovers the secret classes and becomes her aunt's strongest supporter, keeping the secret and helping her through the course.
performance_recognition: Nominated for the Star Guild Award for Best Actress in a Supporting Role

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's flight cameo
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Shashi's older sister in New York, whose daughter's wedding is the reason for the journey and the five weeks alone that change her.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's flight cameo
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: The teenage daughter who joins her father in treating her mother with condescension over her English — the domestic contempt the film measures its heroine against.

relationship_to_protagonist: Plays, in the Tamil version, the exact role Bachchan plays in the Hindi one
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: The kind fellow passenger of the Tamil version — the same reassurance scene Bachchan performs in Hindi, recast for another language's audience. The cast list credits both men for the one part.

relationship_to_protagonist: Introduces Nick to Bachchan's Meyer Wolfsheim at a speakeasy, the scene Bachchan's role consists of
relationship_to_romance: The film's romantic lead
character_gist: Mysterious millionaire throwing vast parties in the hope that his former lover will walk into one, who claims Oxford and a wealthy Midwestern family, and whose fortune is shown to rest on bootlegging with the mobster he introduces to Nick.
performance_recognition: Won the AACTA Award for Best Actor in a Leading Role

relationship_to_protagonist: The man to whom Bachchan's Wolfsheim is introduced, and the film's narrator
relationship_to_romance: Observes the romance and arranges its reunion
character_gist: Alcoholic veteran telling the story from a psychiatric hospital in 1929. He rents the cottage next to Gatsby's mansion, is used to bring his cousin Daisy to tea, and writes the whole account down at his doctor's suggestion.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's Wolfsheim
relationship_to_romance: The film's romantic lead
character_gist: The former lover Gatsby has built a fortune and a house to recover, who begins an affair with him, wants to run away, and stops him from telling her husband anything at the luncheon.
performance_recognition: Nominated for the AACTA Award for Best Actress in a Leading Role

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's Wolfsheim, but publicly exposes the bootlegging that Wolfsheim represents
relationship_to_romance: The husband the romance is conducted against
character_gist: Domineering old-money socialite who despises Gatsby for his new money and his designs on Daisy, keeps a mistress at a garage in the Valley of Ashes, and denounces Gatsby at the Plaza as a fraud and a bootlegger.
performance_recognition: Won the AACTA Award for Best Actor in a Supporting Role; nominated for the AACTA International Award for Best Supporting Actor

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's Wolfsheim
relationship_to_romance: Supplies the history the romance depends on
character_gist: Golf star and Daisy's closest friend, matched with Nick, and the one who tells him that Gatsby loved Daisy before the war and throws the parties hoping she will come.
performance_recognition: Won the AACTA Award for Best Actress in a Supporting Role, on a spanned result cell shared with Isla Fisher's nomination; nominated for the Empire Award for Best Female Newcomer

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's Wolfsheim
relationship_to_romance: The affair running parallel to the central one
character_gist: Tom's mistress and an ambitious social climber, picked up at her husband's garage — the other side of the film's adultery, and the death that sets its ending in motion.
performance_recognition: Nominated for the AACTA Award for Best Actress in a Supporting Role, in the same category Elizabeth Debicki won

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's Wolfsheim
relationship_to_romance: The wronged husband on the film's other marriage
character_gist: Garage owner in the Valley of Ashes, Myrtle's husband, who tells Tom they are moving away and is the last piece of the machinery that closes on Gatsby.

relationship_to_protagonist: The only actor in this four-segment anthology who plays a scene opposite Bachchan, in Anurag Kashyap's "Murabba"
relationship_to_romance: Outside romance; the segment is about fathers and sons
character_gist: Young man from Allahabad sent to Mumbai to make Amitabh Bachchan eat half a jar of homemade murabba and bring the rest back for his dying father. Starving and penniless, he outlasts the security apparatus and wins a brief audience.

relationship_to_protagonist: Sends his son on the errand to Bachchan, and turns out to have been sent on the same errand himself
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: The ailing father whose eccentric last wish drives the segment, who detects the substituted jar at once and then reveals that his own father sent him to make Dilip Kumar dip a finger in honey — and that he faked that too.

relationship_to_protagonist: Leads Dibakar Banerjee's segment and shares no scenes with Bachchan
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Failed stage actor, adapted from Satyajit Ray's "Patol Babu, Film Star", plucked from a street crowd to collide with a film's lead and given one monosyllable to say. He plays it with total dedication and leaves without collecting his fee.

relationship_to_protagonist: Leads Karan Johar's segment and shares no scenes with Bachchan
relationship_to_romance: Half of the marriage her segment dismantles
character_gist: Magazine editor whose easy acceptance of her colleague's sexuality becomes a friendship, and who ends the segment realising that her husband's repressed sexuality, not her own inadequacy, had doomed the marriage. She declares herself free.

relationship_to_protagonist: Leads Karan Johar's segment and shares no scenes with Bachchan
relationship_to_romance: The segment's romantic and sexual centre
character_gist: Young man who declares his homosexuality to his father and leaves home, befriends Gayatri, provokes her husband's repressed desire, and is beaten twice by him — the second beating breaking into a kiss.

relationship_to_protagonist: Appears in Karan Johar's segment and shares no scenes with Bachchan
relationship_to_romance: The closeted husband at the centre of the segment's collapse
character_gist: Uptight husband who bonds with his wife's colleague over vintage Hindi cinema, assaults him, kisses him, and ends the film homeless beside a child street singer, hollowly repeating that lying is bad.

relationship_to_protagonist: Leads Zoya Akhtar's segment and shares no scenes with Bachchan
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Twelve-year-old who secretly learns the choreography to "Sheila Ki Jawani" and cross-dresses to dance while his father pushes him towards football, then stages a ticketed recital in a garage to raise the money his sister was refused.

relationship_to_protagonist: Appears as herself in a different segment from Bachchan's, in a film where both play themselves
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Cameo as herself: the actress the boy idolises, whose television remarks about breaking convention and guarding your passions give him the courage to keep dancing.

relationship_to_protagonist: Best friend of Bachchan's son, and the man in whose lap Bachchan's Dwarka Anand dies
relationship_to_romance: Carries the film's romance, with Yasmin
character_gist: Ambitious telecommunications capitalist who starts a social-media campaign to free his dead friend's father from jail, builds it into a national agitation, and at the end founds a party to carry on the fight against corruption.

relationship_to_protagonist: Journalist who carries the movement Bachchan's Dwarka leads to the public
relationship_to_romance: The film's romantic lead, opposite Manav
character_gist: Hard-headed television reporter with opinions of her own, who joins the agitation, breaks with Manav when their ideologies clash, and reunites with him when he returns to his principles.

relationship_to_protagonist: Widowed daughter-in-law of Bachchan's Dwarka Anand, and jointly with him the reason the movement begins
relationship_to_romance: Widowed at the film's opening; no romance
character_gist: Housewife whose husband is killed in an engineered road accident and who cannot obtain the announced compensation despite daily applications — the refusal that makes her father-in-law slap a District Magistrate and go to jail.

relationship_to_protagonist: Orders the killing of Bachchan's son, and finally of Bachchan's Dwarka
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Minister who is secretly behind the accident that killed Akhilesh, announces the compensation that is never paid, sends in paramilitary force against the agitation, and has his henchman shoot Dwarka Anand.

relationship_to_protagonist: Former pupil at the school where Bachchan's Dwarka Anand was principal
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Socially committed activist intending to enter politics, drawn into the campaign and, at the close, into founding the new regional party with Manav.

relationship_to_protagonist: Son of Bachchan's Dwarka Anand, killed early in the film
relationship_to_romance: Married to Sumitra; the marriage ends with his death
character_gist: The engineer son whose death in a staged road accident, and whose unbuilt school, are what the whole movement is finally about.

relationship_to_protagonist: Carries out the killing of Bachchan's son
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Balram Singh's brother, who maliciously engineers the road accident that kills Akhilesh Anand.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan narrates the film and does not appear in it; Surya is its protagonist
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance, which belongs to his younger brother
character_gist: Disowned son who saved a gangster's life as a boy and was raised by him, grown into a suave transport businessman who fights for justice, and who returns when his father and brother are destroyed by a corrupt police officer.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narrator
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Retired schoolteacher who threw his elder son out after a killing and insists he has only one son. Humiliated and thrown out by the ACP, he is finally the reason the disowned son returns.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narrator
relationship_to_romance: The external opposition to the romance, as the bride's brother
character_gist: Corrupt police officer in league with the home minister, who decides his sister will marry the minister's son whether she wishes it or not, and has her actual suitor convicted of crimes he did not commit.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narrator
relationship_to_romance: The film's romantic lead
character_gist: The favoured younger son, sent to Delhi and posted as security to the ACP's sister, whom he already knows from an intercollege festival. Their love is what gets him framed and jailed.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narrator
relationship_to_romance: The film's romantic lead
character_gist: The ACP's sister, guarded by the man she falls in love with, and promised by her brother to the home minister's son against her will.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narrator
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Kurukshetra transport magnate and notorious gangster, betrayed by his own man and saved by a boy he then takes in and names "Boss" — the surrogate father to the son a real father disowned.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narrator
relationship_to_romance: Wants the heroine married to his own son
character_gist: Corrupt and power-hungry home minister in league with the ACP, who proposes the marriage that drives the plot.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan narrates the film and does not appear in it
relationship_to_romance: Half of the film's marriage, and the object of Kaya's one-sided love
character_gist: In a dual role: the scientist father researching a device to revive dead tissue with solar energy, and his superhero son, repeatedly sacked from day jobs for absenteeism, who makes an antidote from his own blood and spreads it over Mumbai.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: Attacks the marriage by abducting the pregnant wife
character_gist: Handicapped geneticist with telekinetic powers who breeds human-animal hybrids to cure himself, spreads the virus whose antidote he intends to sell, and plans to induce an early birth to harvest the child's bone marrow.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: Impersonates the wife and falls in love with the husband, one-sidedly
character_gist: Shapeshifting mutant and Kaal's most trusted agent, who murders two scientists, takes Priya's form to convince Krishna she has miscarried, and comes to love him while feeling guilty for the deception.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: Half of the film's marriage
character_gist: Television reporter married to Krishna, who announces her pregnancy on his birthday, is injured in the attack on his father and then abducted and impersonated — her unborn child the object of the villain's whole design.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Special appearance as the antagonist of the previous film, whose scientific creation of a son is the fact the new villain's parentage rests on.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Krishna's friend and colleague, the comic register of a film otherwise built on hybrids and pandemics.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narration; her footage predates this film entirely
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Appears only in flashback through archived footage from Koi... Mil Gaya, the character having died between films — so she is present in a Bachchan film without having acted in it, as she is in Sooryavansham and Aakhree Raasta as a dubbing voice.

relationship_to_protagonist: Voices a Pandava in the animated film Bachchan voices Bhishma in; all the work is in the recording booth
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Voice of the second Pandava, the brother warned by Vidura of the plan to burn the family's palace and so the reason they escape it alive.

relationship_to_protagonist: Voice role opposite Bachchan's Bhishma, who presides over the exhibition where his character forces his way in
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Voice of Kunti's abandoned firstborn, barred from the weapons contest for not being royal until Duryodhana makes him a king on the spot, and then judged Arjuna's equal as an archer.

relationship_to_protagonist: Voice role in the film Bachchan narrates the lineage of as Bhishma
relationship_to_romance: Wins Draupadi, who is then shared among the brothers
character_gist: Voice of the third Pandava, who wins Draupadi's contest in a brahmin's disguise and is then told by his mother, before she has heard what he won, to share it equally with his brothers.

relationship_to_protagonist: Voice role; his character's grandsire is the one Bachchan voices
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Voice of the eldest Kaurava, who makes Karna a king to see Arjuna beaten, plots with Shakuni to burn the Pandavas alive, and leaves the palace of illusions humiliated by Draupadi.

relationship_to_protagonist: Voice role in the film Bachchan voices Bhishma in
relationship_to_romance: Married to all five brothers, by a boon explained in the film
character_gist: Voice of the princess won at a contest and married to five men, explained by Krishna as the working out of a request she had made five times in a previous life; her insult to Duryodhana sets the war moving.

relationship_to_protagonist: Voice role opposite Bachchan's Bhishma
relationship_to_romance: Explains the origin of the film's central marriage
character_gist: Voice of Krishna, the guide Vidura promises the exiled brothers, and the one who accounts for Draupadi's five husbands.

relationship_to_protagonist: Voice role in the film Bachchan voices Bhishma in
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Voice of the uncle who devises the plan to burn the Pandavas to ashes in their own palace.

relationship_to_protagonist: The one child who can see Bachchan's Bhoothnath in his true form, and his partner throughout
relationship_to_romance: Outside romance; the bond is a ghost and a boy
character_gist: Slum boy who is not frightened of the ghost but stages a fake haunting with him to get onto a cricket team, pushes him into contesting an election, and refuses to stop the rally even when Bhau's men threaten his life.

relationship_to_protagonist: The candidate Bachchan's Bhoothnath stands against
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Former criminal turned corrupt politician, whose rivalry with a ghost standing for election escalates until his men beat a child for refusing to call off a rally.

relationship_to_protagonist: Part of the campaign built around Bachchan's candidate
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Figure in the election plot, on the side of the ghost's improbable candidacy.

relationship_to_protagonist: Comic foil in the world around Bachchan's Bhoothnath
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Comic turn in the campaign and haunting plots.

relationship_to_protagonist: Returns as the tenant of the villa Bachchan's ghost haunted in the first film
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Reprises his Bhoothnath role in a guest capacity, tying the sequel to the 2008 film; archive footage of Aman Siddiqui's Banku serves the same purpose.

relationship_to_protagonist: Appears as himself in the film Bachchan leads
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Cameo as himself, alongside Anurag Kashyap in the same capacity.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan appears as Pratapji in a special-appearance capacity in this Telugu film; the plot belongs to the Akkineni family
relationship_to_romance: His own parents' romance is the film's innermost flashback
character_gist: The elderly man knocked down and given blood by a stranger, who wakes to recognise his rescuer and his doctor as the exact likenesses of his own parents, dead in 1924, and sets about uniting them without waking their past-life memories.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's special appearance
relationship_to_romance: Half of the 1920s romance and, as Bittu, the engineer of the present-day one
character_gist: In a dual role: the London-returned barrister who courts a poor farmer in disguise to help her raise her own dowry, and the modern businessman who breaks up a couple and remakes it to give his dead parents the ending they never had.
performance_recognition: Won the TSR TV9 Special Jury Award for Best Actor and the CineMAA Award for Best Outstanding Actor; nominated for the Filmfare Award for Best Actor – Telugu

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's special appearance
relationship_to_romance: Half of the 1983 marriage and half of the present-day romance
character_gist: In a dual role: the husband whose strained marriage is on its way to a divorce lawyer when both are killed in 1983, and the modern lookalike whose engagement is deliberately destroyed so he can be paired with his own former wife's double.
performance_recognition: Won the SIIMA Award for Best Actor – Telugu (Critics); nominated for the SIIMA Award for Best Actor – Telugu

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's special appearance
relationship_to_romance: Half of the 1983 marriage and half of the present-day romance
character_gist: In a dual role: the wife whose romance has curdled into a strained marriage and who dies with her husband on the way to file for divorce, and her present-day likeness, courted by the son she left behind at six.
performance_recognition: Won the SIIMA Award for Best Actress – Telugu (Critics) and the CineMAA Award for Best Actress; nominated for the Filmfare and SIIMA awards for Best Actress – Telugu

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's special appearance
relationship_to_romance: Half of the 1920s romance and half of the film's third pairing
character_gist: In a dual role: the poor farmer who asks six months to earn the groom's clothes and is secretly helped to do it in three, and the doctor whom the modern businessman falls for at first sight beside the same clock tower.
performance_recognition: Won the TSR TV9 Award for Best Actress, the SIIMA Award for Best Supporting Actress – Telugu and the Santosham Award for Best Actress; nominated for the Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actress – Telugu

relationship_to_protagonist: One of the family special appearances in the film Bachchan guests in
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Special appearance as a dance teacher — part of the casting that put four generations of one screen family in a single film, which its own Filmfare Best Film award credits simply to the Akkineni Family.

relationship_to_protagonist: Appears as himself, as Bachchan does in his own guest capacity elsewhere in the film
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Special appearance as himself, completing the family line-up alongside his grandfather, father, brother and mother.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan narrates this motion-capture animated Tamil film and does not appear in it
relationship_to_romance: Carries the film's romance, with Vadhana Devi
character_gist: In a triple role. As Rana he leaves home, is raised in a rival kingdom, rises to command its army, then turns a war into a rescue: the whole invasion was staged to free his own kingdom's enslaved soldiers from Kalingapuri's mines.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: The film's romantic lead
character_gist: Daughter of the king of Kottaipattinam and Rana's childhood sweetheart, who rekindles the attachment on his return and who personally fights and captures the masked assassin sent for her father.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: Half of the film's second romance, with Rana's sister
character_gist: Crown prince of Kottaipattinam and Rana's childhood friend, whom Rana meets across a battle line and then marries to his own sister — and who is disowned by his father for it.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: King of Kalingapuri, who promotes Rana to commander-in-chief and approves the attack on his rival, then swears revenge on discovering the whole campaign was a deception.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: The Kalingapuri prince who shows Rana the secret mine worked by captured enemy soldiers, agrees to free them as a war strategy, and is betrayed by the plan he approved.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: The paternal objection to both romances
character_gist: King of Kottaipattinam, alarmed at the sight of Rana, unwilling to let his son marry a commoner, disowning him when he does, and the target of the assassination attempt that unmasks the film's secret.

relationship_to_protagonist: Speaks with the voice of Bachchan's Amitabh Sinha throughout, by way of a surgical implant
relationship_to_romance: Half of the film's understated romance, with Akshara
character_gist: Mute man from Igatpuri who trespasses into Film City to be seen acting, receives a voice-transfer implant in Finland, and becomes a star under a name fusing his own with his voice's — then treats the man supplying it as a servant.

relationship_to_protagonist: Finds Bachchan's Amitabh Sinha on a footpath and recruits him as the voice
relationship_to_romance: The film's romantic lead
character_gist: Assistant director who is the first to see the mute man act, pushes for the surgery, finds the drunk whose voice will serve, and finally makes both men admit they are nothing without each other.

relationship_to_protagonist: Supplies the premise that gives Bachchan's character his function in the film
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Akshara's father, who reveals that a live voice-transfer technology exists in Finland — a larynx chip letting a mute patient speak in a borrowed voice.

relationship_to_protagonist: Part of the film industry that rejects and then launches the two men
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Director who refuses the mute actor outright, then agrees to launch him once he can speak, on condition he change his name.

relationship_to_protagonist: Appears as herself in a film whose subject is Bachchan's voice
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: One of a long line of film-industry figures appearing as themselves, among them Abhishek Bachchan, Karan Johar, Rajkumar Hirani and Javed Akhtar — her third appearance in a Bachchan film in this stretch of the filmography.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan appears only in the song "Birju"; no source places him in a scene with the cast
relationship_to_romance: The article's one-sentence summary describes no romance
character_gist: Villager who comes to Mumbai looking for his mother and twin brother, and finds that he and the brother are opposites in every way. The article's entire plot summary is that single sentence.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's song appearance
relationship_to_romance: No romance is described
character_gist: The estranged twin, head of a Mumbai police station and temperamentally his brother's opposite.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's song appearance
relationship_to_romance: No romance is described in the article
character_gist: Credited as Anjali; with only a one-sentence plot available, the role cannot be described further.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's song appearance
relationship_to_romance: No romance is described
character_gist: The corrupt crime lord the policeman brother is trying to apprehend, per the cast list; the plot summary does not extend to him.

relationship_to_protagonist: Daughter and carer of Bachchan's Bhashkor Banerjee, and the film's title role
relationship_to_romance: Half of the film's romance with Rana — the one romantic thread in this stretch of the filmography, with Bachchan's character as its obstacle
character_gist: Thirty-year-old architect running her father's household and her own practice, exasperated by his hypochondria and his theory that marriage is a low-IQ decision, and driven by both into the company of the taxi owner nobody else will send to her.

relationship_to_protagonist: The taxi owner who ends up driving Bachchan's Bhashkor to Kolkata and taking his measure
relationship_to_romance: Half of the film's romance
character_gist: Taxi business owner whose drivers refuse Piku's custom, who complains about her backseat driving and is brushed off, and who becomes the third party in a road trip conducted almost entirely around one old man's bowels.

relationship_to_protagonist: Sister-in-law of Bachchan's Bhashkor, and the target of his sharpest criticism
relationship_to_romance: The film's counter-argument on marriage
character_gist: Piku's maternal aunt, married three times, whom Bhashkor attacks for it and for neglecting her own daughter — the standing rebuttal to his view that a woman's life is wasted in the service of a husband.

relationship_to_protagonist: No direct dealings with Bachchan's Bhashkor
relationship_to_romance: The mutual friend through whom the couple keep meeting
character_gist: Piku's business partner and Rana's friend, the connection that keeps putting the two of them in the same car.

relationship_to_protagonist: Regular doctor to Bachchan's Bhashkor
relationship_to_romance: Wrecks the heroine's one date
character_gist: The doctor telephoned mid-date to discuss Bhashkor's stool texture and temperature — the call that ends Piku's evening with Aniket.

relationship_to_protagonist: Loses an evening to Bachchan's Bhashkor's invented fever
relationship_to_romance: The suitor the father displaces
