character_gist: Cameo as the man Piku goes on a date with, interrupted repeatedly by a father claiming a fever until his appetite is gone.

relationship_to_protagonist: Befriended at his daughter's grave by Bachchan's Pandit, and used by him from that moment on
relationship_to_romance: Half of the film's marriage, broken by their child's death and reconciled at the end
character_gist: ATS officer whose daughter is killed in a shootout he caused, blamed by his wife, suspended for killing the terrorist he was ordered to capture. Contemplating suicide, he is recruited by a chess master into an investigation that is really an instrument.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan's Pandit had taught her daughter, and his final message is addressed to her as much as to her husband
relationship_to_romance: Half of the film's marriage
character_gist: Mother who blames her husband for their daughter's death and withdraws from him, and whom the Pandit's posthumous video finally urges, with him, to move on from grief.

relationship_to_protagonist: Murdered the daughter of Bachchan's Pandit, and is the target of his entire design
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Government minister at whose residence the Pandit's daughter died, revealed as a militant who massacred a village and took his own ward's guardian's identity — killing the girl because she had learnt the truth.

relationship_to_protagonist: Appears to be the hitman menacing Bachchan's Pandit, and is disclosed as the Pandit's own invention
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: The mysterious assassin who threatens the Pandit and apparently kills him in an explosion — and who, a posthumous video reveals, never existed: a persona the disabled chess master created to move the pieces he could not reach.

relationship_to_protagonist: Daughter of Bachchan's Pandit Omkar Nath Dhar
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: The daughter said to have died falling down the minister's stairs while tutoring his ward — the death her father is certain was murder, and is proved right about.

relationship_to_protagonist: Pupil of Bachchan's Pandit, and the shared loss that lets him approach her father
relationship_to_romance: The child whose death strains the marriage
character_gist: The little girl killed in her father's shootout, whose chess lessons with the Pandit are the connection that makes the whole manipulation possible.

relationship_to_protagonist: Assists the man Bachchan's Pandit has set in motion
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Special appearance as the superintendent who helps disrupt the minister's public appearance in Kashmir and track him down.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan appears as himself; the meeting he arranges with her husband is what precipitates her crisis
relationship_to_romance: Half of the film's marriage
character_gist: Driven executive who marries a man content to keep the house, rises fast, and then turns on him — jealous of the fame his domesticity earns him, and convinced her own work is going unnoticed.
performance_recognition: Won the B4U Viewers Choice Award for Best Actress and the Lux Golden Rose Award for Glamorous Diva of the Year

relationship_to_protagonist: Telephoned by Bachchan, as himself, and invited to meet him
relationship_to_romance: Half of the film's marriage
character_gist: Builder's son who refuses the company and the inheritance, becomes a ghar jamai against his father's wishes, runs the household, and is drawn into a circuit of seminars on gender roles that his wife comes to resent.

relationship_to_protagonist: Appears as herself opposite Bachchan as himself — the two of them a married couple playing a married couple
relationship_to_romance: Their own marriage is used as the film's implicit comparison
character_gist: Sees the husband's television interview, is impressed by the couple's unconventional marriage, and asks her husband to telephone him and arrange a meeting. Her gift to Kia is what finally turns the quarrel.

relationship_to_protagonist: No dealings with Bachchan's appearance as himself
relationship_to_romance: The mother whose collapse brings the wife home
character_gist: Kia's mother, whose hospitalisation cuts short a work trip to the United States and forces the confrontation that ends the film's middle.

relationship_to_protagonist: No dealings with Bachchan's appearance as himself
relationship_to_romance: The paternal disapproval the marriage begins against
character_gist: Kabir's father, a successful building contractor whose company and wealth his son declines, and who disapproves of the arrangement the couple settle into.

relationship_to_protagonist: Met regularly by Bachchan's John Biswas, and the man who works out what he has done
relationship_to_romance: Outside romance; the film has none
character_gist: Priest who was the police inspector on the original kidnapping and left the force out of guilt at failing. He helps the new investigation, discovers that the grandfather staged the second kidnapping, and is revealed to have been driving the car the girl fell onto.

relationship_to_protagonist: The officer Bachchan's John Biswas visits at the station again and again, and who finally investigates alongside him
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Police inspector with no leads on an eight-year-old case, discouraged on all sides, who keeps collecting evidence and reopens the old file when a second kidnapping copies the first exactly. The film's plot section calls her Sarita Sarkar, against the cast list's Sharma.

relationship_to_protagonist: The man Bachchan's John Biswas spends eight years identifying, and then traps
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: The second boy's grandfather, caught fleeing with the ransom, who confesses under questioning that he kidnapped Angela to pay for his daughter's open-heart surgery — and that she died escaping, not by his hand.

relationship_to_protagonist: Wife of Bachchan's John Biswas
relationship_to_romance: A spouse-only role, recorded in Films as an established relationship with no pairing row
character_gist: The ailing wife in a wheelchair whom John cares for while conducting a private investigation and, unknown to her, a kidnapping of his own.

relationship_to_protagonist: Granddaughter of Bachchan's John Biswas, dead eight years before the film opens
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: The kidnapped granddaughter whose death drives the whole film, and who was never murdered: held captive, she escaped, fell from a height onto a moving car and died.

relationship_to_protagonist: Father of the murdered granddaughter of Bachchan's John Biswas
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Angela's father, in the family the first kidnapping destroyed.

relationship_to_protagonist: The boy Bachchan's John Biswas abducts in order to force a confession
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: The second kidnapped child, taken in a replica of the first crime — by the grieving grandfather himself, as a means of reopening a closed case.

relationship_to_protagonist: The woman Bachchan's Deepak Sehgal comes out of retirement to defend
relationship_to_romance: Outside romance; the film is about consent, not courtship
character_gist: Young woman who strikes a man with a bottle when he tries to rape her, is harassed, abducted and molested for reporting it, and is then arrested for attempted murder on his counter-complaint that she is a sex worker.
performance_recognition: Nominated for the IIFA Award for Best Actress

relationship_to_protagonist: One of the three women who seek out Bachchan's neighbour and discover what he used to be
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Flatmate who loses her job to a sexually explicit smear campaign run against the three of them online, and who goes with Andrea to ask the elderly neighbour for help.
performance_recognition: Nominated for the Filmfare and IIFA awards for Best Supporting Actress

relationship_to_protagonist: One of the three defendants Bachchan's Deepak represents
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: The third flatmate, subjected with the others to harassment, a smear campaign and a prosecution built on their morals rather than the facts.
performance_recognition: Nominated for the Stardust Award for Best Debutant (Female), the Zee Cine Award for Best Female Debut and the IIFA Award for Best Supporting Actress

relationship_to_protagonist: The complainant Bachchan's Deepak cross-examines
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Politically connected young man who attempts the rape, is struck with a bottle, and answers by filing a counter-complaint of attempted murder painting the three women as prostitutes.

relationship_to_protagonist: Opposing counsel to Bachchan's Deepak Sehgal
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Prosecuting attorney who builds his case on the women's character — that they live away from family, drink and stay out late — and argues they demanded payment and turned violent when refused.

relationship_to_protagonist: Presides over the trial Bachchan's Deepak argues
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: The judge before whom the case is reframed from assault to consent — the shift the whole film is built to achieve.

relationship_to_protagonist: Wife of Bachchan's Deepak Sehgal
relationship_to_romance: No pairing row: Bollywood Hungama's review states the film "does not explain certain elements very clearly like the relationship between Amitabh Bachchan with an ailing lady named Sarah", and that gap is the explicit basis for creating none
character_gist: The ailing woman in Deepak's house, whose connection to him the film never sets out. The role is recorded here and deliberately not interpreted further.

character: Tukaram Raosaheb Marathe / Advocate Vivek Tupkari
relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan narrates the film and does not appear in it
relationship_to_romance: Half of the film's central couple, both of them in disguise
character_gist: The man who lays claim to the land the Taj Mahal stands on, producing letters from Humayun and Akbar addressed to his ancestors that test as authentic — and who is, in the second half of the credit, a lawyer playing a part.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: Half of the film's central couple
character_gist: His wife in the claim and his girlfriend outside it, who sits the hunger strike on the Yamuna plains beside him and refuses every attempt to move them.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: The jail minister of Uttar Pradesh sent to settle the dispute, who succeeds only in making it considerably worse.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: The Chief Minister whose repeated attempts to end the standoff yield nothing and send the claim to court.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan narrates this film and does not appear in it
relationship_to_romance: Outside romance; the film is a submarine action piece
character_gist: Officer posted aboard S21 expressly to restrain its captain from starting a war, who dives into the sea to rescue two Bengali refugees from a torpedoed merchant ship, and takes command when the captain dies.
performance_recognition: Won the SIIMA Award for Entertainer of the Year

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Belligerent submarine captain who orders a drill as cover for firing on the enemy boat, narrowly misses and gives away his own position, and dies trying to save the officer sent to hold him back.
performance_recognition: Nominated for the SIIMA Award for Best Supporting Actor – Telugu

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Executive officer of S21, ordered to run the drill that doubles as an attack, and part of the crew that patches the flooded boat back together on the seabed.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Bengali doctor turned refugee, pulled from the wreckage of a torpedoed merchant ship along with a child — the civilian cost of the war the submarine is trying not to start.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: The Navy admiral who dispatches S21 on reconnaissance and attaches an officer to its captain with orders to prevent any confrontation. Based on Sardarilal Mathradas Nanda.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Commander of PNS Ghazi, sent to the Bay of Bengal after INS Vikrant, who torpedoes a merchant ship as a diversion and lays the minefield that cripples S21. Based on Zafar Muhammad Khan.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Senior naval officer in the command that deciphers the intercepted Pakistani code and deduces that Vikrant is the target. Based on Jal Cursetji.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan narrates this film and does not appear in it
relationship_to_romance: Refuses the film's one proposal, which turns her suitor into an enemy
character_gist: Brothel-keeper whose house stands directly on the Radcliffe Line and who refuses every notice to vacate, telling her protector she would rather die in her own home like a queen than on the street like a beggar. She arms and trains her girls instead.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Killer hired to force the eviction, who murders the household's dogs and feeds their meat to the women, kills a man returning from the market, and leads the final assault on the brothel on the night of partition.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: The patron Begum Jaan has relied on, who returns to tell her his efforts have failed and she must vacate — the withdrawal of the last protection she had.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: The senior woman of the household, part of the collective the film treats as a family under siege rather than a set of employees.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: Loves the teacher who is courting Begum Jaan, and is used and discarded by him
character_gist: One of the women, in love with Masterji, whom he persuades to betray Begum Jaan and flee — then spurns and has raped by his accomplices in a horse carriage. She vows vengeance.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: The rejected suitor who turns murderous
character_gist: The child Laadli's teacher, in love with Begum Jaan. Refused and dismissed, he concocts a plan to kill her, recruiting the woman who loves him and destroying her in the process.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: One of the eleven women of the brothel trained to fight, in a film whose ensemble is almost entirely female.

relationship_to_protagonist: Grandson of Bachchan's Subhash Nagre, taken into the house at his grandmother's pleading and finally expelled from it
relationship_to_romance: His relationship with Annu is the film's one romantic thread, and it is instrumental
character_gist: Vishnu's son, hot-headed like the father Sarkar's other son killed, who clashes with the old guard, is shown a video implicating them, is accused in turn of being behind everything, and defects to the enemy when expelled.

relationship_to_protagonist: The Dubai-based power Bachchan's Sarkar is set against, who finally comes to India to meet him
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Vallya, to whom the thwarted developer reports, who joins the opposition leader to oust Sarkar, organises a bomb blast at the mill, and arrives in person to point out how easily the grandson can be used.

relationship_to_protagonist: Rival whose murder is blamed on Bachchan's Sarkar
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Rival opposition leader who plots with the developer and Vallya to instigate mill workers against Sarkar, and is then hunted down and killed — the killing pinned on the man with the reputation for it.

relationship_to_protagonist: Long-serving right-hand man of Bachchan's Sarkar, and the film's central question of loyalty
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: The loyal aide of many years, approached by the developer with the argument that the grandson's rise would leave him a servant for ever. He accuses Cheeku, hunts him, and is then shot dead — presumably by him.

relationship_to_protagonist: Implied to be using Bachchan's Sarkar's grandson to reach him, because Sarkar had her father eliminated
relationship_to_romance: The film's romance, and a means to an end within it
character_gist: Cheeku's girlfriend, whom the film implies is with him only to get at his grandfather, who had her father killed — and whose influence over him Gokul blames for everything that follows.

relationship_to_protagonist: Wife of Bachchan's Subhash Nagre, in her third and last appearance in the role
relationship_to_romance: A spouse-only role with no pairing record, as in Sarkar and Sarkar Raj
character_gist: The Nagre matriarch who pleads successfully for her grandson to be brought into the house, and who dies partway through the film — the third film in which she plays this marriage and the one that ends it.

relationship_to_protagonist: Returns briefly as the son of Bachchan's Sarkar who succeeded and then died between films
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Cameo reprise of the son who ran the organisation in the first two films, appearing here after the character's death — the third Sarkar film and the third in which father and son share the cast.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan narrates the film and does not appear in it
relationship_to_romance: The film's romantic lead
character_gist: Jobless 1920s villager born able to cure a bad back with a kick to the buttocks, who cures an Englishman, is rewarded with a police job, and then finds that the job itself is what disqualifies him as a suitor.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: The film's romantic lead
character_gist: The woman Manga falls for at a friend's wedding in Naku Guda, and whom he cannot approach while he is jobless — and then cannot marry once he is employed by the British.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: The whole external opposition to the romance
character_gist: Sargi's grandfather and a follower of Mahatma Gandhi, who refuses the match precisely because the suitor works for the British his village is fighting.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: Unwittingly creates the obstacle to the romance
character_gist: The Englishman whose back Manga cures and who offers him the police job in gratitude — the favour that costs him his marriage prospects.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: The local ruler, on the side of the colonial arrangement the village is resisting.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: Peripheral to the central romance
character_gist: The princess of the ruling household; the plot summary available does not extend to her part in it.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan narrates and appears as himself in a trailer within the film; he plays no scene with the cast
relationship_to_romance: Half of the film's marriage, which his campaign breaks
character_gist: Welder who, appalled that his wife uses an unhygienic rag, makes pad after pad and tests one on himself with a balloon of goat's blood — is branded a man of loose morals, loses his wife, and sets out to build a pad-making machine. Based on Arunachalam Muruganantham.
performance_recognition: Won Best Actor at the Indian Film Festival of Melbourne; nominated for the Filmfare Award for Best Actor

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: Half of the film's marriage
character_gist: The wife whose banishment during her periods begins the story, who tells her husband repeatedly not to interfere in women's matters, suspects an affair, and is taken away by her brothers. Based on Shanthi Muruganantham.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: The second woman in the film's triangle, on the side of the work rather than the marriage
character_gist: The woman who finally agrees to test and then champion the pads, becoming the partner in the enterprise that the wife would not be.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: Family around the marriage
character_gist: Lakshmi's mother, in the household whose customs around menstruation the film sets out to break.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: The professor in whose house Lakshmi works as a manservant, and who tries to discourage him by showing him films of million-rupee machines — with the opposite effect.

relationship_to_protagonist: The seventy-five-year-old son of Bachchan's 102-year-old Dattatraya
relationship_to_romance: A widower; his one romantic act is a love letter to his dead wife
character_gist: Son who believes himself too old and fragile to enjoy anything, threatened with an old-age home unless he performs a series of conditions: writing a love letter to his late wife, giving up his daily doctor's visits, cutting holes in his childhood blanket.

relationship_to_protagonist: Confidant of Bachchan's Dattatraya and the third person in the household's routine
relationship_to_romance: Outside romance; the film has none
character_gist: Pharmacy employee who delivers the medicines, is let into the scheme, and is sent with Babu to the Juhu garden and the Chembur church — bewildered until Dattatraya explains what those places were.

relationship_to_protagonist: Grandson of Bachchan's Dattatraya
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: The third generation of the household, in a film whose entire cast is one family across three generations plus a pharmacy delivery man.

relationship_to_protagonist: Narrates the film Bachchan leads
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Credited as the film's narrator — worth noting because Bachchan himself narrates eight other films in this very stretch of the filmography, and here another actor performs that function over him.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan appears as himself in a film about a singer's abandoned career; no source places him in a scene with her
relationship_to_romance: Half of a marriage her husband walks out of, and no later romance
character_gist: Semi-famous singer whose career-making recording is cancelled and whose husband leaves, convinced the men of his family all die in their late thirties. Left a single mother, she becomes so protective that she enrols in her son's own college.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's appearance as himself
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: The son whose life his mother will not stop meddling in, who moves out of the family home to force her to find an identity of her own, and who then pushes her onto the stage of the competition that bars her.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's appearance as himself
relationship_to_romance: The husband who leaves, and briefly returns
character_gist: The boyfriend turned husband who wrote her songs, then abandoned wife and infant son to pursue his own ambitions in what he believed were his final years — and who returns once, sees he is not needed, and goes.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's appearance as himself
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Figure in the world Eela re-enters on going back to college after twenty-two years.

relationship_to_protagonist: Appears as himself, as Bachchan does in the same film
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Appears as himself in a film whose premise turns on one of his own projects: the heroine's breakthrough song was being recorded for a Mahesh Bhatt production when it was shelved indefinitely.

relationship_to_protagonist: Infiltrates and betrays Bachchan's Khudabaksh, who saves his life and tells him he knows
relationship_to_romance: Courts Suraiyya and is named Zafira's love interest
character_gist: Small-time thug from Awadh who sells information in every direction and dresses as a European. Recruited by the Company to bring down Azaad, he betrays the Thugs' location, then saves Azaad from a fall — the man who tells him he still believes there is good in him.

relationship_to_protagonist: Adoptive daughter of Bachchan's Khudabaksh, raised and trained by him after her family was massacred
relationship_to_romance: Named as Firangi's love interest
character_gist: Sole surviving child of the murdered Nawab of Raunakpur, raised as Azaad's daughter and trained in warfare as a warrior-archer of the Thugs. Firangi takes a bullet meant for her, and she ends the film Queen of Raunakpur.

relationship_to_protagonist: No dealings with Bachchan's Khudabaksh
relationship_to_romance: The film's other romantic interest for Firangi
character_gist: Dancer and performer, billed as an extended cameo, who challenges Firangi to declare himself during her performance before British officers and then strips off his prosthetic disguise mid-number, getting him arrested.

relationship_to_protagonist: Killed the Nawab whose general Bachchan's Khudabaksh was, and is the power his Thugs fight
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: East India Company officer who kills the Nawab of Raunakpur in 1795 and massacres his people, annexes the kingdom, and eleven years later sets a thug to catch the Thugs who are challenging the Company at sea.

relationship_to_protagonist: Helps track down Bachchan's Azaad in the first place
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Firangi's friend and accomplice, with whose help he locates Azaad during a raid on a British ship. The same actor plays the antagonist of Manikarnika (FILM-240) in this batch, also opposite Bachchan.

relationship_to_protagonist: The Nawab whom Bachchan's Khudabaksh served as general, and whose daughter he then raised
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Nawab of Raunakpur, killed by Clive in the film's 1795 prologue — the death that turns a general into a rebel and creates the Thugs.

relationship_to_protagonist: Part of the world around Bachchan's Thugs
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Supporting figure in the Thugs' company; her third film in this batch, after Aarakshan and Begum Jaan.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan narrates the film and does not appear in it
relationship_to_romance: Widowed early; the marriage is political and brief
character_gist: Girl spotted facing a tiger unafraid and married for that reason to the Maharaja of Jhansi. Widowed, her adopted heir rejected by the British, she proclaims herself queen, walks out of the palace into the village, and raises an army of twenty thousand including women.
performance_recognition: Won the National Film Award for Best Actress, recognised jointly with her work in Panga; nominated for Best Actress at the Screen, Zee Cine and Filmfare awards

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: The Maharaja's brother, friendly with the British and wanting the throne, who poisons the queen's infant son and is passed over when a courtier's child is adopted heir instead.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: Half of the film's marriage
character_gist: Maharaja of Jhansi, who renames his bride Lakshmi Bai on their wedding day and, dying, adopts an heir with her so the kingdom cannot be annexed.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Ally in the rebellion, part of the wider 1857 uprising the film's Jhansi campaign belongs to. His second film in this batch, after The Ghazi Attack.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Commander in the queen's service through the defence of Jhansi — the veteran's final appearance alongside Bachchan's work in this filmography, after Ab Tumhare Hawale and Boss in this same stretch.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: The woman who leads the villagers' parade welcoming the dispossessed queen into their midst, and one of the women trained for the army she raises.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: Arranges the film's marriage
character_gist: The Jhansi courtier who sees the girl face down a tiger and asks the Peshwa for her hand on his king's behalf — knowing the British want the kingdom and that her nerve will be needed.

relationship_to_protagonist: The client Bachchan's Badal Gupta interrogates across a single evening — and the target of the impersonation
relationship_to_romance: Her affair with Arjun is the film's premise rather than its romance
character_gist: Sharp London businesswoman arrested for her lover's murder, who tells the defence attorney a version of events, is pressed on a young man's disappearance, and finally admits the hit-and-run and cover-up that everything else was built to conceal.
performance_recognition: Won the Zee Cine Critics Award for Best Actress; nominated for the IIFA Award for Best Actress and the Screen Award for Best Actress (Critics)

relationship_to_protagonist: The film's central identity: the cast list states he is the man who imposed as Badal Gupta, the advocate Bachchan plays
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Rani's husband and Sunny's father, who repaired a stranger's car outside his own house without knowing his son's body was in the boot — and who assumes the identity of a renowned defence attorney to extract a confession.

relationship_to_protagonist: Wife of the man behind Bachchan's assumed identity, and the mother whose grief drives the whole scheme
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Mother who invited a stranger in for tea, heard her missing son's phone ring in his pocket, traced the car by its number plate, and confronted Naina at the ceremony where she was named Businesswoman of the Year, begging for the truth.
performance_recognition: Nominated for the Filmfare, IIFA and Screen awards for Best Supporting Actress

relationship_to_protagonist: The murder victim whose death brings Bachchan's advocate to the flat
relationship_to_romance: Naina's secret lover — the affair the blackmail rested on
character_gist: Naina's lover, who persuaded her not to report the accident, hid the body, took the dead boy's wallet and used it to frame him for embezzlement — and is found dead in a hotel room with the blackmail money gone.

relationship_to_protagonist: The lawyer who hires the attorney Bachchan appears to be
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Naina's lawyer and college friend, who brings in the famous defence attorney and who had earlier falsified the alibi that got the police off her car.

relationship_to_protagonist: The dead son whose parents mount the deception Bachchan's character is part of
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: The young man killed in the hit-and-run, whose body was dumped in a swamp in his own car and who was then posthumously accused of embezzling from his bank.

relationship_to_protagonist: Police presence around the case Bachchan's advocate is dissecting
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: The detective on a case where the police found no evidence of anyone else in the hotel room and no sign of a break-in.

relationship_to_protagonist: Learns combat and philosophy under Bachchan's sage Gosayi Venkanna — the one direct relationship his role has in the film
relationship_to_romance: Married in childhood to Siddhamma, and drawn to the dancer Lakshmi
character_gist: Chief's son of Uyyalawada, believed blessed after being born still and coming to life, who vows retaliation after seeing a British execution, trains under the sage, and twenty-five years later gathers the fallen chiefs into an organised resistance at Renadu.
performance_recognition: Won the Zee Cine Award Telugu for Best Actor

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's sage
relationship_to_romance: Half of the film's marriage, contracted in childhood
character_gist: Reddy's wife by a child marriage, who had feelings for him even then; separated by omens and reunited for a yagam.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's sage
relationship_to_romance: The film's estranged love, set against an existing marriage
character_gist: Orphaned dancer who dedicates her art to God, whose life Reddy saves from drugged cattle and who attempts suicide on learning he is already married — then travels the country promoting the resistance instead.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's sage
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Governor of the Madras Presidency and the film's principal antagonist, who commands the campaigns against the rebellion and receives his own general's severed head for his trouble.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's sage
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Rival chief envious of Reddy's popularity who drugs cattle into a stampede against him — and is forgiven for it, still admiring the man's courage.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's sage
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Tamil warrior who joins the resistance after Lakshmi's campaign across the country carries word of it south.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's sage
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Chieftain of the resistance whose son betrays it. Believing Reddy executed his son while sparing his own traitorous half-brother, he drugs Reddy — the act that leads directly to his capture.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's sage
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Reddy's half-brother, who betrays the resistance for money and whose survival is what convinces Veera Reddy of the leader's partiality.

relationship_to_protagonist: The "CD" of a title whose "AB" is Bachchan himself, appearing in a cameo capacity
relationship_to_romance: No plot summary survives, so no romantic structure can be stated
character_gist: The film's title character opposite Bachchan's own initials. The article carries a full cast list but no plot section at all, so nothing can be said of the part beyond the family relationships the cast list itself sets out.

relationship_to_protagonist: Grandson of the title's CD; no source describes any scene with Bachchan
relationship_to_romance: No plot summary survives
character_gist: CD's grandson, given a Pune-based girlfriend by the cast list. With no plot section available the role cannot be described further.

relationship_to_protagonist: Not described; the article has no plot section
relationship_to_romance: Named in the cast list as Sunny's girlfriend, with no development available
character_gist: Sunny's Pune-based girlfriend, employed by the owner of Planet Marathi according to the cast list.

relationship_to_protagonist: Not described; the article has no plot section
relationship_to_romance: No plot summary survives
character_gist: Credited as the owner of Planet Marathi, the streaming platform that released this film — a real company appearing inside its own production.

relationship_to_protagonist: Not described; the article has no plot section
relationship_to_romance: No plot summary survives
character_gist: One of CD's two friends named in the cast list, alongside Sawant.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan appears in a cameo capacity; the aspiring writer's story is the film
relationship_to_romance: Half of an accidental marriage he refuses to look at
character_gist: Aspiring writer from a UP village who is married off to the wrong bride in the confusion of a group ceremony, refuses to see her face for ten days, and leaves for Mumbai on his aunt's money with a month's supplies and a file of scripts.

character: Inspector Badlani Jr. / Raja Badlani / Sr. Badlani
relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's cameo
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: In a triple role. As the lazy, corrupt inspector given thirty days to find the missing writer or face a punishment posting, he unknowingly houses him in his own tailoring shop, having no photograph to go by.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's cameo
relationship_to_romance: The paternal authority the hero runs from
character_gist: The short-tempered father, remarried after his first wife's death, who never supports his son's ambition to write — and who comes to terms with it in an emotional reunion at the end.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's cameo
relationship_to_romance: Half of the film's marriage, unseen by her own husband
character_gist: The bride exchanged by accident in the group wedding, whose face her husband refuses to look at for ten days out of disappointment — and who, when he finally does, turns out to be beautiful.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's cameo
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: The aunt who backs the writing ambition wholeheartedly, giving him the money and supplies for a month in Mumbai — the one person in the household who does.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's cameo
relationship_to_romance: Outside the central marriage
character_gist: Figure in the village world the writer leaves behind; the article gives the role no development.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's cameo
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Editor among the Mumbai gatekeepers from whom the aspiring writer collects rejections.

relationship_to_protagonist: Wife of Bachchan's Mirza and owner of the mansion he is waiting to inherit
relationship_to_romance: The workbook's PAIR-095 — the only romance row in the last fifty films of the filmography, and a mercenary marriage to a woman seventeen years his senior
character_gist: Owner of the crumbling Fatima Mahal, seventeen years older than the husband who cannot wait for her to die. She leaves him to manage the property, sleeps through his attempt to take her fingerprints, and ends the film having eloped with an old lover and sold the mansion for one rupee.
performance_recognition: Won the Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actress

relationship_to_protagonist: The tenant Bachchan's Mirza harries for rent, and his adversary throughout
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Poor tenant with a wheat mill, a mother and three sisters, who pays less rent than anyone and still will not pay it. He kicks a toilet wall down, refuses the repair bill, and allies with the government archaeologist purely to deprive Mirza of the house.

relationship_to_protagonist: The official whose plan would take the mansion from Bachchan's Mirza altogether
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Government archaeologist who recognises the mansion's historic value and moves to seize it, evict the tenants and declare it a state heritage site — offering alternative accommodation to those he displaces.

relationship_to_protagonist: The lawyer Bachchan's Mirza hires, and the one who proposes forgery
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Local lawyer engaged to get the mansion transferred, who searches for any other heir, is handed fingerprints from the wrong hand, and resorts to forging them instead.

relationship_to_protagonist: Part of the tenant household ranged against Bachchan's Mirza
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: One of Baankey's sisters in the household whose lives Mirza sets out to make miserable in every way he can.

relationship_to_protagonist: The subject Bachchan's Lateef Zaidi selects for the game, and prosecutes in it
relationship_to_romance: His affair with his employer's wife is the crime the trial uncovers
character_gist: Business tycoon sheltering from a snowstorm who presents himself as a self-made orphan, agrees to be the defendant in a mock trial for sport, answers honestly, and is taken apart — convicted by his own candour of colluding with his boss's wife to kill him.

relationship_to_protagonist: Opposing counsel to Bachchan's prosecutor in the group's mock court
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Retired defence counsel assigned to the guest, who warns him that entering the mock court with no charge at all is the dangerous option, since it leaves the prosecutor free to charge anything — advice that is rejected.

relationship_to_protagonist: Presides over the game Bachchan's Lateef Zaidi argues
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Retired judge who sets out the defendant's rights, vouches for the ex-convict among them, and sits over the point at which a parlour game stops being one.

relationship_to_protagonist: One of the circle Bachchan's prosecutor plays the game with
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: A retired hangman among the household in the mountains — the detail that tells the audience what kind of game this group actually plays.

relationship_to_protagonist: Joins the group around Bachchan's Lateef Zaidi
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Ex-convict who served a sentence for killing the man who sexually assaulted his sister — sentenced by the retired judge now on good terms with him, and Anna's brother.

relationship_to_protagonist: Her unpreparedness is the reason Bachchan's prosecutor gets a live defendant
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: The house help, and Joe's sister, who had not prepared the famous case Lateef had set her — which is why the guest is put in the dock instead.

relationship_to_protagonist: No direct dealings with Bachchan's Lateef Zaidi
relationship_to_romance: The affair at the centre of the crime
character_gist: His employer's wife, Sameer's love interest and later partner — the relationship the prosecutor extracts from him and builds the murder charge on.

relationship_to_protagonist: The slum boy Bachchan's Vijay Borade builds a team around
relationship_to_romance: Outside romance
character_gist: Leader among the slum children recruited into the football team a retiring sports teacher assembles. The film's article carries only a one-sentence summary, so the role is described from the cast list and that sentence alone.

relationship_to_protagonist: Wife of Bachchan's Vijay Borade
relationship_to_romance: A spouse-only role with no pairing record
character_gist: The teacher's wife, in a film whose single-sentence plot summary covers only the team and the children whose lives it changes.

relationship_to_protagonist: One of the young players Bachchan's teacher takes on
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: One of the slum youngsters in the team; the article's summary gives no individual arc.

relationship_to_protagonist: One of the young players Bachchan's teacher takes on
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Another of the team assembled from the slum, played by one of the director's Sairat leads.

relationship_to_protagonist: Appears in the film he directed, opposite Bachchan
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: The film's own director in an acting role — the second instance in this filmography of a director appearing in his own Bachchan film, after Major Ravi in Kandahar.

relationship_to_protagonist: Son of Bachchan's Vijay Borade
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: The teacher's son, part of the household behind a story the article summarises in a single line.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan narrates the Hindi version of this film and does not appear in it
relationship_to_romance: The film's romantic lead
character_gist: World-renowned palmist in 1978 Italy, called the Einstein of palmistry after predicting the Emergency, a self-declared playboy who disbelieves in love — until he reads the palm of a woman whose long life he insists on against a terminal diagnosis.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: The film's romantic lead
character_gist: Clumsy, beautiful physician met on a train, who is insulted by his proposal of a casual affair and relents anyway, and whose collapse reveals an incurable tumour that his own prediction refuses to admit.

relationship_to_protagonist: Plays, in the Hindi version Bachchan narrates, the role Krishnam Raju plays in Telugu
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: The spiritual saint whose chief disciple the palmist is. The part is double-cast by language, as the narration itself is — Bachchan narrating the Hindi version and S. S. Rajamouli the Telugu.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Ambitious son of a powerful tycoon, told he is destined to inherit a commercial empire rather than succeed in politics, whose men run the palmist off the road for saying so.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: The paternal-figure objection to the romance
character_gist: Prerana's uncle and hospital dean, who warns her against the palmist, expels him as a fraud, and then tests him with the palm prints of five dead people — accepting his authenticity when he deduces all five deaths correctly.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: Family around the romance
character_gist: Senior family presence in a film whose plot runs on palmistry, prophecy and a train full of passengers sharing one death line.

relationship_to_protagonist: The pilot Bachchan's Narayan Vedant investigates and cross-examines
relationship_to_romance: Married to Samaira; no courtship is dramatised
character_gist: Accomplished pilot who parties the night before a flight, diverts into worse weather than he was told of, and lands on Runway 34 against a deadly tailwind with his eyes closed — explaining afterwards that a photographic memory let him visualise every step.

relationship_to_protagonist: The witness Bachchan's Vedant pressures into the inquiry's decisive disclosure
relationship_to_romance: Outside romance; the film has none
character_gist: Co-pilot who argued for Bengaluru as the safer diversion and was overruled, and who under pressure from the investigator reveals that the captain landed the aircraft with his eyes closed.

relationship_to_protagonist: The airline owner with an interest in what Bachchan's inquiry concludes
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Owner of Skyline Airways, the company whose aircraft and whose captain are the subject of the investigation.

relationship_to_protagonist: Opposing counsel to Bachchan's investigator
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: The captain's lawyer through the inquiry, the polygraph test and the reconstruction that closes the case.

relationship_to_protagonist: Her death is what gives Bachchan's inquiry its urgency
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: The elderly passenger who trusted the captain to land safely and then died of a heart attack on the way to hospital — the death that turns a procedural review into something graver.

relationship_to_protagonist: Wife of the pilot Bachchan's Vedant is investigating
relationship_to_romance: A spouse-only role with no pairing record
character_gist: The captain's wife, the domestic side of a film otherwise conducted in cockpits and hearing rooms.

relationship_to_protagonist: Son of Bachchan's Kanji Parikh, in the film that marks Bachchan's Gujarati debut
relationship_to_romance: Half of the film's romance, with Sneha
character_gist: Young man who, after praying at a temple, finds he can hear the thoughts of every woman — panicked at first, then using it to solve other people's relationship troubles.

relationship_to_protagonist: No direct dealings with Bachchan's Kanji Parikh described in the article
relationship_to_romance: The film's romantic lead
character_gist: Chintan's girlfriend, in a comedy whose whole premise is a man who can hear what women are actually thinking.

relationship_to_protagonist: Wife of Bachchan's Kanji Parikh
relationship_to_romance: A spouse-only role with no pairing record
character_gist: Kanji's wife and Chintan's mother, one of the women in the household whose thoughts the premise makes audible.

relationship_to_protagonist: Daughter of Bachchan's Kanji Parikh
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Chintan's sister in the Parikh household.

relationship_to_protagonist: Mother of Bachchan's Kanji Parikh
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Chintan's grandmother, the eldest of the three generations of Parikh women in the film.

relationship_to_protagonist: Recruited into the Brahmānsh by Bachchan's Raghu, who trains him and tells him who his parents were
relationship_to_romance: The film's romantic lead
character_gist: Mumbai DJ and orphan who carries the Agneyāstra within him, has visions of attacks he is not present at, and is forced to join the secret society by its guru in exchange for the truth about his father Dev and mother Amrita.

relationship_to_protagonist: Arrives at Bachchan's Ashram alongside Shiva
relationship_to_romance: The film's romantic lead
character_gist: London-based NRI visiting India for Durga Puja at her grandfather's pandal, who falls for Shiva at first sight and then travels with him through Varanasi and Himachal as the astras hunt them.

relationship_to_protagonist: The force closing on Bachchan's Ashram through the whole film
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Dev's right-hand woman, wielder of the Kavachāstra, who possesses a scientist with the Vash Mukut to extract the Brahmāstra's location, kills the artist guarding the second piece, and aims to revive the weapon and release Dev.
performance_recognition: Won the IIFA Award for Best Supporting Actress; nominated for the Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actress

relationship_to_protagonist: Fellow member of the Brahmānsh Bachchan's Raghu leads
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Artist, architect and archaeologist guarding the second piece of the Brahmāstra in Varanasi, who wields the Nandi Āstra, hands the piece to Shiva, and stays behind to fight Junoon and Zor, and is killed. His return to Hindi cinema after nineteen years.

relationship_to_protagonist: A member of the society Bachchan's Raghu leads, killed before the two meet
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Special appearance as the scientist guarding a piece of the Brahmāstra, who fights with the Vānarāstra, is possessed and interrogated by Junoon, and throws himself off a balcony rather than give up the Ashram's location.
performance_recognition: Nominated for the IIFA Award for Best Supporting Actor

relationship_to_protagonist: Fellow member of the Brahmānsh under Bachchan's Raghu
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Member of the secret society, in the Ashram where the new recruits are trained in their respective astras.

relationship_to_protagonist: A former member of the society Bachchan's Raghu leads, and the mother whose identity he discloses
relationship_to_romance: Half of the film's previous generation's love, between Dev and Amrita
character_gist: Uncredited cameo as Shiva's mother, a former Brahmānsh member who wielded the Jalāstra — the revelation Raghu trades for the boy's obedience.

relationship_to_protagonist: One of the two henchmen hunting the pieces Bachchan's society protects
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Junoon's henchman, who attacks the scientist for the first piece, stole the Nandi Āstra from Anish, and pursues the couple by truck towards Himachal.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan appears as himself, credited as Amit, in a film about the killing of film critics
relationship_to_romance: Half of the film's romance — with the reporter he later abducts
character_gist: Florist who courts an entertainment reporter and is revealed to the audience as the killer mutilating critics who write dishonest reviews. Enraged by his own girlfriend's review, he kidnaps her and is arrested as he is about to kill her.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's appearance as himself
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: IPS officer who works out that the killer targets critics who pan films, is refused cooperation by the critics themselves out of fear, and traces the pattern to Guru Dutt and Kaagaz Ke Phool.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's appearance as himself
relationship_to_romance: The film's romantic lead
character_gist: Entertainment reporter given Kaagaz Ke Phool as a birthday present on Guru Dutt's birth anniversary, asked by the police to write a bait review, and abducted by her own boyfriend for writing it badly.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's appearance as himself
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Criminal psychologist and the investigating officer's friend since college, who suggests the killer has a connection to the film industry — the insight that cracks the case.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's appearance as himself
relationship_to_romance: Family around the romance
character_gist: The reporter's mother; the cast list gives her no name of her own.

relationship_to_protagonist: Only daughter of Bachchan's Harish Bhalla, and the one who quarrels with him hardest
relationship_to_romance: Living with a partner her father disapproves of
character_gist: Lawyer who learns of her mother's death from a bar waiter, having ignored the calls in which Gayatri wanted to hear about her first case. She reaches Chandigarh first and immediately disagrees with her father over the cremation rites.

relationship_to_protagonist: Wife of Bachchan's Harish Bhalla, dead before the film's present action begins
relationship_to_romance: A long marriage recorded posthumously; no pairing row
character_gist: The mother whose death assembles a scattered family under one roof. Her last call to her daughter went unanswered, and the film is the household's reckoning with her absence.

relationship_to_protagonist: Eldest son of Bachchan's Harish, and a target of his anger
relationship_to_romance: Married to Daisy
character_gist: Eldest son, flying in from Los Angeles with his American wife, and one of the sons his father is furious with for seeming unaffected by their mother's death.

relationship_to_protagonist: Adoptive son of Bachchan's Harish Bhalla
relationship_to_romance: Named as Delna's love interest
character_gist: The family's adopted Sikh third son, who books the first flight from Dubai, and who shares the household's other quiet attachment with their foster daughter.

relationship_to_protagonist: Youngest son of Bachchan's Harish, unreachable when his mother dies
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: The son climbing Everest with his phone out of range, for whom his father has to leave a message about his mother's death to be heard later.

relationship_to_protagonist: Conducts the rites Bachchan's Harish insists upon
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: A modernistic pandit in Haridwar, the film's comic register in the middle of its funeral — and the figure standing between a father's insistence on ritual and a daughter's resistance to it.

relationship_to_protagonist: The partner Bachchan's Harish disapproves of
relationship_to_romance: Half of the daughter's relationship
character_gist: Tara's live-in boyfriend, a DJ. The cast list records that her mother liked him while her father disapproved of him for being Muslim — the film's sharpest statement of what divides the household.

relationship_to_protagonist: One of the three friends who trek with Bachchan's Amit Srivastava to Everest Base Camp
relationship_to_romance: Outside romance
character_gist: One of the three ageing friends who set out for Everest Base Camp to fulfil their dead fourth friend's last wish, battling their own bodies on the way.
performance_recognition: Nominated for the Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actor

relationship_to_protagonist: The third of the friends trekking with Bachchan's Amit
relationship_to_romance: Married to Shabina
character_gist: The third friend on the trek, and the one whose wife's presence sets the film's domestic argument against its mountain one.

relationship_to_protagonist: The fourth friend, whose last wish sends Bachchan's Amit up the mountain
relationship_to_romance: Mala is his long-lost love
character_gist: The friend who dies before the journey begins and whose wish to see Everest Base Camp the other three carry out — and whose lost love joins them on the way.

relationship_to_protagonist: Wife of one of Bachchan's fellow trekkers
relationship_to_romance: Half of the film's established marriage
character_gist: Javed's wife, whose part in the journey the National Film Awards singled out — her second film in this batch after Goodbye, where she plays the dead wife.
performance_recognition: Won the National Film Award for Best Supporting Actress at the 70th National Film Awards, the ceremony at which the film's director also won Best Direction

relationship_to_protagonist: Joins Bachchan's party along the way
relationship_to_romance: The film's unrealised romance, with the dead friend
character_gist: The woman who joins the trek and turns out to be Bhupen's long-lost love, regretting that she never fought for it — the film's romance is the one that did not happen.

relationship_to_protagonist: Accompanies Bachchan's party on the trek
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: The younger member of the expedition, among the four old friends and the woman who joins them.

relationship_to_protagonist: Wife of Bachchan's Amit Srivastava
relationship_to_romance: A spouse-only role with no pairing record
character_gist: Amit's wife, at home while her husband walks to Everest Base Camp in his eighties.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan appears as a cricket commentator; his son carries the film
relationship_to_romance: Outside romance; the film's bond is coach and player
character_gist: Unsympathetic failed test cricketer who gives a one-handed batting prodigy a second career as a bowler, inventing with her the spin style the film is named for.
performance_recognition: Nominated for the Filmfare Critics Award for Best Actor

relationship_to_protagonist: The player whose matches Bachchan's commentator would be calling
relationship_to_romance: Has a boyfriend in Jeet; the film's centre is the sport
character_gist: Batting prodigy who loses her right hand in a freak accident and is retrained as a bowler, with less than ten months to qualify for the Indian women's team.
performance_recognition: Nominated for the Filmfare Critics Award for Best Actress

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's commentator described
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: The grandmother in the household around the injured cricketer; the cast list gives her no name of her own.
performance_recognition: Nominated for the Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actress, on a spanned result cell shared with the film's two Critics nominations

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's commentator described
relationship_to_romance: The player's boyfriend
character_gist: Anina's boyfriend, present through the accident and the long retraining that follows it.

relationship_to_protagonist: Appears as himself, as Bachchan does in the same film
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Cameo as himself — a real cricketer appearing in a cricket film in which Bachchan also appears as himself, commentating.

relationship_to_protagonist: The saviour Bachchan's Maharishi Dalapathi prophesied, and his grandson
relationship_to_romance: Entangled with Dimple, and trained alongside Jassi
character_gist: In a dual role. Buried alive for being caught with his boss's girlfriend, he survives, crosses the wall to the city of the poor, learns he is the prophesied Ganapath, and throws a fixed fight in a way that ruins the men who fixed it.

relationship_to_protagonist: Trains the grandson of Bachchan's Maharishi in the cause he was prophesied for
relationship_to_romance: The film's romantic lead
character_gist: The trainer's confidante who prepares Guddu for the fights, is confined by the enemy, and is released with secret instructions to get the poor to stake their savings on the final bout.

relationship_to_protagonist: The power the prophecy of Bachchan's Maharishi is aimed against
relationship_to_romance: Dimple's boyfriend, and the reason the hero is buried alive
character_gist: Henchman of the Silver City's ruler who runs the boxing rackets, catches Guddu with his girlfriend and has them both buried alive, and loses his and his patron's money on the final fight.

relationship_to_protagonist: Son of Bachchan's Maharishi Dalapathi and father of the hero
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Combat trainer in the city of the poor, revealed on television at the film's close to be Guddu's biological father.

relationship_to_protagonist: No dealings with Bachchan's Maharishi
relationship_to_romance: The entanglement that begins the plot
character_gist: John's girlfriend, taken to a nightclub by Guddu on John's own instruction, who gets physical with him and is buried alive beside him for it.

relationship_to_protagonist: Daughter-in-law of Bachchan's Maharishi Dalapathi
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Ganapath's mother, in the family line the prophecy runs through.

relationship_to_protagonist: In his ancient life he was the warrior Bachchan's Ashwatthama fought beside among the Kauravas; in the present he is the mercenary hunting the woman Ashwatthama is sworn to protect
relationship_to_romance: Roxie is his love interest; the film's centre is the prophecy
character_gist: In a dual role: Karna, the ancient warrior allied with the Kauravas, and Bhairava, a cynical bounty hunter six thousand years later chasing enough points to buy a life inside the Complex, aided by his sentient vehicle Bujji.
performance_recognition: Nominated for the SIIMA Award for Best Actor – Telugu

relationship_to_protagonist: The mother of Kalki — the one person Bachchan's Ashwatthama was cursed to wait six thousand years to protect, and whose divine presence he senses
relationship_to_romance: Outside romance; she is a captive lab subject
character_gist: Laboratory subject of Project K, the first to survive past the 150-day threshold of an artificial pregnancy meant to yield an immortality serum. She escapes, is renamed Sumathi by a rebel, and reaches Shambhala, where the world blooms around her.
performance_recognition: Nominated for the SIIMA Award for Best Actress – Telugu

relationship_to_protagonist: The power whose entire project Bachchan's Ashwatthama exists to defeat
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Totalitarian god-king ruling the last city of Kashi from the Complex, an inverted pyramid floating above it, who abducts fertile women from the outskirts to extract a life-extending serum and make himself immortal.
performance_recognition: Won the SIIMA Award for Best Actor in a Negative Role – Telugu

relationship_to_protagonist: Her sacrifice is what buys Bachchan's Ashwatthama the time to intervene and take custody of Sumathi
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Rebel from Shambhala who renames the escaped subject Sumathi during the trek back, and who dies holding off Yaskin's Raiders long enough for the immortal warrior to reach her.
performance_recognition: Won the SIIMA Award for Best Supporting Actress – Telugu

relationship_to_protagonist: The companion Bachchan's Ashwatthama confides in, disclosing his ancient ties to Karna
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Young girl who disguised herself as a boy to escape the Raiders' abductions, and the one person the six-thousand-year-old warrior tells his own history to.

relationship_to_protagonist: Leads the sanctuary Bachchan's Ashwatthama brings Sumathi to
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Leader of Shambhala, the hidden mountain refuge of those who believe in the Kalki prophecy, and the authority receiving the prophesied mother.

relationship_to_protagonist: Commands the forces Bachchan's Ashwatthama overpowers
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Commander in the Complex's militarised apparatus, on the side hunting the escaped subject.

relationship_to_protagonist: No direct dealings with Bachchan's Ashwatthama
relationship_to_romance: The bounty hunter's love interest — the film's only romantic thread
character_gist: Bhairava's love interest in the slums below the Complex, in a film otherwise built on prophecy, captivity and pursuit.

relationship_to_protagonist: Carries the film Bachchan appears in as Prabhudas, in a special-appearance capacity
relationship_to_romance: Sets himself against his grandson's romance
character_gist: Grandfather who descends from the afterlife during the sixteen days of Shraadh, armed with magic powers, expressly to break his grandson's marriage to his childhood love — old patriarchal principle pitted against the present.

relationship_to_protagonist: No direct dealings with Bachchan's Prabhudas described in the article
relationship_to_romance: The film's romantic lead
character_gist: The grandson whose marriage to his childhood love a returning ancestor sets out to wreck. The lead of both of Bachchan's Gujarati films, having played Chintan in Fakt Mahilao Maate (FILM-250).

relationship_to_protagonist: No direct dealings with Bachchan's Prabhudas described
relationship_to_romance: The film's romantic lead
character_gist: The woman at the centre of the marriage the ghost of a grandfather is trying to prevent, in a comedy the article describes as aimed at generational patriarchy.

relationship_to_protagonist: No direct dealings with Bachchan's Prabhudas described
relationship_to_romance: Peripheral to the central romance
character_gist: Supporting figure in the household the returning ancestor disrupts.

relationship_to_protagonist: The encounter specialist whose killings Bachchan's Justice Pandey scrutinises, and whom he proves to have killed an innocent man
relationship_to_romance: Married to Thara; the film is a procedural
character_gist: Superintendent of police famed for extrajudicial killings, who shoots a drug producer and then an alleged rapist — and is shown by the human rights commission that the second man was in another city at the time. Devastated, he reopens the case.

relationship_to_protagonist: Part of the reinvestigation Bachchan's Justice Pandey forces into being
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Thief turned police informer and technical genius, whose expertise uncovers both the contract killer behind the murder and the senior officer who took a bribe to frame an innocent man for it.

relationship_to_protagonist: The figure at the end of the chain Bachchan's Justice Pandey set the police back onto
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Chairman of Nat Academy, running a coaching scam that promised guaranteed exam results, refused refunds, and used a contract killer's gang to threaten the families who complained — then partnered with the government to bury it.

relationship_to_protagonist: Her murder is the case Bachchan's Justice Pandey ultimately corrects
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: The middle-school teacher whose complaint about marijuana in her classrooms begins the film, who grows close to the policeman's family, and is raped and murdered on her new school's terrace, her body left in the water tank.

relationship_to_protagonist: The corruption Bachchan's Justice Pandey's intervention exposes
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Officer who led the original investigation and is revealed to have tipped off the contract killer and taken a bribe to frame an innocent software engineer for the murder.

relationship_to_protagonist: The innocent man Bachchan's Justice Pandey proves was killed for nothing
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Software engineer and a student's brother, named as the rapist on the strength of an alleged pornography addiction, killed in an encounter at sea — and then shown by the commission to have been in Hyderabad when the crime took place.

relationship_to_protagonist: Part of the reopened investigation Bachchan's Justice Pandey compelled
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Assistant superintendent on the original murder inquiry who then works the case again from the beginning, finding the gaps the first investigation left.

relationship_to_protagonist: Wife of the officer Bachchan's Justice Pandey investigates
relationship_to_romance: A spouse-only role with no pairing record
character_gist: Athiyan's wife, in the household the murdered teacher had grown close to.

relationship_to_protagonist: Bachchan narrates this film and does not appear in it
relationship_to_romance: Married to Shugan; the film is a battle account
character_gist: Company commander of Charlie Company, 13 Kumaon, sent to hold the freezing pass of Rezang La in 1962 without artillery support. Offered the chance to retreat, he answers that they will not fall back, and dies of his wounds — awarded the Param Vir Chakra.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: The major's radio operator, and one of only six men of the 120 to survive the day — among those who recount the battle to the commanders afterwards.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: The cheerful, spirited rifleman of the company, one of the men whose banter the film uses to cover their fear before the bombardment.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Platoon commander of the 7th platoon, one of the seasoned leaders assigned to the forward firing posts, decorated with the Vir Chakra.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Brigade commander at headquarters who knows the men will have to hold alone until relief arrives, if it arrives, and who is shaken by the scale of the sacrifice afterwards.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: Outside the romance
character_gist: Commanding officer of 13 Kumaon, who with the brigade commander does what little can be done for a company holding an exposed pass without support.

relationship_to_protagonist: No scenes with Bachchan's narration
relationship_to_romance: A spouse-only role, billed as a special appearance, with no pairing record
character_gist: The major's wife, who prays for his return while understanding what is being asked of him, and who receives the news at the film's close.
